| | 8192 | 130 | 120 | 1.08 |

Sum of the GEMM launches per prefill (ms): 512 rows 50.3 against 53.0 with the library (incl. the SiLU·mul launches), 2048 rows 196.5
against 218.6, 8192 rows 804.7 against 888.9. cuBLASLt is no longer needed for the 16-bit models on this GPU: our kernel is within
±1 % of it on the large shapes and ahead where the fusion applies. Where it trails: small grids, K / V at 512 rows (32 blocks for 82
SMs: no K split yet) and the down projection at 512 rows (7 %). The standalone kernel against the cuBLASLt probe of section 51 on the
same shapes (`bench/s53_gemm/bench_f16.cu`): 136-161 TFLOPS at 2048 rows against cuBLASLt's 144-165, 145-156 at 8192 rows (the
grouped rasterization: 117-123 without it).

### 53.4 The FP8 GEMM: what limits it

In the model (Qwen3-8B-FP8, 2048 rows, `profiles/` of this section against section 51): gate / up dual 1.98 → 1.81 ms per layer
(208 → 227 TFLOPS), down 1.03 → 0.98 ms (201 → 211), q / o 0.354 → 0.323 ms (194 → 213), k / v 0.103 → 0.092 ms (167 → 187); the
prefill GPU time 172.9 → 167.7 ms. vLLM's 14,948 tok/s at 2048 rows put its GEMMs near 260-280 TFLOPS.

Ablations of the standalone kernel (`bench/s53_gemm`, [4096 → 12288] at 2048 rows, TFLOPS):

| variant | TFLOPS |
|---|---:|
| `mma.sync` E4M3 peak (register operands, 4-32 accumulators per warp) | 462-474 |
| `ldmatrix` + `mma.sync` loop of 64 x 32 warp tiles, no copies | 445 |
| kernel, compute only (no global loads, no promotion, no stores) | 368 |
| + block-scale promotion (fresh accumulator per K block, one FMA per output) | 319 |
| + output stores | 301 |
| + global loads (the shipped form) | 224 |
| loads only (no MMAs) | 435 equivalent |
| 128 x 256 tiles, accumulator kept divided by the block's scale product: without the rescale, without the scale loads | 297 |
| the same with the per-row scale loads (4 bytes from a separate 128-byte line per row and K block) | 229 |
| the same with the rescale | 171 |

The copies of the codes overlap with the MMAs only partly at 96 KB of stages (in flight: ~64 KB per SM, which the latency of L2 under
load does not cover), and the per-row scale loads cost as much as the codes: each K block needs 256-384 scattered 4-byte loads. Tried
and not kept: TMA (`cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d`, 128-byte swizzle, full / empty mbarriers, one issuing thread; 190-200 TFLOPS: the
issue cost of `cp.async` was not the limit), mbarrier pipelines in place of `__syncthreads` (223), 16 warps of 32 x 32 (210), two
blocks per SM with 64-value stages (200), 128 x 256 tiles with per-column or per-row promotion (spills: 120-150). Blackwell's
block-scaled `mma.sync ... kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale` needs UE8M0 (power-of-two) scales per 32 values and `sm_120a`, which the f32
128-value scales of the checkpoints do not fit. The next step is a scale layout the GEMM can stream densely (a K block's scales for
consecutive rows next to each other: the activation quantization can write it, the weights need a repack at load), which the
ablation puts at ~300 TFLOPS before promotion.

### 53.5 Decode: CUDA graphs and the attention batch

| model (CUDA, 512-token prompt) | launch graphs off | on | GPU ms per step off / on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 | 622 | 645 | 1.51 / 1.46 |
| Qwen3-8B (bf16) | 51.3 | 51.6 | 19.38 / 19.27 |

The graph removes the gaps between ~300 launches on the GPU timeline (the event-timed GPU time includes them); host time per step
(wall minus GPU) was already ~0.1 ms with the recordings of phase 1. `DEC_R` = 4 on CUDA (develop's round 11 set 1 for every target)
gives the rest of the 1B decode gain (Qwen3-0.6B 1.68 ms per step on CUDA in section 51 with `DEC_R` = 1). Batched decode on CUDA
with `DEC_R` = 4 is in the serving runs of 53.6.

The 8B decode stays 1-2 % behind Vulkan (bf16 19.27 against 18.97 ms per step; the matvecs' weight streaming, section 51: 848 against
875 GB/s), not addressed in this phase.

### 53.6 Serving on CUDA (procedure of section 43, median of 2 rounds, same session)

`bench/s16_serve.sh` with 64 slots of 512-token contexts, ~250-token prompts, 128 output tokens, 1 / 4 / 16 / 64 concurrent streams;
Sharplight with `--provider cuda` / `--provider vulkan` (the adaptive step budget of section 50), vLLM 0.33.0 fresh in the same
session (`bench/results/s53/serve-*`). Aggregate output tok/s / TTFT p50 ms / mean inter-token latency ms:

| model | streams | CUDA | Vulkan | vLLM | CUDA / vLLM tok/s |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| gpt-oss-20b HF | 1 | 177 / 32 / 5.4 | 177 / 32 / 5.4 | 168 / 32 / 5.7 | 1.05 |
| | 4 | 470 / 75 / 8.1 | 472 / 75 / 8.1 | 500 / 78 / 7.5 | 0.94 |
| | 16 | 1275 / 138 / 11.5 | 1270 / 131 / 11.6 | 1417 / 178 / 9.9 | 0.90 |
| | 64 | 2256 / 317 / 24.6 | 2249 / 318 / 24.7 | 3163 / 420 / 16.9 | 0.71 |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 HF | 1 | 86 / 35 / 11.4 | 86 / 35 / 11.4 | 86 / 43 / 11.4 | 1.00 |
| | 4 | 299 / 88 / 12.9 | 300 / 88 / 12.9 | 325 / 75 / 11.8 | 0.92 |
| | 16 | 938 / 159 / 15.8 | 938 / 154 / 15.9 | 1112 / 167 / 12.9 | 0.84 |
| | 64 | 2090 / 390 / 26.2 | 2094 / 390 / 26.2 | 2697 / 398 / 20.2 | 0.77 |

* CUDA serves at Vulkan's level at every concurrency (within 0.5 %): the serving steps are decode-dominated (64 rows plus prompt
  chunks), where neither the hand-written GEMMs (from 256 rows) nor the graphs (a new recording per step size) apply; with `DEC_R` = 4
  CUDA's batched steps keep the inter-token latency of Vulkan's `DEC_R` = 1 (11.5 / 24.6 against 11.6 / 24.7 ms for gpt-oss).
* Against vLLM: single streams at or above vLLM (lower TTFT for Qwen3-8B-FP8), 0.90-0.94x at 4-16 streams, 0.71-0.77x at 64 (vLLM's
  inter-token latency at 64 streams is 30 % lower). The serving gap is the batched decode step (the multi-row GEMMs and attention of
  64 sequences), not prefill.

### 53.7 Vulkan unchanged

The shared changes are inert for SPIR-V and MSL: the `.cu` kernels are compiled only by a compiler with a CUDA C++ translator, the
lowering emits them only for the `native_gemm_*` features (reported by the CUDA provider alone), and `DEC_R` stays 1 off PTX. The
kernel inputs (source and macros, `SHARPLIGHT_DUMP_KERNELS`) of the 642 kernels the Vulkan provider compiles for Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0,
Llama-3.2-1B Q8_0, gemma-3-1b Q8_0, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-8B-FP8 and gpt-oss-20b are byte-identical between `develop` (`79fccbd1`) and this
branch, with the same Slang build, so their SPIR-V is too. The Vulkan columns of 53.1 agree with section 51 within 1-2 % except
Qwen3-0.6B at 2048 rows (77.7k against 82.2k tok/s); with identical kernels that difference is not this branch's (not investigated).

## 54. CUDA provider phase 4: dense FP8 scale layouts, 64-row FP8 tiles, the batched decode step against vLLM (2026-11-19)

Branch `cuda/provider-r4` ([cuda.md](cuda.md#kernels-written-in-cuda-c)). GPU 1 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, 82 SMs,
nothing else on it), driver 595.112.07, NVRTC 13.0.88, procedure of sections 51 / 53 (`bench/s53_providers.sh`, one process per
prompt length, prefill median of 5, decode median of 64 steps). vLLM 0.33.0 fresh in the same session. Raw output in
[`bench/results/s54/`](../bench/results/s54). This phase changes the FP8 paths only: models without block-scaled E4M3 weights run
the kernels of section 53.

### 54.1 Qwen3-8B-FP8 per provider (tok/s; prefill median of 5 / decode median)

| rows | Vulkan | CUDA phase 3 (§53) | **CUDA** | CUDA / Vulkan | vLLM DeepGEMM (§51) | vLLM CUTLASS (today) | CUDA / vLLM |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 10,817 / 87.0 | 11,348 / 87.7 | **12,688 / 87.4** | 1.17 / 1.00 | 14,546 / 87.3 | 13,946 / 86.5 | 0.87-0.91 / 1.00 |
| 2048 | 10,972 / 86.1 | 11,808 / 86.2 | **12,819 / 85.7** | 1.17 / 1.00 | 14,948 | 14,971 | 0.86 |
| 8192 | 9,282 / 77.0 | 9,791 / 78.1 | **10,494 / 77.7** | 1.13 / 1.01 | 12,316 | 12,391 / 77.2 | 0.85 |

* FP8 prefill +7-12 % over phase 3 (0.79x → 0.85-0.87x of vLLM), decode unchanged. The 1.0x target is not reached (54.3).
* vLLM selects DeepGEMM on this GPU, which rounds the block scales up to powers of two (UE8M0) and requantizes the weights; with
  `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` it takes CUTLASS's block-scaled kernel with the checkpoint's f32 scales and is just as fast (the "CUTLASS"
  column, `bench/results/s54/vllm-nodg`). The exact scales are therefore not what separates us from vLLM.

### 54.2 What changed

* **Dense scale layouts for the hand-written FP8 GEMM.** Weights are repacked at upload into 128-row groups
  (`WeightRepack.Fp8B128Grouped`, type `f8e4m3_b128g`, same bytes): [128 rows of K codes][K / 128 blocks of the 128 rows' f32
  scales], so a tile's weight scales of a K block are 512 contiguous bytes. `quantize_fp8` and the norms that write E4M3 rows add a
  dense copy of the activation scales ([K / 128][capacity] after the rows, `DENSE_XCAP`). A K block's scales are now 64 16-byte
  `cp.async` copies instead of 256 4-byte loads from separate lines. Every generated kernel reading FP8 weights decodes the grouped
  layout too (`FP8_GROUPED` in `quant_fp8.slang`, `F8_GROUPED` in `gemm_fp8.slang`), so decode and small batches keep their kernels.
* **64-row tiles** of the hand-written FP8 GEMM (four `cp.async` stages in the same 99 KB), chosen per batch by estimated block waves
  (a 128-row block costs 1.75 of a 64-row one), and the hand-written GEMM serves from 65 rows instead of 256
  (`SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_GEMM_MIN_ROWS`).
* `SHARPLIGHT_FP8_GROUPED=1|0` forces the grouped weight layout on every target or none (54.7).
* `bench/BatchBench --provider cuda` profiles the batched decode step on CUDA; `bench/s54_vllm_decode_profile.py` gives vLLM's
  per-kernel decode step (torch profiler, CUPTI kernel records: no performance counters needed).

### 54.3 The FP8 GEMM

In the model (Qwen3-8B-FP8, 2048 rows, `SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_PROFILE=1`), GPU time per launch, phase 3 → phase 4: gate / up dual 1.81 →
1.72 ms (227 → 240 TFLOPS), down 0.98 → 0.90 ms (211 → 228), q / o 0.323 → 0.306 ms (213 → 225), k / v 0.092 → 0.089 ms (187 → 192);
the prefill's GPU time 167.7 → 155.3 ms, of which the GEMMs are 122.7 ms. vLLM's prefill GEMMs run at ~280-297 TFLOPS (its own
8192-row profile: gate / up 5.91 ms = 279, down 2.85 ms = 289, qkv 1.40 ms = 294); at that speed ours would take ~98 ms, which is
the whole remaining gap at 2048 rows (vLLM's 2048-row prefill: 137 ms).

Standalone kernel (`bench/s54_gemm/bench_fp8.cu`, random data, TFLOPS at 2048 / 8192 rows):

| shape | phase 3 (per-row scales) | dense scales | ablations of the dense kernel at 2048 rows: no scale loads / no promotion / no code loads / neither |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| q / o [4096 → 4096] | 202 / 211 | 236 / 250 | 232 / 253 / 272 / 295 |
| k / v [4096 → 1024] | 163 / 194 | 214 / 232 | 213 / 232 / 243 / 259 |
| gate / up [4096 → 12288] x2 | 201 / 190 | 233 / 223 | 234 / 247 / 280 / 308 |
| down [12288 → 4096] | 199 / 212 | 241 / 258 | 238 / 259 / 287 / 311 |

The scale loads now cost nothing (the "no scale loads" column equals the kernel). What is left: the per-block promotion (~6 %) and
the copies of the codes that the MMAs do not hide (~15 %); with neither the loop runs at 295-311 TFLOPS. Tried and not kept:

| variant | TFLOPS (2048 rows, q / o, gate / up) | why not |
|---|---|---|
| promotion with one weight scale per 128-row tile (128 x 128 checkpoints) | 250 / 247 | +6 %, but needs the scales uniform over each 128-row group, which the format does not guarantee (per-channel checkpoints) and the lowering cannot see before the weights are read |
| warp specialization: a producer warp with `cp.async.mbarrier.arrive`, full / empty mbarriers, scales prefetched to registers | 230 / 217 | no `__syncthreads`, but not faster |
| 256 x 128 or 128 x 256 tiles, 16 warps of 64 x 32 | 146 / 157 | 128 registers per thread: spills |
| 64 x 128 or 128 x 64 tiles, four stages | 228 / 211 | more L2 traffic per MMA |
| A fragments double-buffered in registers, the next stage's copies issued after the B fragments | 234 / 232 | ptxas already overlaps them |
| `cp.async ... L2::256B` prefetch hints | unchanged | |

CUTLASS's block-scaled sm120 kernel reaches ~290 TFLOPS with the same exact f32 scales (54.1), so there is headroom; reaching it
needs a different main loop (likely TMA with warp-specialized ping-pong of two consumer groups, so that one group's promotion
overlaps the other's MMAs), which did not fit this phase.

### 54.4 The batched decode step (64 sequences)

`BatchBench --slots 64 --ctx 512 --depth 256 --sizes 64 --modes greedy` (GPU ms per step; CUDA / Vulkan: minimum launch times from
the per-launch profile, x 36 layers), vLLM: `s54_vllm_decode_profile.py` (64 sequences of 256-token prompts, the annotated
`execute_context_0(0)_generation_64` ranges of the warm run; `bench/results/s54/batch`):

| per step | CUDA | Vulkan | vLLM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPU time per step | 17.53 (wall 17.92) | 16.90 (wall 17.34) | 14.08 without LM head and sampling (+1.55 LM head) |
| gate / up (dual, SiLU·mul) | 5.35 | 5.22 | 4.73 |
| down | 2.68 (+ split-K reduce) | 2.50 | 2.45 |
| q, k, v, o | 2.74 (4 launches) | 2.58 | 2.22 (qkv fused + o) |
| attention (+ combine) | 3.89 + 0.41 | 3.98 + 0.44 | 3.65 |
| split-K reduce, activation quantization, norms, rope, cache | ~1.9 | ~1.4 | 3.36 split-K reduce (overlapped through PDL) + 0.6 |
| LM head [4096 → 151936] | 1.59 | 1.53 | 1.55 |

* vLLM's weight GEMMs stream the weights at ~766 GB/s (the read limit of this GPU is ~780 GB/s); ours at 680-700 GB/s, plus 3 % more
  bytes (one scale per row instead of per 128 x 128 block). A `cp.async` skinny GEMM prototype (64-row tiles, four stages, split-K
  1-12) stayed at 600-700 GB/s: the generated kernels are not limited by how many copies are in flight.
* The CUDA step is ~0.6 ms slower than Vulkan's (the same Slang kernels; the grouped layout costs the decode GEMMs ~2 %).

**Mixed steps** (64 decode rows plus one prompt chunk, `BatchBench --mixed`, GPU ms) improved with the 64-row FP8 tiles and the lower
row threshold:

| prompt rows | 0 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 96 | 128 | 256 | 512 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CUDA before (generated below 256 rows) | 17.53 | 20.99 | 21.90 | 23.64 | 30.98 | 32.21 | 40.63 | 63.73 |
| **CUDA** | 17.52 | 19.64 | 19.73 | 20.08 | 25.59 | 25.63 | 33.75 | 65.32 |
| Vulkan | 16.90 | | | | | 33.04 | 43.39 | 74.46 |

### 54.5 Serving (procedure of section 43, median of 2 rounds, same session)

Aggregate output tok/s / TTFT p50 ms / mean inter-token latency ms, Qwen3-8B-FP8 (`bench/results/s54/serve-*`):

| streams | CUDA | vLLM | CUDA / vLLM |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 86 / 35 / 11.4 | 86 / 38 / 11.4 | 1.00 |
| 4 | 299 / 88 / 12.9 | 327 / 77 / 11.7 | 0.92 |
| 16 | 938 / 151 / 15.9 | 1119 / 167 / 12.9 | 0.84 |
| 64 | 2093 / 389 / 26.2 | 2692 / 464 / 19.9 | 0.78 |

Unchanged from section 53 (0.77x at 64 streams): of the 396 steps of a 64-stream round, 364 are pure decode steps of up to 64 rows
and 23 carry 1025-2048 rows (several prompts at once), so the mid-size steps that got faster hardly occur. The time splits into the
decode steps (~364 x 17.5 ms = 6.4 s) and the prompt batches (~48,000 prompt rows at the prefill rate of 54.1, ~3.5 s); vLLM spends
~5.7 s and ~3.2 s. Closing the gap needs both: the decode step at vLLM's 15.6 ms (54.4) and the FP8 GEMM at CUTLASS's speed (54.3).
gpt-oss-20b is unchanged by this phase (MXFP4, no FP8 path).

### 54.6 Not done in this phase

* FP8 prefill at 1.0x of vLLM (0.85-0.87x reached), serving at 64 streams at 0.9x (0.78x): see 54.3-54.5 for what is measured.
* The decode-step items beyond the measurement: a split-KV decode attention with `cp.async` (ours is within 7 % of vLLM's
  FlashAttention split-KV), a fused q / k / v GEMM (~0.5 ms per step), graph capture of mixed steps (host time is ~0.4 ms per
  decode step on both providers).
* The FlashAttention-2-style prefill kernel in CUDA C++ (`fe` is 24 % of an 8192-token FP8 prefill, 105 TFLOPS), split-K for the
  native f16 GEMM's small grids, the dual GEMM writing the f16 copy, the 8B decode matvec gap, and the MXFP4 expert GEMM for
  gpt-oss.

### 54.7 Vulkan unchanged

The grouped layout is selected only where the hand-written FP8 GEMM runs (CUDA); on Vulkan the generated kernels keep the split
rows. The kernel library changes are inert for them: of the 225 kernels the Vulkan provider compiles for Qwen3-8B-FP8 and
Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 (`SHARPLIGHT_DUMP_KERNELS`), 204 preprocess to identical text against `develop` (`48a7af26`) and the 21 fp8 GEMM /
quantization kernels compile to byte-identical SPIR-V (`slangc -g0 -target spirv`, both kernel libraries). The Vulkan column of
54.1 matches section 53 within 1-3 %. With `SHARPLIGHT_FP8_GROUPED=1` Vulkan's generated fp8 GEMM reads the coalesced weight scales:
prefill +1-4 % (2048 rows 11,060 → 11,365 tok/s), decode -0.3 to -2 % (the matvecs' scale loads leave the row's DRAM page), so it
stays off there.

## 55. Hybrid prefix caching on CUDA and Metal, recurrent state kept inside a step (2026-11-19)

Branch `engine/copy-state-rows`. Two changes for models with recurrent state (gated delta nets, Mamba, RWKV, short convolutions):

- `CopyStateRows` on CUDA (`cuMemcpyDtoDAsync` on the segment's stream) and Metal (copies in shared storage): recurrent-state
  snapshots for prefix caching and copy-on-write forks of `n` > 1 samples now work there too (before, such models ran without prefix
  caching on CUDA and Metal). Metal is compiled and its test project builds; it has not run on Apple hardware.
- In-step snapshots ([kv-cache.md](kv-cache.md), `Graph.RecurrentSnapshots`): the recurrent kernels store the state at a block boundary
  inside a prompt chunk into a spare state row while they walk the run (the chunked delta rule starts such a run with a chunk of k mod 64
  rows so that a chunk ends at k). A snapshot inside a chunk no longer cuts the chunk (one more pass), and no copy follows. 48.6 ended
  with the conversations as the one load where the cache made TTFT worse than without it: each turn's prompt-end snapshot cost a pass.

Qwen3.5-0.8B (HF bf16), `bench/prefix_bench.py` as in 48.3: 16 multi-turn conversations of 6 turns resending their history, and a
1500-token shared system prompt at 16 chats; `sharplight serve --slots 64 --ctx 8192 --kv-tokens 73728`, GPU 0 (RTX PRO 4500, shared
machine, other agents' CPU load ~10-14). Settings: in-step snapshots (default), copied after the step with the chunk cut
(`SHARPLIGHT_STEP_SNAPSHOTS=0`, the behaviour of 48.6) and without prefix caching. TTFT p50 / p99 ms, output tok/s, hit rate. Raw
results in [`bench/results/s55/`](../bench/results/s55).

| provider | workload | round | in-step | copied, chunk cut | no prefix cache | in-step / copied TTFT p50 |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| Vulkan | multiturn 16 | 1 | 74 / 139, 3271, 50.2 % | 109 / 208, 3044, 50.9 % | 104 / 204, 1694, 0.0 % | 0.68x |
| Vulkan | multiturn 16 | 2 | 64 / 144, 3400, 53.2 % | 96 / 168, 3207, 47.1 % | 75 / 136, 2929, 0.0 % | 0.67x |
| Vulkan | shared 16 | 1 | 55 / 96, 3761, 95.1 % | 79 / 106, 3665, 95.1 % | 105 / 569, 1982, 0.0 % | 0.70x |
| Vulkan | shared 16 | 2 | 51 / 81, 3793, 95.1 % | 75 / 97, 3662, 95.1 % | 105 / 537, 2005, 0.0 % | 0.68x |
| CUDA | multiturn 16 | 1 | 67 / 145, 3271, 51.9 % | 102 / 189, 3098, 49.0 % | 81 / 167, 2797, 0.0 % | 0.66x |
| CUDA | multiturn 16 | 2 | 72 / 130, 3212, 52.1 % | 99 / 213, 3191, 48.6 % | 54 / 154, 2908, 0.0 % | 0.73x |
| CUDA | shared 16 | 1 | 51 / 98, 3771, 95.1 % | 75 / 117, 3643, 95.1 % | 73 / 565, 1980, 0.0 % | 0.68x |
| CUDA | shared 16 | 2 | 50 / 83, 3443, 95.1 % | 75 / 108, 3680, 95.1 % | 106 / 537, 2000, 0.0 % | 0.66x |

- In-step snapshots take 0.66-0.73x of the TTFT p50 of copied snapshots on both providers and both loads, at the same hit rates and
  equal or higher throughput. On the conversations the cache-on TTFT is now at or below the cache-off TTFT in 3 of 4 rows (48.6:
  1.2-1.3x above it); CUDA round 2 (72 against 54 ms) is the exception, and single rows vary by ~20 % between runs (48.6).
- The CUDA column "copied, chunk cut" is what hybrid prefix caching on CUDA does with copies alone; before this branch CUDA had no
  hybrid prefix caching (the "no prefix cache" column).

Tests: `StepStateSnapshotTests` (Families, new: a state kept inside a step at 48 or 112 rows and restored in another slot continues like
the whole prompt; 9 tiny models covering every recurrent op on CPU and GPU, Qwen3.5-0.8B with f32 and bf16 state on the chunked delta
rule): 20 / 20 on Vulkan and 20 / 20 on CUDA. `PrefixCacheParityTests` 16 / 16 on Vulkan and on CUDA (`SHARPLIGHT_TEST_PROVIDER=cuda`,
now selectable), `PrefixCacheTests.RecurrentModel_InsideStepSnapshots_CostNoPass` (Serving).

Reproduce:

## 56. LLM round 12: a hand-written grouped MXFP4 expert GEMM on CUDA, gpt-oss-20b against vLLM's Marlin MoE (2026-11-19)

Branch `perf/llm-r12` ([cuda.md](cuda.md#kernels-written-in-cuda-c)). GPU 0 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, 82 SMs, shared
with other agents' short GPU tests: every run below started only when `nvidia-smi` showed no other compute process), driver
595.112.07, NVRTC 13.0.88, vLLM 0.33.0 fresh in the same session (its MXFP4 MoE backend on this GPU is Marlin, W4A16: bf16
activations, `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm`), identical checkpoint (openai/gpt-oss-20b) on both sides. "Before" is this branch with
`native_gemm_moe` disabled (the generated kernels of `develop`, which this round leaves unchanged). Raw output in
[`bench/results/s56/`](../bench/results/s56).

### 56.1 Prefill and decode (procedure of §53: `bench/s53_providers.sh`, prefill median of 5 / decode median, tok/s)

| rows | Vulkan | CUDA before | **CUDA** | vLLM | CUDA / vLLM before → after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 10,254 / 167.4 | 9,208 / 183.5 | **12,221 / 183.1** | 11,436 / 172.8 | 0.81 → **1.07** (decode 1.06) |
| 2048 | 12,024 / 166.4 | 12,057 / 181.1 | **14,223 / 181.4** | 16,379 | 0.74 → **0.87** |
| 8192 | 9,857 / 159.4 | 9,916 / 173.4 | **11,297 / 174.1** | 15,812 / 166.0 | 0.63 → **0.71** |

vLLM's decode columns are its `tg128` at depth 16 and 8192 (`bench/s42_gap.sh`). The 8192-token prefill runs as four 2048-row passes on
our side; the gap that is left there is attention (56.3).

### 56.2 Where a 2048-token prefill goes (GPU ms, `SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_PROFILE=1`; vLLM: `s54_vllm_decode_profile.py --prefill 2048`)

| | CUDA before | **CUDA** | vLLM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPU time of the pass | 164.1 | **139.8** | 118.4 (kernel sum 110.8) |
| expert gate / up (dual, clamped SwiGLU and bias rows in the store) | 70.0 (gemm_cm2 + half tiles) | **54.3** | 81.5 (Marlin, both products) + 4.1 SwiGLU |
| expert down (bias, router weight in the store) | 38.2 | **28.8** | |
| gather into sorted f16 rows, slot sum | 4.3 + 2.9 | 4.8 + 2.7 | 1.3 (moe_sum) + 0.2 routing |
| prefill attention (`fa` / FlashInfer) | 16.3 | 16.4 | **4.4** |
| q / k / v / o projections | 9.6 + 3.2 + 8.6 | 9.6 + 3.2 + 8.5 | 8.5 (qkv) + 7.9 (o) |

Per layer the grouped gate / up product (8192 routed rows x 2880 → 2 x 2880) takes 2.26 ms (120 TFLOPS; before 2.92 ms, 93 TFLOPS) and
the down product 1.20 ms (113 TFLOPS; before 1.59 ms, 85), against Marlin's 3.40 ms for both (120 TFLOPS) plus its separate SwiGLU.
The expert part of the pass is now at vLLM's level (91 against 87 ms); the remaining 21 ms are attention (12 ms), the projections
(4.5 ms) and norms / rope / small kernels.

### 56.3 The kernel and what limited it

`gemm_moe_native.cu` (selected through `native_gemm_moe`, CUDA compute capability 8.0+, MXFP4 experts in the 16-row groups of
`WeightRepack.Mxfp4Split`, K a multiple of 64; the generated kernels stay the fallback): one block per 128-row routing tile and 256 (dual)
or 192 weight rows, a four-stage `cp.async` ring of 64-value K steps holding the sorted f16 activation rows and the raw codes and E8M0
scales (25 KB per stage instead of 48 KB for f16 weights), eight warps of 128 x 32 that decode the codes of the B fragment they
multiply right before `mma.sync.m16n8k16`, and the expert group's epilogue in the store (CUDA C++ generated from the same nodes as the
Slang epilogue, `MoeEpilogueWriter`). Development steps in the standalone harness (`bench/s56_moe/bench_moe.cu`: 32 experts, gpt-oss
shapes, uniform routing, L2 evicted before each launch; gate / up ms at 128 / 2048 tokens):

| step | 128 tokens | 2048 tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| first form: 2 x 4 warps of 64 x 64, scale factors converted per decode | 1.05 | 2.56 |
| one warp row (each decoded fragment serves 8 row fragments), E8M0 factor table per block, dead rows not copied | 0.94 | 2.38 |
| `L2::256B` prefetch on the code copies (a stage takes only 32 bytes of each weight row) | 0.80 | 2.44 |
| decode of the next 32-value block software-pipelined against the MMAs | 0.83 | 2.42 |
| a partial tile's empty fragments skipped by a warp-uniform branch (predicated-off MMAs still take the tensor pipe's time) | **0.46** | **2.29** |
| the next block's decode issued between the current block's MMAs | 0.46 | **2.26** |

The last one is the shipped form; the down product (single, 192 weight rows per tile) takes 1.14 ms at 2048 tokens. Ablations at 2048
tokens: without the in-loop copies 1.86 ms, without the decode arithmetic 2.16 ms, with constant scales 2.25 ms; the copies' waits
are ~2 % of a K step and the barrier ~0 (clock64 instrumentation), so what is left is the shared-memory traffic and power-limited
clocks the f16 GEMM also has (our f16 GEMM on the dense equivalent [8192 x 2880 → 5760]: 1.78 ms, 153 TFLOPS). The f16 `mma.sync`
peak of this GPU measures 235 TFLOPS.

Tried and not kept:

| variant | result (gate / up, 2048 tokens) |
|---|---|
| 16 warps (2 x 8, 64 x 32 warp tiles, 128 registers) | 2.78 ms |
| 2 x 4 warps with the final loop | 2.63 ms (faster only at 128 tokens: 0.60 against 0.46 before the skip) |
| three stages | 2.31 ms |
| 128-row weight tiles for the down product | 1.26 against 1.14 ms |
| E2M1 decode through a `prmt` byte table (one multiply by the scale instead of two, bit-identical including every E8M0 value) | 8 % fewer cycles per decode in a micro benchmark; not integrated (decode is ~4 % of the kernel) |
| Vulkan: the same skip of empty fragments in gemm_cm2's MoE tiles (subgroup-uniform branch around the cooperative-matrix loads and MMAs) | gate / up 2.44 → 3.69 ms per layer on the NVIDIA Vulkan driver: reverted |

### 56.4 Serving steps (BatchBench `--provider cuda`, GPU ms, minimum of 10, `SHARPLIGHT_DISABLE_FEATURES=native_gemm_moe` for "before")

| step | before | **after** |
|---|---:|---:|
| 64 decode rows | 19.19 | 19.20 (expert-grouped skinny GEMM, unchanged) |
| 64 + 32 prompt rows (12 per expert) | 24.12 | 24.08 (skinny GEMM, unchanged) |
| 64 + 107 | 33.69 | **25.75** |
| 64 + 192 | 40.16 | **29.61** |
| 64 + 448 | 58.15 | **45.64** |
| 2048 prompt rows | 172.22 | **146.96** |
| 64 slots of 512: 64 + 250 / 8 prompts of 250 | 43.81 / 154.30 | **32.44 / 132.42** |

The native GEMM serves from 12 routed rows per expert on average (`SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_MOE_MIN_ROWS`), where the skinny expert GEMM hands
over; 4, 8 and 12 measured the same. At 64 sequences the decode step (19.8 ms with LM head and sampling in the profile) is not
changed: its expert GEMMs (11.8 ms) already stream the MXFP4 weights at ~800 GB/s, Marlin takes 10.6 ms for the same step, and vLLM's
whole step is 14.6 ms without its LM head (projections 1.8 against our 3.2 ms, attention 1.2 against 1.6 ms).

### 56.5 Serving against vLLM (procedure of §43: `bench/s16_serve.sh`, 64 slots of 512 tokens, median of 2 rounds, same session)

Aggregate output tok/s / TTFT p50 ms / mean inter-token latency ms. The rounds ran with `QUIET_GPU=1` (new: a round starts only
while no other process computes on the GPU and is repeated, up to three tries, when one appeared during it; none was needed here):

| streams | CUDA before | **CUDA** | vLLM | CUDA / vLLM before → after |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 16 | 1065 / 144 / 13.8 | **1119 / 114 / 13.3** | 1413 / 178 / 10.0 | 0.75 → **0.79** |
| 64 | 2194 / 319 / 25.4 | **2351 / 270 / 24.0** | 3152 / 421 / 16.8 | 0.70 → **0.75** |

* **`serve --provider` was ignored** (only `--disable-features` reached the hosting options), so `sharplight serve --provider cuda`
  ran on the default provider, Vulkan: the "CUDA" serving rows of §53.6 and §54.5 are Vulkan's (which is why they matched it within
  0.5 %). `serve` now maps `--provider` and `--device` to the device id (`cuda:0`). The figures above are the first CUDA serving runs;
  `SHARPLIGHT_DISABLE_FEATURES` in the environment does not reach `serve` either, so "before" passes `--disable-features native_gemm_moe`.
* The gain at 64 streams (+7 %) comes from the prompt steps (23 of a round's 396 steps carry 1025-2048 rows, 56.4); TTFT p50 is below
  vLLM's at both concurrencies. 364 of the 396 steps are decode steps of up to 64 rows, unchanged by this round, and they are the
  rest of the gap: mean inter-token latency 24.0 against 16.8 ms (56.4: our 64-sequence step 19.8 ms against vLLM's ~16.2 ms).
* Earlier attempts of this measurement were discarded: other agents' tests ran on the GPU during them, and one long run measured
  a leftover server on the same port. `s16_serve.sh` now refuses to start while the port is in use or another server runs, stops
  its server's process group on any exit (trap), and marks a round `.contaminated` after three disturbed tries.

* Greedy output of gpt-oss-20b on CUDA (200 tokens; prompts of 666 and ~260 tokens, both on the native GEMM): byte-identical with

  expert with partial tiles and a partial column tile, K = 576; dual halves with bias and SiLU·mul, down with bias and router weight):

  (71 with expert epilogues, written by the refactored generators) are byte-identical to `develop` (`7b107d4e`), so its SPIR-V is too.

## 57. LLM round 13: FP8 GEMM under the power limit, tensor copies, warp-specialized persistent main loop; decode step at 16-64 sequences (2026-11-20)

Branch `perf/llm-r13` (base `develop` at `8ca10b24`). GPU 0 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, 82 SMs, 200 W board
limit), driver 595.112.07, NVRTC 13.0.88, vLLM 0.33.0 (`VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`: CUTLASS's block-scaled kernel with the checkpoint's
f32 scales, as in 54.1). Another agent's idle `sharplight serve` held 16 GB of the GPU throughout (no kernels running; vLLM ran with
`--gpu-util 0.45`). "Before" is this branch with `SHARPLIGHT_FP8_TMA=0` (the phase-4 kernel), run in the same session. Raw output
in [`bench/results/s57/`](../bench/results/s57).

### 57.1 Qwen3-8B-FP8 per provider (tok/s; prefill median of 5 / decode median, procedure of section 51)

| rows | Vulkan | CUDA before | **CUDA** | CUDA / before | CUDA / Vulkan | vLLM | CUDA / vLLM (before) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 10,229 / 86.1 | 12,323 / 87.0 | **13,627 / 87.0** | 1.11 | 1.33 / 1.01 | 13,806 / 86.7 | **0.99** (0.89) / 1.00 |
| 2048 | 10,238 / 85.2 | 11,811 / 85.5 | **13,150 / 85.6** | 1.11 | 1.28 / 1.01 | 14,957 | **0.88** (0.79) |
| 8192 | 8,651 / 76.0 | 9,690 / 77.6 | **10,582 / 77.7** | 1.09 | 1.22 / 1.02 | 12,296 / 77.3 | **0.86** (0.79) / 1.00 |

* FP8 prefill +9-11 % on CUDA: 0.99x of vLLM at 512 rows, 0.86-0.88x at 2048-8192 (before: 0.79-0.89x). Decode unchanged.
* The phase-4 kernel measured 0.85-0.87x of vLLM on GPU 1 (54.1) and 0.79-0.89x here: the same build is 3-8 % slower on this board
  at 2048-8192 rows, vLLM is not. Ratios below compare runs of the same session.
* GEMM time of a 2048-row prefill (`SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_PROFILE=1`, two 1024-row passes, `profiles/`): 136.6 → 118.3 ms (gate / up
  dual 873 → 765 µs minimum per launch, down 522 → 446, q / o 168 → 144, k / v 44 → 37).

### 57.2 What limits the FP8 GEMM: the 200 W limit, not the copies

The ablations of 53.4 / 54.3 timed short bursts. Sampled during a model's prefill the board sits at its 200 W limit at 2.1 GHz
(8192-token prefill: 195-201 W, 2.09-2.25 GHz), and so does a standalone GEMM run back to back for 1.5 s. Two measurements that do
not depend on the clock make the kernels comparable (`bench/s57_gemm`, `-DF8N_CYCLES`: FLOPs per SM cycle from `clock64()`;
`SUSTAIN`: steady-state time and the board's NVML energy per FLOP):

| kernel, [4096 → 4096] at 8192 rows | burst TFLOPS | sustained TFLOPS | SM clock (sustained) | FLOPs per SM cycle (of 2048) | pJ / FLOP |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| phase 4 (`gemm_fp8_native.cu`) | 228 | 220 | 2.18 GHz | 1337 (65 %) | 0.93 |
| ablation: no code copies (54.3's "no code loads") | 335 | 341 | 2.71 GHz | 1509 (74 %) | |
| ablation: no code copies, no block barrier | | | | 1778 (87 %) | |
| ablation: no code copies, no barrier, no promotion | | | | 1959 (96 %) | |
| **warp-specialized with tensor copies (`gemm_fp8_tma.cu`)** | 246 | 236 | 2.14 GHz | 1565 (76 %) | 0.86 |
| vLLM / CUTLASS block-scaled (`vllm_gemm.py`) | 302 | 289 | 1.90 GHz | ~1850 (~90 %) | ~0.69 |

* The "no code loads" ablation was fast mostly because the tensor cores multiplied stale shared memory: with less switching the
  board held 2.7 GHz instead of 2.2. Per cycle it gained 9 points, not the 50 % its TFLOPS suggested; the copies are not hidden
  badly (with L2-resident data, `HOT`, the tensor-copy kernel runs at the same cycles).
* What costs cycles is the block barrier per K block (13 points: all eight warps drain the tensor pipe together at the promotion
  and the next block's first `ldmatrix`) and the promotion itself (9 points: 64 FMULs for the per-output scale products and 64
  FFMAs per thread and K block; CUTLASS's 128 x 128 scales need one product per row).
* CUTLASS runs at ~90 % of the MMA peak per cycle and so at a lower clock under the same 200 W: 0.69 against our 0.86-0.93 pJ per
  FLOP. Under the limit a kernel is as fast as it is efficient in energy, and more work per cycle is the lever that pays.

### 57.3 Warp-specialized persistent FP8 GEMM with tensor copies (kept, default from compute capability 9.0)

`gemm_fp8_tma.cu` (`DeviceFeatures.TensorCopies`, the 128-row tiles; 64-row tiles keep `gemm_fp8_native.cu`):

* **Persistent**: one block per SM walks its share of the 128 x 128 tiles in the grouped order, so the copies of a tile's first K
  blocks overlap the previous tile's last blocks and its stores. On its own (per-thread copies with the copy pointers advanced
  per K block instead of recomputed) +2-4 %; recomputing them per block made it 6 % slower: the main loop is sensitive to every
  integer instruction.
* **Tensor copies** (`cp.async.bulk.tensor`, 128-byte swizzle by the copy engine) of the activation and weight tiles, bulk copies of
  the K block's 128 + 128 scales into a two-slot ring, all issued by one lane of a copy warp; full barriers (transaction counts)
  and empty barriers (one arrival per computing warp) replace `__syncthreads`. The ring is 3 x 32 KB of codes, 2 x 1 KB of scales
  and 64 bytes of barriers (100,416 of the 101,376 bytes a block may take).
* **Tensor maps in the kernel parameters**: the lowering states them in a header line (`// sharplight-tensormaps:` pointer argument,
  dimensions, strides, box); the CUDA provider encodes them with `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` when it records a launch and appends them
  (64-byte aligned) after the scalars, so CUDA graphs and precompiled packages carry nothing new.
* Results are bit-identical to `gemm_fp8_native.cu` (same per-output order of MMAs and fused multiply-adds; dual form with the w and
  w2 halves of the B tile instead of interleaved 8-row groups). 128-row tiles now cost 1.3 of a 64-row block in the tile choice
  (was 1.75): 8192-row prefill 9,971 tok/s at 1.75, 10,515 at 1.3, 10,486 at 1.0.

Per shape (`bench/s57_gemm/run.sh`, random codes, burst = best of 17 after an L2 flush / sustained = 1.5 s back to back, TFLOPS;
vLLM: `vllm_gemm.py`, its gate / up is one [4096 → 24576] GEMM without the SiLU·mul):

| shape | rows | phase 4 | **tensor copies** | vLLM / CUTLASS | ours / vLLM (sustained) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| q / o [4096 → 4096] | 2048 | 235 / 212 | **256 / 224** | 305 / 280 | 0.80 |
| | 8192 | 228 / 220 | **246 / 236** | 302 / 289 | 0.82 |
| k / v [4096 → 1024] | 2048 | 205 / 195 | **215 / 206** | 240 / 252 | 0.82 |
| | 8192 | 218 / 207 | **235 / 219** | 284 / 276 | 0.79 |
| gate / up [4096 → 12288] x2, dual | 2048 | 245 / 218 | **269 / 237** | 291 / 282 | 0.84 |
| | 8192 | 221 / 218 | **240 / 237** | 287 / 284 | 0.83 |
| down [12288 → 4096] | 2048 | 237 / 215 | **258 / 230** | 281 / 275 | 0.84 |
| | 8192 | 231 / 227 | **248 / 243** | 294 / 293 | 0.83 |

Two compiler effects decided whether this reached a model (first in-model runs: no gain, then a launch failure):

* **Spills under NVRTC**: with `__launch_bounds__(288, 1)` the provider's NVRTC 13.0 produced PTX that ptxas allocates at its 168-
  register cap with 76-92 bytes of spills, 5-9 of them inside the MMA loop (nvcc 13.2 on the same source: none); the kernel was then
  no faster than phase 4 in the model. `__launch_bounds__(288)` without the block minimum: 168 registers, no spills.
  `bench/s57_gemm/nvrtc_check.sh` runs a kernel through the provider's NVRTC and counts local-memory accesses in the MMA loop.
* **Local memory and "out of memory" at launch**: copies with a `shared::cluster` destination make ptxas check at run time that the
  address is the block's own, with a fallback call (`__cuda_syscall_cp_async_bulk_*`) that needs an 8-byte stack; the first launch
  then failed with `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` when the KV cache had filled the GPU (BatchBench, 64 slots). `shared::cta`
  destinations (PTX 8.6, chosen from CUDA 12.8 by `__CUDACC_VER_*`) and an explicit `cvta.to.global` for the bulk sources remove the
  calls and the stack.

Tried and not kept on the way (all measured in cycles as well as time): `kk`-outer promotion with all 16 fragment accumulators
(same cycles, 242 registers); software-pipelined promotion of fragment i - 1 after fragment i's MMAs (ptxas reorders it back);
TMA issued by a thread of a computing warp with a block barrier (69 %) or blocking on the empty barrier (65 %, dual 48 %); weight
and activation scales read from global memory in the computing warps (66 %: their latency lands before the first promotion);
64-row tiles in the TMA kernel (65 %); a warp-vote fast path for one weight scale per warp (one product per row, exact when the
scales agree; +3.7 points without the vote, but at the 168-register cap the two promotion paths spill); a phase offset between the
two warps of a scheduler (no effect); tile orders of 4-64 token tiles per group (±2 %); packed `fma.rn.f32x2` (split into scalar
FFMAs on sm_120).

### 57.4 Decode step at 16-64 sequences

`BatchBench --slots 64 --ctx 512 --depth 256 --modes greedy --reps 12` (GPU ms per step, median / wall, minimum):

| step | CUDA | Vulkan | vLLM (54.4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 sequence | 11.41 / 11.50, 11.35 | 11.27 / 11.34, 11.19 | |
| 16 sequences | 13.46 / 13.82, 13.39 | 13.62 / 14.08, 13.54 | |
| 64 sequences | 17.93 / 18.08, 17.83 | 17.25 / 17.63, 17.14 | 14.08 + 1.55 LM head |

Per layer at 64 sequences (CUDA profile, mean µs): gate / up 155 (670 GB/s of weights), decode attention 119 + combine 13 (64 MB of
K / V at 540 GB/s), down 79, q and o 33 each (524 GB/s), k and v 12 each (357 GB/s), five split-K reductions 20, norms 16. Measured
and not changed:

| candidate | result |
|---|---|
| fused split-K combine for 4 x 128 head groups (`SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_FUSED_WIDTH=512`, new switch) | 64 sequences -0.6 % (CUDA) / -0.2 % (Vulkan), 1 and 16 sequences ±0.4 %; section 36 measured -1 % at 4096 tokens: not worth a default |
| decode attention target workgroups 1024-4096, minimum keys 64-128, 1-4 rows per batch (`SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_CFG`) | 16 sequences within ±0.3 %; 64 sequences -0.4 % to +1.5 % (slowest: 4096 workgroups, 2 rows) |
| `__launch_bounds__` on every Slang kernel's CUDA form | -0.8 / +0.5 / -0.7 % at 1 / 16 / 64 sequences: noise |
| two workgroups per SM for the CUDA forms of `gemm_fp8.slang` (`__launch_bounds__(256, 2)`, 128 registers) | 16 sequences +0.2 %, 64 sequences +10 % (spills) |
| the split row layout instead of the 128-row groups on CUDA (`SHARPLIGHT_FP8_GROUPED=0`) | 64 sequences 17.87 against 17.91 ms: the grouped layout costs decode nothing |
| the TMA kernel at decode sizes | does not apply (64 rows run the generated split-K GEMMs) |

* CUDA is 0.7 ms per step behind Vulkan at 64 sequences with the same Slang kernels: q / o 28.3 against 26.4 µs, down 74.6 against
  70.5, gate / up 148.5 against 145.0 (minimum per launch), the split-K reductions 0.72 against 0.60 ms. The decode forms of
  `gemm_fp8.slang` (64-row tiles, split-K) take 146 registers without spills under NVRTC (the 128-row forms take 255 with 84-byte
  spills, but the hand-written GEMM serves those sizes), so one 256-thread workgroup fits per SM.
* Against vLLM (15.6 ms) the step is 2.3 ms longer: the weight GEMMs stream at 520-670 GB/s against vLLM's ~766 (1.3 ms), five
  split-K reductions per layer (0.7 ms; vLLM overlaps its reduction with programmatic dependent launch), attention (0.4 ms). A fused
  q / k / v GEMM needs a multi-output GEMM (separate outputs; the dual form combines its two products) and saves an estimated
  0.5-0.8 ms per step with its reductions; it did not fit this round.

### 57.5 Vulkan unchanged

The changes are CUDA-only: the new kernel is compiled only by the CUDA provider's translator and selected only with
`tensor_copies` (reported by CUDA from compute capability 9.0); the tile-cost change and the new switches are behind the native FP8
GEMM (CUDA) or default-off. No `.slang` file changed. The kernel inputs (source and macros, `SHARPLIGHT_DUMP_KERNELS`) of the 207
kernels the Vulkan provider compiles for Qwen3-8B-FP8 and Qwen3-0.6B are byte-identical to `develop` (`8ca10b24`), so their SPIR-V
is too; the Vulkan column of 57.1 is the same build.

limit, shared with other agents' tests: every timed run started only once `nvidia-smi` showed no other compute process), driver

machine and checkpoints). The serving rows below ran fresh, in this session. Raw output in [`bench/results/s58/`](../bench/results/s58).

* gpt-oss-20b at 2048 tokens (`SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_PROFILE=1`): GPU time of the pass 140.3 → 123.5 ms (vLLM 118.4). Attention
  16.4 → 3.5 ms (FlashInfer 4.4): `fa` took 250 µs on a sliding-window layer and ~1.1 ms on a full one. `attn_prefill_native` takes
  51 µs and ~240 µs. The 8192-token prefill runs as four 2048-row passes against a growing cache, so attention was 30 % of it.
* Qwen3-8B-FP8 (plain causal, which `fe` served): attention at 2048 tokens 12.7 → 9.6 ms.
* This session's FP8 figures are 3-6 % above §57's for both "before" and "after" (board state). The ratios compare runs of one session.

### 58.2 The kernel

`attn_prefill_native.cu` (`native_attention`, CUDA compute capability 8.0+, [cuda.md](cuda.md#kernels-written-in-cuda-c)) works in the
FlashAttention-2 form:

* Each warp keeps its 16 query rows (Q · SCALE in f16), the scores, the online-softmax statistics and the output accumulators in
  registers for the whole key loop. The probabilities become the A operands of P · V without shared memory.
* The block shares 64-key K / V tiles in a two-stage `cp.async` ring (swizzled 16-byte chunks; `ldmatrix` / `ldmatrix.trans`).
* Masks apply only on tiles crossing a row's limits, and warp-uniform skips drop tiles a warp cannot see. Blocks run longest first.
* Head sizes 64 and 128. Sliding windows, chunks, soft caps, sinks, GQA, multi-sequence runs (also paged) and mixed steps.

Standalone harness (`bench/s58_attn/bench_attn.cu`: one sequence, random Q / K / V, L2 flushed before each launch, minimum of 20;
FLOPs of the visible scores only, Q·Kᵀ and P·V):

| shape | form | ms | TFLOPS |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| gpt-oss (64 / 8 heads, D 64), 2048 queries, causal + sinks | 4 warps (first form) | 0.268 | 128 |
| | 8 warps | 0.297 | 116 |
| | 4 warps, 32 rows per warp (`FN_MR=2`) | 0.250 | 138 |
| | **4 warps, no compare per probability (sentinel maximum)** | **0.252** | **136** |
| same, window 128 | 4 warps | 0.102 | 41 (66 MB of f32 Q / O: ~650 GB/s) |
| same, 2048 queries after 6144 cached keys | 4 warps | 1.554 | 155 |
| Qwen3-8B (32 / 8 heads, D 128), 2048 queries, causal | 4 warps | 0.391 | 88 |
| | **8 warps** | **0.266** | **129** |
| | 4 warps, `FN_MR=2` | 0.449 | 77 (spills) |
| same, after 6144 cached keys | 8 warps | 1.708 | 141 |

Kept: 4 warps at head size 64 (three 32 KB blocks per SM), 8 at 128 (one 64 KB block per SM). Against an f32 reference over the
f16-rounded Q · SCALE the outputs differ by at most 1.9e-4 (values in ±1); every edge case of the harness agrees, including partial
tiles, windows after cached keys and 5-query chunks.

### 58.3 Programmatic dependent launches

From compute capability 9.0 the translator starts every kernel with `griddepcontrol.wait; griddepcontrol.launch_dependents;`, and
the segment launches it with `cuLaunchKernelEx` and programmatic stream serialization (`dependent_launches`,
[cuda.md](cuda.md#kernels-written-in-cuda-c)). Decode steps (`BatchBench --slots 64 --ctx 512 --depth 256 --modes greedy --reps 20`, GPU ms per
step, minimum; runs alternated twice, `pdl-modes.txt`):

| launches as dependents | Qwen3-8B-FP8 1 / 16 / 64 sequences | gpt-oss-20b 1 / 16 / 64 sequences |
|---|---|---|
| none (`dependent_launches` disabled) | 11.36 / 13.51 / 17.93 | 5.38 / 11.88 / 17.99 |
| every kernel | 11.32 / 13.71 / 18.28 (-0.3 / +1.5 / +1.9 %) | 5.30 / 11.74 / 17.82 (-1.5 / -1.2 / -0.9 %) |
| after a one-wave kernel | 11.34 / 13.38 / 18.10 (-0.2 / -1.0 / +0.9 %) | 5.32 / 11.89 / 17.98 (-1.1 / +0.1 / 0 %) |
| **one-wave kernel after a one-wave kernel (kept)** | **11.33 / 13.45 / 17.90** (-0.2 / -0.4 / -0.2 %) | **5.34 / 11.90 / 18.00** (-0.7 / +0.2 / +0.1 %) |

(Mean of the two runs' minima.) With every kernel launched early, gpt-oss gains ~1 % but Qwen3-8B-FP8 loses up to 2 % at 16-64
sequences. A dependent's blocks are resident, waiting, while the previous kernel still runs. They take SM slots its later waves
need, or they are placed before that kernel releases the SMs. The kept rule, with one-wave kernels from the driver's occupancy
query, is neutral to slightly positive. Graph-replayed launches leave almost no gaps to remove: ~0.2 µs per launch at 679 launches
per step.

### 58.5 Decode step

All of this round at once (BatchBench as in 58.3, GPU ms per step, mean of two runs' minima; before: both features disabled and
`SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_CFG=1024,128,64`; `decode-steps-final.txt`):

| model | before 1 / 16 / 64 sequences | **after** | vLLM at 64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b | 5.38 / 11.89 / 17.99 | **5.35 / 11.91 / 17.81** | ~16.2 (§56.4) |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 11.35 / 13.45 / 17.90 | **11.33 / 13.45 / 17.46** | 15.6 (§57.4) |

What was measured and not changed:

* At 64 sequences the step is kernel-bound, not launch-bound. Programmatic dependent launches gain ≤ 1 %, so the gaps between the
  679 graph-replayed launches are ~0.2 µs.
* Per layer at 64 sequences (gpt-oss, profile): q 37.9, k 10.9, v 10.9, o 42.8 µs (f16 split-K gemm_cm2, 600-680 GB/s; k / v ~320 GB/s).
  Five split-K reductions take 21 µs and the f16 copy for o 4.3 µs, against vLLM's ~75 µs for qkv + o.
* A fused q / k / v GEMM over the concatenated weight rows was not built. Each weight is its own device buffer with a single model
  parameter as its source (`BufferDecl.Weight`), so one GEMM over all three needs either buffers holding several parameters (every
  provider's uploader and the `.slm` layout) or a GEMM with several weight and output pointers. Estimated gain: ~0.6-0.8 ms per step
  with one reduction instead of three.
* Decode attention:
  * The fused split-K combine for gpt-oss's 8 x 64 head groups (`SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_FUSED_WIDTH=512`) measured 17.90 → 17.97 ms
    at 64 sequences and 11.90 → 11.92 at 16, so it was not made the default.
  * Changed: on PTX the split count now aims for 512 workgroups instead of 1024 (`DEC_TARGET_WG`; Vulkan keeps 1024). A 64-sequence
    step then runs one key range per row (64 rows x 8 KV-head groups) and skips the combine launch. GPU ms per step, mean of two
    runs (`decode-target-workgroups*.txt`):

| step | 1024 | **512** |
|---|---:|---:|
| gpt-oss-20b, 64 sequences, depth 256 | 18.15 | **17.95** (-1.1 %) |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8, 64 sequences, depth 256 | 18.04 | **17.60** (-2.4 %) |
| 16 sequences, depth 256 (both models) | | ±0.2 % |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8, 16 sequences, depth 3500 | 23.54 | **23.15** (-1.7 %) |
| gpt-oss-20b, 16 sequences, depth 3500 | 14.13 | 14.23 (+0.7 %) |
| 1 and 4 sequences, depth 3500 | | ±0.5 % |

### 58.6 Correctness and tests

* The native kernel sums in another order and rounds the probabilities to f16, as `fa` and `fe` do (they differ from each other
  the same way):
  * Qwen3-8B-FP8, 1852-token prompt, last-token logits (|logit| ≤ 24): max |Δ| 0.58 against `fe`, 0.44 against `fa`. `fa` against
    `fe` is 0.41.
  * gpt-oss-20b, 1784-token prompt: max |Δ| 0.05. Short prompt: 0.004, same top-3.
* Greedy text:
  * Qwen3-8B-FP8, 100 tokens after the default and a ~370-token prompt: byte-identical.
  * After the 1852-token prompt (200 tokens): diverges after ~230 characters (`fa` against `fe`: after 53).
  * gpt-oss-20b diverges early: a few tokens into the outputs of the 5-token and ~370-token prompts, and ~100 characters after
    the 1784-token one. Its logits are close: max |Δ| 0.004 on the short prompt, and top-3 tokens and values agree to 0.002.
    The flips are near-ties under different f16 rounding, the same kind of difference as between `fa` and `fe` on Qwen3.
* New `CudaCodeTests.NativeAttentionMatchesTheCpu` (head sizes 64 / 128, window 100, sinks, chunks of 150 / 70 / 5 queries against the
  cache): within 5e-3 of the CPU and of the generated kernel. `PagedAttentionTests` on CUDA covers the paged multi-sequence form.
* Vulkan: the kernel inputs (source and macros, `SHARPLIGHT_DUMP_KERNELS`) of the 337 kernels Vulkan compiles for gpt-oss-20b,
  Qwen3-8B-FP8 and Qwen3-0.6B (`--batch 1024`) are byte-identical to `develop` (`a494e881`). The changes are CUDA-only: the new kernel is
  selected only where the target compiles CUDA C++, and the dependent launches live in the CUDA translator and segment. The dump
  predates the decode attention's 512-workgroup target, which applies only to PTX (SPIR-V and MSL keep `DEC_TARGET_WG` 1024).

### 58.8 Long contexts against vLLM (16K-128K tokens)

`bench/s58_long.sh` (new): our side `--bench N --ctx N+256` (prefill median of 5; its decode is one stream at depth N) and
BatchBench (`--batch 2048`, deep slots prefilled in 2048-row chunks) for 4 streams; vLLM `bench/s58_long_vllm.py` (offline API,
its default chunked prefill, prefix caching off, `--gpu-util 0.92`, median of 2). Same session, every run waited for a GPU without
other compute processes, the vLLM runs held the verify lock. Qwen3-8B-FP8 runs with YaRN (factor 4 over its 32,768 positions:
a copy of the checkpoint whose `config.json` sets `rope_scaling`, read by both engines); gpt-oss-20b has 131,072 positions
(YaRN in its config). KV caches are 16-bit on both sides (ours f16, vLLM's `auto` = bf16); FP8 KV was not compared, since the
CUDA provider has no FP8 cache format (q8_0 / q4_0 only). The longest point exceeds the checkpoints' limit by its 256 decode
positions on our side; vLLM needed `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1` for the same, and its decode at depth 131,072 hit a
device-side assert (positions past 131,072), so its 128K decode ran at depth 130,560. Raw output in
[`bench/results/s58/long/`](../bench/results/s58/long).

Prefill (tok/s) and TTFT of one prompt (s; = the prefill time):

| model | tokens | **CUDA** | vLLM | CUDA / vLLM | TTFT CUDA / vLLM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| | 32,768 | 11,420 | 12,327 | 0.93 | 2.87 / 2.66 |
| | 65,536 | 8,715 | 9,440 | 0.92 | 7.52 / 6.94 |
| | 131,072 | 5,894 | 6,435 | 0.92 | 22.2 / 20.4 |

| | 32,768 | 6,965 | 7,152 | 0.97 | 4.70 / 4.58 |
| | 65,536 | 4,559 | 4,553 | 1.00 | 14.4 / 14.4 |
| | 131,072 | 2,445 | 2,639 | 0.93 | 53.6 / 49.7 |

Decode at depth (tok/s per stream; 4 streams: aggregate):

| model | depth | 1 stream CUDA / vLLM | 4 streams CUDA / vLLM |
|---|---:|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b | 32,768 | 156.7 / 150.7 (1.04) | 305.8 / 310.8 (0.98) |
| | ~128K | 98.7 / 107.3 (0.92) | **does not fit** (needs 36.9 GiB) / 174.9; 2 streams fit: 129.4 (15.46 ms per step) |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 (YaRN) | 32,768 | 58.2 / 57.8 (1.01) | 110.9 / 107.1 (1.04) |
| | ~128K | 28.5 / 29.6 (0.96) | does not fit on either (4 x 19.3 GB of KV) |

Where a long prefill goes (`SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_PROFILE=1`, `bench/profile_categories.py`, whole prompt in 2048-row passes):

| model, tokens | total | attention | MoE / dense GEMMs | rest | attention TFLOPS (Q·Kᵀ + P·V of the visible keys) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| gpt-oss-20b, 32,768 | 2.87 s | 0.81 s (28 %) | 1.47 s MoE + 0.39 s dense | 0.19 s | 131 |
| gpt-oss-20b, 131,072 | 22.2 s | 13.8 s (62 %) | 5.99 s MoE + 1.60 s dense | 0.79 s | 122 |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8, 32,768 | 4.58 s | 2.43 s (53 %) | 1.84 s | 0.31 s | 130 |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8, 131,072 | 53.3 s | 43.5 s (82 %) | 8.70 s | 1.10 s | 117 |

* The attention kernel scales: 131 → 122 TFLOPS (gpt-oss) and 130 → 117 (Qwen3) from 32K to 128K, all in the FlashAttention-2
  class. The prefill ratio to vLLM is flat for gpt-oss (0.92-0.93 from 16K to 128K; at 8192 it was 0.72 before this round).
  Assuming vLLM's GEMMs and the rest cost what ours do, its attention takes ~12.0 s at 128K for gpt-oss (ours 13.8) and ~39.9 s
  for Qwen3 (ours 43.5): 9-15 % ahead at the longest prompts.
* No index overflow past 65K or in the KV offsets (64-bit element offsets throughout the kernel). The harness agrees with the
  f32 reference for 1024 queries after 70,000 cached keys (max error 4.2e-4) and after 129,000 with a 128 window and sinks
  (1.7e-4). Every length ran without errors on both models, and there is no chunk-size cliff: the 2048-row passes cost what their
  attention predicts.
* **Found: sliding-window layers keep full-length KV caches.** gpt-oss's 12 window layers (128 keys) hold as many cache rows as
  its full layers, so four 128K streams need 36.9 GiB and do not fit. vLLM's hybrid allocator stores only the window for those
  layers and fits them (175 tok/s). Window-sized caches would halve gpt-oss's KV memory: more concurrent long sequences, and more
  slots in serving.
* Decode at 128K is 0.92x of vLLM on gpt-oss: the decode attention takes ~4.8 of the 10.0 ms step. It reads 3.2 GB of K / V per
  step (12 full layers), so ~670 GB/s against ~800 at the read limit.

### 58.9 Gap to vLLM and plan (state after this round)

| benchmark | CUDA / vLLM | where the time goes (ours against vLLM) |
|---|---:|---|
| gpt-oss-20b prefill 2048 | 0.97 | GPU 123.5 against 118.4 ms per pass: experts 79.8 against 85.6 and attention 3.5 against 4.4 are ahead; q / k / v / o 20.9 against 16.4 (q / k / v carry biases, and a matmul with an epilogue never takes the native f16 GEMM: `gemm_cm2` 382 µs for q); expert gather + slot sum 7.5 against 1.5; norms / rope / adds ~9 |
| gpt-oss-20b prefill 8192 / 16K-128K | 0.92 / 0.92-0.93 | the same per pass, plus attention 9-15 % behind FlashInfer at 128K (122 against ~141 TFLOPS) |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 prefill 2048 / 8192 | 1.00 / 0.95 | FP8 GEMM main loop 76 % of the MMA peak per cycle against CUTLASS's ~90 % (§57.2); attention at 8192 |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 prefill 16K-128K | 0.93-1.00 | attention ~9 % behind at 128K (117 TFLOPS) |
| gpt-oss-20b decode step, 64 sequences | ~0.91 (17.81 against ~16.2 ms) | expert GEMMs 11.7 against Marlin's 10.6; projections ~3.1 against 1.8 (three q / k / v GEMMs, five split-K reductions per layer); attention ~1.3 against 1.2 |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 decode step, 64 sequences | ~0.89 (17.46 against 15.6 ms) | weight GEMMs at 520-670 against ~766 GB/s (~1.3 ms); split-K reductions ~0.7 ms; CUDA forms of `gemm_fp8.slang` 0.7 ms behind their SPIR-V forms |
| gpt-oss-20b serving 16 / 64 streams | 0.82 / 0.75 | decode steps (above) plus prompt rows in mixed steps (~60 µs per row) and ~0.4 ms host time per step (wall against GPU) |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 serving 16 / 64 streams | 0.87 / 0.87 | its decode step (above); TTFT p50 ahead of vLLM (116 / 283 against 168 / 400 ms) |
| gpt-oss-20b decode at 32K / 128K (1 stream) | 1.04 / 0.92 | decode attention at long depth (~670 GB/s) |
| gpt-oss-20b, 4 streams at 128K | does not fit | full-length caches for the window layers |

Ranked levers (estimated saving; ordered by what they move on the headline numbers):

1. **Decode-step GEMMs (serving at 16 / 64 streams).** A multi-output q / k / v GEMM plus split-K reductions in the GEMM's last
   workgroup: gpt-oss ~0.6 + ~0.35 ms per step, Qwen3 ~0.5 + ~0.7 ms. The q / k / v GEMM needs weight buffers that hold several
   parameters (uploader and `.slm` layout in every provider) or a GEMM with several weight pointers.
2. **MXFP4 skinny expert GEMM at Marlin's level** (gpt-oss 64-sequence step 11.7 → 10.6 ms, ~1.1 ms), and the **FP8 decode GEMMs
   at the read limit** (Qwen3 ~1.3 ms; their CUDA forms are 0.7 ms behind Vulkan's). With 1-2, gpt-oss's step reaches ~15.8 ms
   (1.03x of vLLM) and Qwen3's ~15.0 ms (1.04x).
3. **Host time and mixed steps in serving**: asynchronous step preparation (~0.4 ms per step) and the prompt rows of mixed steps.
   Serving at 64 streams is 0.75x while the decode step is 0.91x, so this is the larger part of the serving gap. It needs a serving
   profile to size (TTFT is already ahead of vLLM's at both concurrencies).
4. **gpt-oss prefill GEMMs and MoE glue**: the bias epilogue in `gemm_f16_native.cu`, so q / k / v leave `gemm_cm2` (~2-3 ms per
   2048-row pass), and the expert gather / slot sum fused into routing and the down GEMM's store (~5 ms per pass). Together
   ~6 % → ~1.03x at 2048, ~0.98x at 8192+.
5. **FP8 GEMM main loop** at CUTLASS's cycles (§57's open item): ~+7 % Qwen3 prefill → ~1.07x at 2048.
6. **Attention at long prompts**: Q pre-scaled by log2(e), separate K and V waits, three stages at head size 64, 128-row tiles
   with 8 warps at head size 64 (~10-15 % of attention, ~2 s of gpt-oss's 128K prefill and ~4 s of Qwen3's → ≥1.0x at 128K).
   Also the decode attention at depth (~0.7 ms per step at 128K → 1.0x).
7. **Window-sized KV caches for sliding-window layers** (memory, not speed): four 128K gpt-oss streams, and serving with more slots.

for n in 512 2048 8192; do $CLI ~/models/hf/gpt-oss-20b --provider cuda --bench $n --ctx $((n + 256)); done   # before: SHARPLIGHT_DISABLE_FEATURES=native_attention,dependent_launches

SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_ATTN=2 SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_PROFILE=1 $CLI ~/models/hf/Qwen3-8B-FP8 --provider cuda --bench 2048 --ctx 2304   # fe for plain causal
bench/BatchBench/bin/Release/net11.0/BatchBench ~/models/hf/gpt-oss-20b --provider cuda --slots 64 --ctx 512 --depth 256 --sizes 1,16,64 --modes greedy --reps 20
QUIET_GPU=1 ROUNDS=2 SLOTS=64 OUT_DIR=bench/results/s58/serve-cuda bench/s16_serve.sh sharplight gpt-oss-20b-hf ~/models/hf/gpt-oss-20b "16 64" --provider cuda   # before: --disable-features native_attention,dependent_launches

VLLM_VENV=<venv with vLLM 0.33.0> bench/s58_long.sh bench/results/s58/long qwen3-8b-fp8-yarn ~/models/hf/Qwen3-8B-FP8-yarn both
