## 74. Feed round 1: the verified feed's GGUF K-quant models against llama.cpp, attention for head sizes 256 and 512 (2026-11-21)

Branch `perf/feed-r1` (base `develop` at `060d579c`, §73 merged; `develop` at `ff3b70b1` (§71, perf/offload-r5's fusions) merged before
the first measurement). GPU 0 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell 32 GB, 200 W cap, no resizable BAR), shared with three other
agents and a model-feed upload: every run held the verify lock, both engines ran in the same hold for each provider, Sharplight first.
llama.cpp b11177 (`-ngl 99 -fa 1`, CUDA 13 and Vulkan builds). Every round before this one tuned gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4) and Qwen3-8B-FP8
against vLLM; the models customers run from the verified feed (`catalog/verified-models.json`) are mostly GGUF K-quants fully on the
GPU, and this round measures where three of them stand and fixes the largest gap. Raw output in
[`bench/results/s74/`](../bench/results/s74).

Models (the feed's recommended variants): **Gemma 4 31B-it Q4_K_M** (unsloth, 60 layers: 50 sliding-window layers with head size 256
and a 1024-key window, 10 global layers with head size 512, 4 KV heads and k = v; Q4_K with Q6_K v / down), **Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M**
(hybrid: 48 gated-delta-rule layers and 16 attention layers with head size 256, 24 query / 4 KV heads), **Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M** (dense,
head size 128, 40K positions, so no 128K point).

Procedure (`bench/s74_feed.sh <out> <name> <gguf> <cuda|vulkan>`): prefill at 512 / 2K / 8K / 32K (Sharplight `--bench N`, best of 5
after a warm-up; llama-bench `-p N -n 0 -r 3`, its mean); decode of one stream (the `--bench 512` decode, best of 64 steps, against
tg128); decode at depth 32K / 128K (BatchBench, one sequence in a paged pool sized for it, tokens fed back, minimum GPU ms of 20
steps, against llama-bench `-p 0 -n 64 -d D`); batched decode at 16 / 64 sequences at depth 256 (BatchBench `--feedback`, sequences x
1000 / minimum GPU ms per step, against llama-batched-bench `-npp 256 -ntg 64`, S_TG). These models are dense, so their decode work
does not depend on the token ids (fixed and fed-back ids measure the same step); BatchBench feeds the chosen tokens back anyway.
llama.cpp's Vulkan backend compiles pipelines for new shapes while llama-batched-bench times them, which made its first-pass batched
numbers of phase 1 meaningless (Qwen3-8B 1 stream at 76 tok/s against 136 in tg128); the final runs pass the sequence counts twice and
take the second pass.

Gemma 4 31B on Vulkan was not measured in phase 1 (its run was stopped once the CUDA gap was clear); the generated paths had the same
fallbacks there (74.3). Gemma's 32K prefill and 128K decode are missing on our side: they do not fit (below).

* Prefill: best of 5 (Sharplight) against llama-bench's mean of 3; decode: best tok/s of 64 steps (one stream) and 1000 / minimum GPU ms
  of 20 steps (BatchBench) against llama-bench / llama-batched-bench (S_TG, second pass). Medians are within 1-2 % of the best values
  (raw files list both).
* Phase 1's llama.cpp CUDA runs of the 27B at tg128 (28.2 ± 6.4) and at 128K (22.6) were disturbed by another process; the final hold
  measured 43.5 and 29.8, so the 27B's "before" ratios for these two points are not comparable (the before / after change on our side
  is +1 %).
* Gemma 4 31B at 32K does not fit on the session path (`--bench 32768`: 44.8 GiB): the single-sequence session keeps full-length caches
  for the 50 sliding-window layers (0.8 MB per token); the paged multi-sequence decoder (serving, BatchBench) holds window-sized caches
  (`window_kv`, §60), and llama.cpp a window-sized cache too. This is the main gap left for Gemma 4 (74.6).

### 74.2 What changed

* **Hand-written prefill attention for head sizes 256 and 512** (`attn_prefill_native.cu`, CUDA, `native_attention`): the key tile is
  now a macro (`FN_BC`: 64 up to head size 128, 32 up to 256, 16 above), so a warp's 128 output registers and the stages fit at head
  size 256 (255 registers, a 4-byte spill, three 48 KiB stages). Above 256 two warps share each 16-row group (`FN_DS` = 2): each holds
  the query fragments of half the key dimensions and the accumulators of half the value dimensions, the two partial score tiles are
  exchanged through 8 KiB of shared memory behind a named barrier per pair and summed in the same order in both warps, so both run
  the same softmax. Harness (`bench/s58_attn`, 4096 causal queries, RTX PRO 4500): head size 128 142.5 TFLOPS, 256 142.8 TFLOPS
  (8 warps; 4 warps 114.2), 256 with a 1024 window 121.8, 512 111.9 (two stages; three do not fit).
* **Register-softmax `fe` for wide heads** (Vulkan, and CUDA without the hand-written kernel): 32-key tiles and 64-query blocks up to
  head size 256, and above 256 the same split of the head dimensions between subgroup pairs (`FE_DS`, 16-key tiles, 32-query blocks,
  4 KiB exchange) inside Vulkan's 48 KiB. `SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_FE_WIDE=0` keeps wide heads off it.
* **Wide heads on the flash path**: `fa`, the generated flash kernel, takes padded head sizes up to 256; above that, prefill rows
  used the per-(head, query) scalar kernel. Now the flash path serves them where the hand-written kernel or `fe` with split heads
  does (`WideFlashAttention`).
* **Causal `fe` with sliding windows**: the block's key loop starts at its first query's window and the mask drops keys before each
  row's window (`SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_FE_WINDOW=0` keeps windows on `fa`).
* **Split-K decode attention with fewer heads per workgroup** where the merged states of 8 heads x 512 values exceed the shared
  memory (Vulkan's 48 KiB): previously the decode rows of such layers fell back to the scalar kernel (Gemma 4 31B decode on Vulkan
  31.5 → 37.5 tok/s).
* **Two key rows per lane group and batch** in the Vulkan / Metal split-K decode at head sizes of 256 and more (a whole subgroup per
  key row kept only two 16-byte loads in flight per lane): Qwen3.8 27B at 128K 39.43 → 37.72 ms per step (four rows 37.54), Gemma 4
  31B at 32K 34.9 → 34.5-34.6, batched steps unchanged (16 / 64 sequences within 0.5 %). On PTX two rows cost 2 %, so CUDA keeps one.
* **Parallel branches in captured CUDA graphs**: the CUDA recording takes the Vulkan recorder's launch order and hazard batches
  (`HazardTracker.Order`), and the capture runs the launches of a batch side by side on three side streams forked and joined by events
  (`CudaConcurrentLanes`); launches of multi-launch batches are not programmatic dependents. Same build, same hold, two runs each
  (`experiments/cuda_concurrent_graphs.txt`, GPU ms per step, on / off): Qwen3-8B 1 / 16 / 32 / 64 sequences 6.83 / 11.38 / 19.4 /
  23.03 against 7.01 / 11.6 / 20.2 / 24.68; Qwen3.8 27B 21.93 / 42.98 / 73.6 / 93.15 against 22.29 / 43.9 / 73.3 / 94.55; Gemma 4 31B
  1 / 16 sequences 26.53 / 49.49 against 26.86 / 50.79. Greedy text byte-identical. `SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_CONCURRENT=0` switches it off.
* Bench: `bench/s74_feed.sh` (both engines in one call, per provider), BatchBench prefills only the slots its batch sizes reach (one
  sequence at 128K in a paged pool sized for it).

### 74.3 Where the gaps were (phase 1)

* **Gemma 4 31B prefill, 0.32-0.79x of llama.cpp on CUDA** (pp8192 496 against 1570 tok/s): its 10 global layers have head size 512,
  which `fa` (padded head sizes up to 256) does not take, so their prefill rows ran the per-(head, query) scalar kernel: 66 ms per
  layer at 2048 tokens, 36 % of the pass (`profiles/prof_gemma_cuda_2048.txt`). Its 50 sliding-window layers (head size 256) ran `fa`
  at 1.84 ms per layer on Vulkan against 0.45 ms for the hand-written kernel at head size 256 on CUDA. On Vulkan the global layers'
  decode rows also fell back to the scalar kernel (143 µs per layer and step): the split-K decode kernel's merged states of 8 heads x
  512 values need 64 KiB, Vulkan offers 48.
* **Qwen3.8 27B prefill at 32K, 0.84 / 0.87x** (CUDA / Vulkan), at par or ahead below: its 16 attention layers (head size 256) ran the
  generated `fa` / `fe` paths at ~23 TFLOPS; the hand-written kernel covered head sizes 64 and 128 only.
* **Qwen3-8B batched decode on CUDA, 0.97 / 0.92x at 16 / 64 sequences** (Vulkan 1.7-2.1x of llama.cpp's Vulkan backend): the K-quant
  matmuls at 17-64 rows run `gemm_cm2` on dequantized tiles, and the CUDA step ran every launch on one stream, where the Vulkan
  recording lets independent dispatches between two barriers overlap (Vulkan's step at 32 sequences 15.5 against 19.8 ms on CUDA with
  the same kernels; profiled, kernel by kernel, 18.5 against 20.7 ms).
* Not gaps: K-quant prefill GEMMs (1.04-1.16x everywhere at 512-8K), single-stream decode (0.98-1.12x), decode at 32K (1.0-1.06x).
  The K-quant decode matvec (mmvq, int8 dot products on q8_1 activations) reads Qwen3-8B's 4.7 GB in 7.0 ms per token, ~670 GB/s
  of the card's 896, where llama.cpp's is 6.99 ms.

### 74.3.1 Against vLLM (equivalent 4-bit checkpoints)

vLLM 0.33.0 (`vllm-r12`) cannot load these GGUFs: its GGUF loader needs the `gguf` package, which the venv lacks, and it maps neither
`qwen35` nor `gemma4`. The comparison therefore uses the closest vLLM-native 4-bit checkpoints of the same models: **Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ**
(`4da05a8e`, AWQ int4 g128, Marlin kernels) and **RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4** (`71dface3`, compressed-tensors W4A16 g128). They are not
the same weights or bit layout as Q4_K_M (Q4_K is 4.5 bits per weight with 6-bit sub-block scales and mins, plus Q6_K down / v
projections), so these are engine-to-engine figures on comparable 4-bit models, not like-for-like kernels. vLLM ran in the hold right
after the final Sharplight / llama.cpp runs (`vllm_single.py --depth 8192`, `s58_long_vllm.py` at 32K and for 1 / 16 / 64 streams at
depth 256: prefill median of 5 with `max_tokens=1`, decode (t(129) − t(1)) / 128 over generated tokens).

| Qwen3-8B (tok/s) | Sharplight Q4_K_M, CUDA | vLLM AWQ | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 512 / 2K / 8K / 32K | 7274 / 7264 / 6583 / 4738 | 8407 / 8471 / 7525 / 5206 | 0.87 / 0.86 / 0.87 / 0.91 |
| decode, 1 stream (depth 16-512) | 144.4 | 137.7 | 1.05 |
| decode at 32K | 79.1 | 75.5 | 1.05 |
| decode, 16 / 64 sequences at depth 256 | 1404 / 2785 | 1909 / 4243 | 0.74 / 0.66 |

| Qwen3.8 27B (tok/s) | Sharplight Q4_K_M, CUDA | vLLM INT4 (W4A16) | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 512 / 2K / 8K / 32K | 1910 / 1958 / 1910 / 1774 | 2511 / 2542 / 2450 / 2186 | 0.76 / 0.77 / 0.78 / 0.81 |
| decode, 1 stream | 45.7 | 47.4 | 0.96 |
| decode at 32K / 128K | 39.2 / 27.9 | 44.0 / 38.1 | 0.89 / 0.73 |
| decode, 16 / 64 sequences at depth 256 | 371 / 687 | 601 / 880 | 0.62 / 0.78 |

The 27B's W4A16 checkpoint keeps its linear layers at ~4.1 bits per weight, where Q4_K_M has 4.5 (Q4_K) and 6.6 (Q6_K for the QKV,
down and output projections), so part of the decode gap is bytes read per token; at 128K most of it is the decode attention at head
size 256 (our split-K `decode` reads the cache at ~620 GB/s).

Against vLLM the K-quant prefill GEMM (f16 tensor cores on dequantized Q4_K tiles, ~0.86x) and above all the batched decode GEMMs at
16-64 rows (0.66-0.74x: Marlin's int4 GEMM reads the weights once per step at those batch sizes, our `gemm_cm2` does not reach the read
rate, 74.6 lever 1) are the gaps for Qwen3-8B, whose single-stream and 32K decode are ahead (1.05x); the 27B trails vLLM everywhere
(0.62-0.96x).
### 74.4 Correctness

* Greedy text (`--chat --temp 0 -n 64`, a 25-token prompt and a 1,600-token one) of the round's start (`ff3b70b1`) against this branch,
  both providers: Qwen3-8B byte-identical on both. Qwen3.8 27B: the short prompt's text on CUDA and on Vulkan swap places (the base
  gave text A on CUDA and B on Vulkan, the branch B on CUDA and A on Vulkan), the long prompt's Vulkan text leaves the base's after ~40
  tokens. Gemma 4 31B: the long prompt leaves the base after ~30 tokens on CUDA (and, with the two decode rows per batch, on Vulkan the
  same way: both providers now give the same text); the short prompt changes at
  its second token (" is composed" → " reaches") on both providers, because its global layers no longer run the f32 per-(head, query)
  kernel. That token is a near tie: " reaches" 24.17 against " is" 24.01 on every build and provider (`--logits`), and llama.cpp
  itself picks " is" on CUDA and " reaches" on Vulkan; the branch now gives llama.cpp Vulkan's text on both providers.
* Concurrent graph branches: greedy text byte-identical with and without (`SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_CONCURRENT=0`) on all three models, and
  on gpt-oss-20b (HF MXFP4, f16 projections with biases) on both providers after `develop` (`bae54776`, the f16 bias epilogue fix) was
  merged; the three feed models' greedy text is unchanged by that merge (all numbers of this section were taken before it; the fix
  touches f16 / bf16 weights with bias epilogues, which these Q4_K_M models do not have).
* Tests: Sharplight.Cuda.Tests 43 (1 skipped, the cuBLASLt probe), new `NativeAttentionMatchesTheCpu` cases at head sizes 256 and 512,
  with a window and sinks, against the CPU and the generated kernels; Vulkan.Tests classes MatMul, Mmq, QuantFormat, SkinnyGemm,
  RowInvariance, FullAttention, SparseAttention, CompressedKv, PagedAttention and Stateful (new `CachedAttentionLongPrefill` cases at 256
  and 512 with grouped heads) on Vulkan and on CUDA (`SHARPLIGHT_TEST_PROVIDER=cuda`), all passing; FamilyGenerationTests for `gemma-4`
  (gemma-4-E2B-it HF ids, head sizes 256 / 512, CPU / Vulkan / CUDA; the GGUF cases need files not on this machine) and `qwen3` (33 run,
  30 skipped for missing files), all passing.

### 74.5 Measured and not kept

* **MMQ (int8 tensor cores) for Q4_K / Q6_K at decode batches** (`SHARPLIGHT_MMQ=q4_k,q6_k`, from 33 rows): Qwen3-8B steps at 64
  sequences 24.61 → 25.51 ms on CUDA and 23.11 → 24.50 ms on Vulkan, 32 unchanged. The f16 GEMM on dequantized tiles stays.
* **Four warps for head size 256** in the hand-written prefill attention: 114 against 143 TFLOPS with eight (harness, 4096 queries).
  A single-stage 64-key tile at 256 does not fit (and is wrong without a second stage).
* **Three stages at head size 512**: 3 x 32 KiB plus the exchange exceed the 99 KiB a block may take.

### 74.6 Leads worth promoting and the next levers

Large enough to promote (like for like, same hour, both engines interleaved):

* **Vulkan batched decode against llama.cpp's Vulkan backend: 1.7-2.5x** on every model (Qwen3-8B 2.13 / 1.72x at 16 / 64 sequences,
  Qwen3.8 27B 2.48 / 2.46x, Gemma 4 31B 2.03x at 16), with llama.cpp's second, warm pass; our Vulkan steps are within 0.9-1.1x of our
  CUDA ones, llama.cpp's Vulkan batched path is far from its CUDA one.
* **Vulkan prefill**: 1.12-1.18x for both Qwen models at every length, Gemma 4 31B 1.10 / 1.27 / 1.21x at 512 / 2K / 8K.
* **Qwen3.8 27B (hybrid)**: batched decode on CUDA 1.17 / 1.55x at 16 / 64 sequences, prefill 1.11-1.19x on CUDA and 1.15-1.16x on
  Vulkan at every length (32K from 0.84 / 0.87x), single-stream decode 1.05x (CUDA) / 1.26x (Vulkan, llama.cpp's tg128 moved between
  35.7 and 40.2 over the day).
* **Prefill at 32K on CUDA**: Qwen3-8B 1.19x, Qwen3.8 27B 1.19x.

Against vLLM (74.3.1, comparable but not identical 4-bit checkpoints) nothing here is a lead to promote except Qwen3-8B's single-stream
and 32K decode (1.05x); vLLM leads prefill (0.76-0.91x) and batched decode (0.62-0.78x).

Parity, not a lead: single-stream decode of Qwen3-8B (0.99-1.01x) and Gemma 4 on Vulkan (1.03x), decode at 32K (1.01-1.06x, Qwen),
Qwen3-8B CUDA prefill at 512-8K (1.06-1.09x) and its CUDA batched decode (0.99x), Gemma 4 CUDA prefill at 2K / 8K (1.02 / 0.98x).
Behind: Gemma 4 on CUDA beyond prefill (below), decode at 128K (0.94 / 0.96x for the 27B, the decode attention at head size 256).

Levers, ranked:

0. **Gemma 4 31B on CUDA** is where the feed's biggest remaining gaps are: decode 0.96x, decode at 32K 0.90x, 16 sequences 0.84x, prefill
   at 512 tokens 0.89x, and 32K / 128K contexts that do not fit on the session path (window-sized caches exist only in the paged
   decoder: 44.8 GiB at 32K) or in the paged decoder at 128K (30.4 GiB). In order: window-sized caches for the session graphs; a
   tensor-core split-K decode kernel for head size 512 (the 10 global layers' 8-head groups run the generic `decode`); then the
   512-token prefill (the GEMMs at 512 rows).
1. **K-quant GEMM at 17-64 rows on CUDA** (Qwen3-8B 64 sequences 0.98x after this round's graph branches): the generated `gemm_cm2`
   on dequantized tiles reads Q4_K / Q6_K weights at 240-560 GB/s at 32-64 rows (the 1-row matvec at ~700); CUDA's compiled form is
   10-30 % slower per kernel than the same Slang kernel on the NVIDIA Vulkan driver (LM head [4096 → 151936] Q6_K at 32 rows 1317
   against 908 µs). A hand-written K-quant decode GEMM (dequantize into registers, f16 MMAs, 32 / 64 token rows) is the CUDA lever.
2. **Decode attention at head size 256 at long depth** (Qwen3.8 27B at 128K, 0.94x / 0.96x): the split-K `decode` reads the cache at
   620 GB/s on CUDA and, after this round's two rows per batch, ~520 on Vulkan (`profiles/prof_q27_d128k_*.txt`); the tensor-core
   decode kernel covers 64 / 128 only (lever 4).
3. **Gemma 4 global-layer attention at 32K+**: the split-head kernel runs at 112 TFLOPS against 143 at head size 256; the pair's
   score exchange and 16-key tiles cost barriers. A one-warp form with Q fragments re-read from shared memory would avoid the exchange.
4. **Native decode attention for head sizes 256 / 512** (the tensor-core split-K kernel covers 64 / 128).

### 74.7 Reproduce

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<i> SHARPLIGHT_VK_DEVICES=<i> GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<i> LLAMA_ROOT=...
M=~/models/gguf/gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf   # or Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf (DEPTHS="32768 131072"), Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf (DEPTHS=32768)
for P in cuda vulkan; do DEPTHS="32768 131072" SEQS="16" bench/s74_feed.sh out gemma4-31b $M $P; done
python3 bench/s74_summarize.py out gemma4-31b
# hand-written prefill attention harness (head sizes 128 / 256 / 512)
nvcc -O3 -arch=sm_120 -std=c++17 -DHQ=32 -DHKV=4 -DD=512 -DDV=512 -DTQ=4096 -DNPAST=0 -DWINDOW=0 -DHAS_SINKS=0 -DFN_WARPS=8 -DFN_STAGES=2 \
  -DKFILE='"../../src/Sharplight.Shaders/Kernels/attn_prefill_native.cu"' bench/s58_attn/bench_attn.cu -o b && ./b
# A/B switches of this round: SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_CONCURRENT=0, SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_FE_WINDOW=0, SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_FE_WIDE=0,
# SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_CFG=1024,128,64 (Vulkan's one row per batch), SHARPLIGHT_DISABLE_FEATURES=native_attention
```

## 75. LLM round 24: one expert-GEMM main loop per fragment count; gpt-oss-20b on CUDA repaired after perf/offload-r5; 64-row expert tiles measured (2026-11-21)

Branch `perf/llm-r24` (base `develop` at `ff3b70b1`, perf/offload-r5 merged). GPU 0 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, 82 SMs,
200 W cap, performance counters blocked), shared with perf/feed-r1, a server agent and a model-feed publish job: every timed run held the
verify lock, before and after alternated in the same hold, vLLM 0.33.0 (§56's CUDA build) profiled inside the final hold. Raw output in
[`bench/results/s75/`](../bench/results/s75).

**`develop` was broken for gpt-oss-20b on CUDA.** Since the perf/offload-r5 merge its greedy text is garbage from the first generated
token ("I, given that the pathwise values, the next of the overall ... atposyn"), and its 64-sequence decode step looked 35 % faster (10.8-11.5
against 17.7 ms: the garbage hidden states route to few experts, gate / up 102 µs per layer against ~340). Vulkan is unaffected. Bisected
(`bisect/`): `b4ed568e` and `9c69ca35` are correct, `572eeb80` ("elementwise groups after int-dot matmuls in the matvec's store") is not,
and with its lowering reverted (its kernels kept) the text is correct again; none of the new `SHARPLIGHT_NO_*` switches restores it, nor a
fresh compilation cache. The commit limited the GEMM store / split-K reduction epilogue to f32 weights, so that epilogues folded for
int-dot weights run as their own launch; that also moved the biases of gpt-oss's f16 projections (q / k / v as one multi-output matmul,
o, the router) to the separate launch path, which produces wrong results on CUDA. The fix keeps the exclusion for int-dot weights only
(`GraphLowerer.MatMul.cs`); gpt-oss-20b's greedy text is then byte-identical to the §73 build's (`060d579c`). Why the separate path is
wrong on CUDA is not found: the new `MatMulEpilogueTests.HalfWeightsBias` (q / k / v + router shapes, f16 weights with biases, 1-300
rows) passes on the broken build too, so the failure needs more of gpt-oss's graph. All "before" numbers below are `develop` with this
fix.

### 75.2 The expert GEMM: one main loop per live fragment count

`gemm_moe_native.cu` skips a partial tile's row fragments past its rows (predicated-off MMAs still take the tensor pipe's time) through a
switch over the warp's live fragment count, which sat inside the K loop: twice per K step, around the MMAs of each 32-value block. The
switch now selects one of `NM_FM` + 1 copies of the whole software pipeline, each a tight loop with its fragment count fixed at compile
time (the products are unchanged: same MMAs, same order). Sustained replay of §67.2 / §73.3 (24 layer copies back to back, ms per layer,

### 75.3 64-row expert tiles (lever 1 of §73.6), measured and not kept

On vLLM's routing 2.27 experts per layer have more than 32 items and cost a second 32-row tile. Variants of one launch with 64-row
routing tiles (each expert's weights read once up to 64 items), sustained replay as 75.2, ms per layer (gate / up, down; "small tiles" = the
same build on 32-row routing, i.e. the cost of the 64-row build where no expert needs it):

| variant | vLLM routing, 64-row tiles | small tiles | our routing, 64-row tiles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32-row `develop` | 0.3385-0.3419, 0.1755-0.1775 (32-row tiles) | | 0.3426-0.3459, 0.1747-0.1769 |
| 32-row, hoisted loop (75.2) | 0.3371-0.3400, 0.1718-0.1734 | | 0.3390-0.3402, 0.1723-0.1734 |
| §73's 64-row build (gate / up without the factor table, down in 3 stages) | 0.3482-0.3488, 0.1785-0.1790 | 0.3642-0.3665, 0.1807-0.1815 | 0.3499-0.3733, 0.1839-0.1858 |
| one loop over the fragments with a warp-uniform branch per fragment instead of the switch | | 0.4435, 0.2256 | |
| activations one stage behind the weights in a 3-slot ring (64-row stages fit twice per SM with the table; down at 128 weight rows), switch in the loop | 0.3440-0.3455, 0.1847-0.1855 | 0.3610-0.3631, 0.1926-0.1934 | |
| the same without the 3-fragment case (rounded up to 4) | 0.3426-0.3433, 0.1850-0.1852 | 0.3526-0.3532, 0.1886-0.1890 | |
| hoisted loop + split ring | 0.3295-0.3303, 0.1739-0.1762 | 0.3411-0.3427, 0.1805-0.1829 | 0.3560-0.3571, 0.1815-0.1816 |
| hoisted loop, no split ring, no table (down at 128 weight rows) | 0.3328, 0.1777 | 0.3470, 0.1849 | 0.3515, 0.1799 |
| 32-row, hoisted loop + split ring | | 0.3391, 0.1750 (vLLM routing) | 0.3421, 0.1790 |

* The best 64-row form (hoisted + split ring) takes 2.3 % off gate / up on vLLM's routing but adds 1.2 % on down there and 5 % on gate /
  up on ours, so the gain needs a per-expert choice. Per tile, its 64-row tiles cost 21.3 µs against 12.9 µs for a 32-row one (gate /
  up on vLLM's routing: 0.3303 ms = 21.9 small tiles x 12.9 µs + 2.27 large ones): the second 32 rows cost two thirds of a tile, not the
  little the weight-read model of §73.3 suggested, so even a free per-expert choice gains 4.4 µs per large expert (~3 % of gate / up on
  vLLM's routing, ~1.5 % on ours).
* What makes the 64-row build dearer for small tiles: code size inside the loop (dropping one switch case gains 2.3 %, hoisting the switch
  out of the loop 5 %), the split ring's shallower activation pipeline (+0.9 % gate / up, +3.9 % down even at 32 rows) and, without the ring,
  the decode without the factor table. Registers (102-126 of 128) and occupancy (two blocks per SM in every variant) are not it.
* A per-expert tile height in one launch therefore needs either two launches (32-row tiles, then 64-row tiles of the experts above 32
  items, a second routing list) or a kernel whose 64-row code path costs nothing when unused; with the gain bounded at ~3 % of the expert
  GEMMs on vLLM-like routing it moves down the plan.

### 75.4 Qwen3-8B-FP8's norms with the FP8 quantization

The row norm's shared copy of the row (read four consecutive values per lane by the E4M3 and q8_1 quantizations, a stride of four words:
4-way bank conflicts, offload-r5's note) gets one padding word per 32 values, and the FP8 quantization loop is unrolled where every lane
has the same groups (four for 4096-wide rows). Same arithmetic, same codes. Profile of the 64-sequence step (`profiles/`): the fused Add +
RmsNorm + E4M3 launch 11.41 → 11.19 ms over 1440 launches (7.92 → 7.77 µs mean, min 5.2 → 5.1); the step is within noise (15.81-15.99
against 15.91-15.94 ms). The launch is not bound by its quantization: it moves ~4.3 MB per 64-row launch (f32 residual and hidden rows in,
the f32 sum and the f32 normalized rows out, the E4M3 rows), where vLLM's fused kernel moves bf16 rows (~1.8 MB). What would help is the
residual stream in bf16 / f16 or the normalized f32 rows skipped when every reader takes the E4M3 copy (the norm's skip variant exists for
the half copies, `ReadersUseCopy`); not done this round.

| benchmark | CUDA / vLLM | where the time goes |

| Qwen3-8B-FP8 decode step, 64 sequences | 0.98 | norms with the E4M3 rows (0.56 ms, f32 rows in and out), the o / down inputs' own quantization (0.37 ms), q / k norm + rope |

| Qwen3-8B-FP8 long prefill 128K | 0.94 | attention at head size 128 |

Ranked levers:

1. **Marlin's memory path** (§73.6 item 2, now first): a repacked weight layout read in contiguous 16-byte-per-thread blocks with an
   explicit deep L2 prefetch instead of a hint on every copy, judged by energy per byte with the sampler. It is the larger part of the
   gap at 64 sequences (Marlin -10 % per byte on both routings), where 64-row tiles are worth at most ~3 % of the expert GEMMs (75.3).
2. **Qwen3-8B-FP8's small launches**: the residual stream's norm launches move f32 rows (75.4); skip the normalized f32 rows when every
   reader takes the E4M3 copy, quantize the o / down inputs in their producers (attention combine, gate / up epilogue), q / k norm +
   rope in one launch (~0.5-0.8 ms per 64-sequence step together).
3. **Long-context 4-stream decode at 128K (0.93x)**: the 16-row expert GEMMs on fed-back routing and the LM head.
4. **Per-expert tile height in two launches** (32-row tiles, then 64-row tiles of the experts above 32 items from a second routing list):
   ≤ ~3 % of the expert GEMMs on vLLM-like routing, ~1.5 % on ours (75.3).
5. **The separate epilogue launch path on CUDA**: the bias of f16 projections run as its own launch gave garbage for gpt-oss-20b; the fix
   avoids the path for those weights, but why it is wrong on CUDA (and right on Vulkan) is not found, and HalfWeightsBias (q / k / v
   and router shapes) does not reproduce it: a failing test from gpt-oss's own graph is still needed.
6. **Fused combine in `attn_decode_native.cu`** for narrow groups; **head size 128 prefill attention** (Qwen3 128K 0.94x).

## 76. LLM round 25: the separate matmul epilogue's root cause (q / k / v biases read before the multi-output GEMM wrote them); wide row norms for decode steps; a K-major expert weight layout measured (2026-11-21)

Branch `perf/llm-r25` (base `develop` at `bae54776`, `2a6c6611` with perf/feed-r1 merged before the final hold). GPU 0 of the RunPod
machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, 82 SMs, 200 W cap), shared with perf/feed-r1: every timed run held the verify lock, `develop` and this
round alternated in the same hold, vLLM 0.33.0 (§56's CUDA build) profiled inside it. Raw output in [`bench/results/s76/`](../bench/results/s76).

### 76.1 Root cause of §75's gpt-oss-20b garbage: the separate epilogue launch ran before the multi-output GEMM

A matmul whose epilogue (a bias row) is not applied in its own split-K reduction gets it as an elementwise launch emitted right after the
matmul's launches (`GraphLowerer.LowerMatMul`). q / k / v projections that read the same rows also form a multi-output group
(`GraphLowerer.MultiGemm.cs`): each member is lowered on its own, and the group's one GEMM over the concatenated weights, which serves
9-256 rows in place of the members' split launches, is emitted **after the group's last member**. For those batches the members' bias
adds therefore read their products before the multi-output GEMM wrote them (left-over values of an earlier launch), and nothing in the
recorded hazards could reorder them: the add precedes the write in program order. Before `572eeb80` every f16 / bf16 bias was applied in
the reduction (the multi-output GEMM's `MULTI_BIAS` store), so only paths without a fused bias hit it:

| path | weights | providers | on `develop` |
|---|---|---|---|
| int-dot weights (since `572eeb80` their epilogues run as their own launch; the gemm_cm2 multi-output GEMM is CUDA-only) | Q8_0, K-quants, ... | CUDA | **broken**: Qwen2.5 0.5B-7B GGUF, gpt-oss-20b Q4_K_M GGUF (all in the verified catalog), any GGUF model with separate biased q / k / v |
| the fp8 GEMM's batches (its multi-output form has no bias store; the member's reduction epilogue does not cover them) | E4M3 | CUDA and Vulkan | **broken** for FP8 checkpoints with q / k / v biases (none verified) |
| f16 / bf16 with `SHARPLIGHT_SPLITK_EPILOGUE=0` or `SHARPLIGHT_NO_MATMUL_EPILOGUE=1` | f16 / bf16 | CUDA | broken (the switch paths); gpt-oss-20b on `572eeb80` |

Evidence (`bug/`): gpt-oss-20b (safetensors) on `develop` with `SHARPLIGHT_SPLITK_EPILOGUE=0` gives §75's garbage ("I, given that the
pathwise values ..."), with `SHARPLIGHT_MULTI_GEMM=0` as well it is correct, and this round's build with `SHARPLIGHT_SPLITK_EPILOGUE=0`
gives the default text. Greedy, CUDA, the ~40-word prompt: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q8_0 "-vehicle-ase-los-los-los ..." → the Vulkan text
byte for byte; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M "pione g but with a change in perspective ..." → "Water and power have played a significant
role ..."; gpt-oss-20b Q4_K_M "!!!!!!!!..." → a coherent continuation. The ~1000-token prompt was correct before too (its prefill rows are
above the multi-output GEMM's 256) and is unchanged.

**Fix** (`LowerSeparateEpilogue`): the separate epilogue launch of a multi-output group's member runs, for the bindings the group's GEMM
serves, as a launch emitted right after that GEMM (`MultiGemmGroup.AfterEmit`); other bindings keep their launch in place, so batches the
GEMM does not serve, and every model whose biases were fused, run the same launches in the same order as before. Both separate paths (no
reduction epilogue; bindings the reduction did not cover, e.g. the fp8 GEMM's) use it. 8f4a8727's fusion for f16 / bf16 weights stays (it
is the faster form), and int-dot weights keep their own bias launch (now after the GEMM).

**Why §75's test passed on the broken build:** `MatMulEpilogueTests.HalfWeightsBias` read the graph's input directly, which lives
outside the activation arena, so each projection made its own f16 copy and the multi-output group was skipped ("members differ"); and its
biases were constants, not weights, so no bias unit formed. `ProjectionBiases` (replacing it) reads a norm's rows with weight biases, in
gpt-oss-20b, Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-7B shapes, f16 / Q8_0 / Q4_K / FP8 weights, 1-300 rows; `ProjectionBiasesSeparateEpilogue` reruns
it with `SHARPLIGHT_SPLITK_EPILOGUE=0`. On `develop` (`bug/projection_biases_develop_vs_fix.txt`): CUDA Q8_0 x3, Q4_K and both f16
shapes with the switch fail (q off by 0.1-1.0), Vulkan FP8 fails; this round: 13 / 13 on both providers. `SHARPLIGHT_MULTI_DEBUG=1` now
also lists the groups emitted.

### 76.3 Wide row norms for decode steps

The fused Add + RmsNorm (+ E4M3 rows) launch runs one 256-thread workgroup per row: at a 64-sequence step, 64 workgroups on 82 SMs, each
thread holding 16 values of a 4096-wide row, so the launch's time is one row's latency (load, block reduction, normalized row through
shared memory, E4M3 quantization). With 1024 threads (four values each) the phases are 4x shorter per thread. Lowering: on targets that
compile CUDA C++ (every CUDA device runs 1024-thread blocks; Vulkan only guarantees 256 invocations, so it keeps 256), rows of 4096
values and more, steps of at most `ComputeUnits` rows (one wave) take the 1024-thread kernel, larger steps the 256-thread one
(`SHARPLIGHT_NORM_WIDE=0` turns it off, `SHARPLIGHT_NORM_THREADS=n` sets every norm's width for experiments). Profiles
(`profiles/`, two runs each, 64 sequences, 20 steps): Qwen3-8B-FP8's fused norms 10.84-10.89 → 9.54-9.55 ms, step 15.73 → 15.53-15.55 ms
in profile mode; gpt-oss-20b's 2880-wide norms at 1024 threads 2.89-2.99 → 2.99-3.05 ms (slower, so they keep 256). Greedy text
byte-identical on CUDA (76.5): the norm's sum of squares is a different order of the same f32 additions, which on these prompts changes
no token.

The other Qwen3 small-launch levers of §75.6 measured or checked: the norm already skips its f32 normalized rows at 17+ rows when every
reader takes the E4M3 copy (all 72 norms of Qwen3-8B-FP8 take the skip variant: `ReadersUseCopy` is true for each), so §75.4's "f32 rows
out" was the residual sum only; q / k norm + rope (two `rope_row` launches and a cache write per layer, 0.53 ms per step) and the o / down
input quantization in their producers (0.37 ms) are not done.

### 76.4 A K-major expert weight layout with bulk L2 prefetches (lever 1 of §75.6), measured and not kept

Marlin reads a repacked weight layout in contiguous blocks with a deep prefetch. In the harness (`bench/s56_moe`, sustained replay of
§73.3, 24 layer copies, ms per layer, two rounds, `harness/kmajor_bulk_prefetch.txt`; `rejected/kmajor_*.diff`), each 16-row MXFP4 group
is stored K-step-major ([K / 64 steps][16 rows x 32 code bytes][32 scale bytes], 544 contiguous bytes per step instead of 16 rows 1440
bytes apart), so a stage's codes are 8 (gate / up) or 12 (down) contiguous 512-byte runs; optionally one thread per group issues
`cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2` of the group's step `kb + D` (`NM_BPF=D`, `NM_BPF_N` steps at once). Products identical to the reference
(same maxima as `develop`'s layout).

| variant | gate / up, vLLM routing | down, vLLM routing | gate / up, our routing | down, our routing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `develop` layout, 256-byte hints | 0.3389-0.3405 | 0.1737-0.1746 | 0.3393-0.3411 | 0.1720-0.1733 |
| K-major, 256-byte hints | 0.3433-0.3435 | 0.1818-0.1820 | 0.3680-0.3683 | 0.1897 |
| K-major + bulk prefetch 4 steps ahead | 0.3499-0.3500 | 0.1812 | 0.3608-0.3662 | 0.1816-0.1821 |
| K-major + bulk prefetch 8 ahead, 4 steps per prefetch | 0.3495-0.3504 | 0.1848-0.1849 | 0.3610-0.3644 | 0.1887-0.1891 |
| K-major + bulk prefetch 4 ahead, no hints | 0.3503-0.3505 | 0.1812-0.1816 | 0.3605-0.3636 | 0.1816-0.1841 |

Every K-major form is slower (1-8 %). The current layout's 256-byte hint on each row's 32-byte copy fetches the row's next seven K steps,
a prefetch depth of eight steps on every row for free; the K-major layout puts the next steps 544 bytes away, where the hint no longer
reaches, and one bulk prefetch per group and step (issued by 8-12 threads) does not replace it. So the remaining per-byte gap to Marlin
is not its layout as such; candidates are its larger blocks (up to 64 rows of an expert per pass, §75.3) and the clock it holds at the
power limit (§73.2).

### 77.2 Window-sized KV caches for single-sequence sessions

Until now only the paged multi-sequence decoder (serving, BatchBench) gave sliding-window layers window-sized caches (§60); the
session path (CLI, Studio, one-slot serving) kept a row per position in every cache, so Gemma 4 31B (50 of 60 layers attend to a
1024-key window, 0.8 MB per token) needed 44.8 GiB at 32K.

* `SessionKvLayout` (Core, generic: any graph whose caches only sliding-window attention reads, `MultiSequence.WindowedCaches`): when
  the decode graph has such caches, `CreateSession` compiles the one-slot paged form of the graph (`MultiSequence.Transform` with
  window rows), the same kernels the serving decoder runs on CPU, Vulkan, CUDA and Metal. Both block tables are fixed and uploaded
  once: the full caches map position p to row p, the window caches block b to block b mod R of a ring of
  R = ceil((window + rows per pass − 1) / 16) + 1 blocks, every position one pass reads or writes. The session only appends, so no
  query ever sees a reused row; `InferenceSession` fills the sequence tables per pass (one run of slot 0).
* Used where the ring at most halves those caches (the one-slot paged form costs ~2 % of a CUDA decode step against the contiguous
  cache: Gemma 4 31B at 4K context 37.96 → 37.25 tok/s, GPU 26.13 → 26.68 ms; Vulkan 38.43 either way). Fallbacks to the plain
  graph: `window_kv` or `paged_kv` disabled, encoder-decoder graphs, graphs without a multi-sequence form, devices without the paged
  kernels. Nothing new is stored in `.slm`: the layout is derived from the stored graph at compile time.
* `EstimateFootprint(slots: 1)`, the automatic rows per pass (`SessionFootprint`) and `PlacementPlanner.Estimate` count the ring.

| Gemma 4 31B Q4_K_M, session path (CUDA) | rows per pass | ring rows | weights + state | result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 32K, f16 KV, before | | (full: 32,768) | 44.8 GiB | does not fit |
| **32K, f16 KV** | 1024 | 2,064 | **21.14 GiB** | prefill 1351-1359 tok/s, decode after it 30.1-30.2 tok/s |
| **128K, f16 KV** | 512 | 1,552 | **28.23 GiB** | fits (prefill 512 1491 tok/s, decode 37.0 tok/s at shallow depth) |
| **128K, q8_0 KV** | 1024 | 2,064 | **23.20 GiB** | fits (decode 36.4 tok/s at shallow depth) |
| 128K, paged decoder with 2 slots (BatchBench, §74) | 2048 | | 30.42 GiB | does not fit |

So 128K fits a 32 GB card on the session path with f16 caches; the 10 global layers (head size 512, 4 KV heads) hold 5 GiB at 128K,
the 50 window layers 1.2-1.6 GiB. A timed 128K run was not made (seven 128K prefills of the CLI bench take ~15 minutes of the shared
GPU); llama.cpp's 128K decode of this model is 25.0 tok/s (§74).

Correctness: `SessionWindowKvTests` (Families.Tests; tiny random Cohere2 MoE GGUF / HF and Gemma 4 MoE with 8-key windows, 16-row
passes so the 48-row ring wraps during prompts of 5 and 70 tokens and 40 decode steps): the ring gives the one-slot paged session's
logits bit for bit and the plain session's tokens, CPU / Vulkan / CUDA. Gemma 4 31B greedy text (`--chat --temp 0 -n 64`) is
identical with and without the ring on both providers.

### 77.3 The K-quant decode GEMM (CUDA, `native_gemm_kquant`)

At 9-64 rows the K-quant projections ran gemm_cm2 with split-K on dequantized tiles, at 285-390 GB/s on this card (§74's profiles:
Qwen3-8B gate / up [4096 → 12288] Q4_K 99.3 µs at 32 rows). `gemm_kq_native.cu` (Shaders, compiled by NVRTC, selected in
`GraphLowerer.KQuantGemm.cs` beside the f16 decode form, multi-output form for q / k / v of one format):

* A block covers 16, 32 or 64 token rows (by batch) and 64 weight rows; its eight warps take 8 weight rows each and every token row,
  so each weight value is dequantized once per block. A K step is one 256-value superblock: `cp.async` copies the activation rows
  (four 64-value swizzled sub-tiles, read by `ldmatrix`) and the raw Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K blocks of the 64 rows (each row's 16-byte
  window around its block: Q6_K rows of 210-byte blocks start at any even byte) into a ring of 2-4 stages (≤ 96 KiB). Each thread
  builds its `mma.sync.m16n8k16` B fragments straight from the raw codes (two codes per `byte_perm`, exact f16 integers from the
  0x6400 bias trick, then one f16 FMA with the sub-block scale and minimum; Q4_K / Q5_K scales unpacked with word operations), f32
  accumulation. No weight is ever written back as f16.
* K split only where the grid is small or its last wave nearly empty (Gemma's [21504 → 5376]: 84 blocks on 82 SMs, 220 → 182 µs
  split in two), reduced in the last block of each tile in slice order (deterministic, counters self-resetting).
* Batches of 9-16 rows of K-quant matmuls leave the skinny GEMM for it (`SkinnyMaxRowsFor`), the dual gate / up form included (two
  launches and the activation product: steps at 16 sequences Qwen3-8B 9.87 → 8.35 ms, Qwen3.8 27B 35.75 → 30.05, Gemma 4 31B 43.64
  → 38.12 against keeping the skinny dual form, `ab22`). Decode batches whose generated
  split would be 1 (wide matrices, e.g. Qwen3.8 27B gate / up [5120 → 17408] at 16 rows: 165 µs each on unsplit gemm_cm2) are routed
  to the split-K emission, where the K-quant GEMM takes them (`NativeKQuantPlanSplit`).

Kernel times (bench/s77_kq harness, sustained µs over 16 weight copies, against §74's gemm_cm2 in the step profile):

| shape | 16 rows | 32 rows | 64 rows | gemm_cm2 (32 / 64 rows) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Q4_K [4096 → 12288] | 43.8 | 52.4 (482-512 GB/s) | 82.1 | 99.3 / 115.9 |
| Q6_K [12288 → 4096] | 58.8 | 60.4 (650 GB/s) | 89.7 | 127.3 / 145.7 |
| Q4_K [4096 → 4096] | 14.1 | 17.8 | 27.3 | 31.5 / 43.6 |
| Q6_K [21504 → 5376] (Gemma down, unaligned blocks) | 182.5 | 179.7 | 282 | |

Decode steps (CUDA, GPU ms, feature on / off in the same hold, `bench/results/s77/ab13`):

| sequences | 9 | 16 | 24 | 32 | 48 | 64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M, off | 10.27 | 11.77 | 18.61 | 19.65 | 21.43 | 23.51 |
| **on** | **7.80** | **8.31** | **10.49** | **11.00** | **16.61** | **16.91** |
| Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M, off | 36.38 | 43.26 | 68.93 | 73.69 | 83.11 | 93.36 |
| **on** | **27.31** | **30.16** | **39.05** | **41.62** | **65.08** | **71.14** |

feature is CUDA's); Gemma 4 31B on Vulkan at 16 sequences 306 tok/s against 310 in §74.

outputs, bias rows, q / k / v multi-output) against the CPU (f32 products: the CPU's int-dot path quantizes activations below 32 rows)

### 77.4 Measured and not kept

* **Split rings** (v4: 64-value activation stages in a shallow ring, weight superblocks copied 2-3 ahead in their own slots): more
  barriers per superblock; Q6_K [12288 → 4096] at 32 rows 76.0 against 60.4 µs, Q4_K [4096 → 12288] 56.6 against 52.4.
* **2 x 4 warps** (token halves x 16 weight rows, v1): each weight value dequantized twice; Q4_K [4096 → 12288] at 32 rows 58.7 µs.
* **Per-value scale lookups** for Q4_K (`get_scale_min_k4` per sub-block): 54.6 against 52.4 µs with word-wise unpacking.
* **64-row token tiles below 33 rows** (two stages only: 96-107 µs for the 32-row shapes above) and **two 32-row tiles at 64 rows**
  (each block re-reads the weights: 89.5 / 115.1 against 82.1 / 89.7 µs).
* **The wave-count K split** (`WaveFillSplit`) on grids of 1.5-3 waves: memory-bound blocks of a partial last wave run faster, so
  splitting [4096 → 12288] (192 blocks) cost 5 %; the split is kept only for nearly empty last waves and small grids.
* **Batches of 9-16 rows on unsplit gemm_cm2**: capping the skinny GEMM first sent wide gate / up matrices whose generated split is 1
  to the unsplit gemm_cm2 (Qwen3.8 27B at 16 sequences 42.96 → 47.98 ms, Gemma 4 31B 49.23 → 54.93 ms); routing them to the split-K
  emission (`NativeKQuantPlanSplit`) puts them on the K-quant GEMM.

New tools: `bench/s78_decode/bench_decode.cu` (a harness of `attn_decode_native.cu` at long contexts: T sequences of L keys in a
contiguous or paged f16 cache, gpt-oss-20b's shape by default; timing, read rate and a check of the merged partials against an f32
reference), `--gpu-util` in `s54_vllm_decode_profile.py` (its `--depth` profile of 4 x 130,048 keys needs 0.92).

### 78.1 The 4 x 128K point like for like: vLLM's decode step profiled at depth 130,048

The 0.93x of §73-§76 compared our GPU ms per step (BatchBench `--feedback`, depth 131,072) with vLLM's 174.9 tok/s from §64, which is
`s58_long_vllm.py`'s `(t(129 tokens) - t(1 token)) / 128` at depth 130,560: four 130K-token prefills of ~80 s each, minus each other,
for a decode of ~3 s, so a 2 % difference between the two prefills moves the decode figure by 50 %. vLLM's decode past 131,072
positions hits a device assert, so this round measures **both engines at depth 130,048** (127K; 129 more tokens stay below 131,072) and
takes vLLM's step from its own profile (`s54_vllm_decode_profile.py --seqs 4 --depth 130048 --ctx 131072 --skip 5`, random-token prompts,
steps 6-15 of its annotated decode ranges), the method of §64 for the 64-sequence steps. vLLM's range has no LM head (its logits are
computed after it); ours costs 1.42 ms at 4 rows (the [2880 → 201088] f16 GEMM at 817 GB/s), and vLLM's bf16 one reads the same bytes.

| gpt-oss-20b, 4 streams, depth 130,048, fed back (GPU ms per step) | `develop` | this round | vLLM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| step (BatchBench min; vLLM: annotated range + 1.45 ms LM head and sampling at our cost) | 23.50-23.51 | **23.01-23.02** | 22.20 + 1.45 = 23.65 |
| ours / vLLM, profile method | 1.01 | **1.03** | |
| vLLM `s58_long_vllm.py` tok/s in the same hold (173.8 tok/s = 23.02 ms) | 0.98 | **1.00** | |
| full-attention layers (12 per step; our profile, 20 steps) | 16.47 ms (1.37 per layer) | 15.97 (1.33) | 15.57 (1.30, `kernel_mha`) |
| expert GEMMs gate / up + down | 2.80 + 1.29 | 2.80 + 1.29 | 3.96 (Marlin) |
| q / k / v + o projections | 2.03 | 2.04 | 2.11 (cutlass bf16) |
| LM head [2880 → 201088] | 1.42 | 1.42 | (outside the range) |
| 1 stream, depth 130,048 | 9.15-9.17 | 9.17 | 9.62 (103.9 tok/s, `s58_long_vllm.py`) |

`develop` and this round alternated twice in the final hold (`final/long/`), vLLM's profile twice in two holds (22.21 and 22.20 ms,
`profiles/vllm_gptoss_d130048_x4.txt`, `final/long/vllm_prof_d130048_x4.txt`), its tok/s once. The tok/s method gives vLLM 23.02 ms
per step here against 22.87 in §64 (174.9 tok/s); its step with our LM head is 23.65 by the profile, so its own LM head and sampling
are cheaper than ours or the difference method's noise is at least 0.6 ms (2.5 %); the two methods bracket the ratio at 1.00-1.03x.

So the point was at par before this round (0.98-1.01x), not 0.93x: vLLM's XQA attention (`kernel_mha`) took 1.30 ms per full-attention
layer against our 1.37 (each reads 1.07 GB of keys and values: 820 against 777 GB/s), its Marlin expert GEMMs 3.96 against our 4.09 ms
per step, its dense projections 2.11 against our 2.03; our small launches (~1.0 ms per step against ~0.35) are the rest. The
per-launch profile adds ~2 ms per step to our sums (25.7 ms of kernels against the 23.5 ms step), so only its shares are compared.

### 78.2 The decode attention prefetches its next tile into L2

`attn_decode_native.cu`'s warps each load a tile of 32 keys (16 at head size 128) straight from the cache into registers, compute it
and only then issue the next tile's loads: every tile waits a full DRAM latency. Each warp now first issues `prefetch.global.L2` for
the key and value rows of the tile after the current one (one 128-byte line per lane: lanes 0 / 1 of a row's four at head size 64,
all four at 128), then loads the current tile, which L2 then mostly serves. Same loads, same arithmetic in the same order: the
products are unchanged (the harness's maximum error against the f32 reference is identical, 1.13e-6 / 5.99e-7 / 2.1e-6).

Harness (`bench/s78_decode`, 20 launches, min, ms per launch and cache read rate; two rounds each, `harness/*.txt`):

| shape | `develop` | prefetch 1 tile ahead | other variants |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| gpt-oss-20b (64 / 8 heads, D 64), 4 x 130,048 keys, contiguous slots | 1.440 (740 GB/s) | **1.307 (815)** | 2 tiles ahead 1.353-1.359; 8 warps 1.439-1.443 |
| same, paged (16-key blocks in random order) | 1.405-1.416 (755) | **1.326-1.328 (803)** | 2 ahead 1.456-1.458; 8 warps 1.329; bulk prefetch of the blocks 1.327-1.328 |
| same, paged in order | 1.367-1.371 (778) | **1.307-1.309 (815)** | bulk 1.310-1.312 |
| gpt-oss-20b, 1 x 130,048, paged / contiguous | 0.344 / 0.344-0.346 | 0.340 / 0.337 | |
| gpt-oss-20b, 16 x 8192 / 64 x 2048 | 0.350-0.353 / 0.357-0.360 | 0.340-0.341 / 0.342 | |
| Qwen3-8B (32 / 8 heads, D 128), 4 x 32,768 / 64 x 2048 | 0.699-0.705 / 0.699-0.702 | 0.663-0.664 / 0.673-0.674 | |

* Without the prefetch, more key ranges help (4 x 130,048: 32 splits 1.44 ms, 82 splits 1.366, 256 splits 1.335-1.339, the tail of the
  3.1-wave grid), with it they do not (64 splits 1.336 against 1.327 paged), and in the engine the split counts moved the step by
  -0.1 to -0.3 ms within the hold's noise (`explore/engine_split_configs.txt`); the split rule is unchanged.
* The bulk form (`rejected/bulk_l2_prefetch.diff`: the KV group's blocks prefetch the next 16-key blocks of the cache together,
  `cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2`, each block an eighth) is as fast as the per-row one, not faster.

* Key ranges of fewer than four tiles per warp (`ND_PF_MIN_TILES`) skip the prefetch: with it, one stream at 32K (128 ranges of 256
  keys, two tiles per warp) took 6.16 → 6.21 ms per gpt-oss-20b step, and the harness shows the cost where the keys are L2-resident
  (1 x 32,768: 0.0413-0.0415 → 0.0428-0.0434 ms; with the limit 0.0404-0.0412, `harness/prefetch_short_ranges.txt`,
  `prefetch_min_tiles.txt`). Every shape of the table keeps the prefetch (4 x 130,048 paged with the limit: 1.331-1.333 ms).

In the engine (BatchBench, `--feedback`, the final build with the limit, two alternated pairs, `final/long2/`): 4 streams at depth
130,048 23.47-23.53 → **23.01 ms** (-2.0 %; the full-attention launches 329.4 → 319.5 ms over 20 steps in the profile, 1.37 → 1.33 ms
per layer), one stream 9.16 → 9.17-9.18, 4 x 32K 12.24-12.27 → 12.24-12.25, 1 x 32K 6.16-6.17 → 6.17-6.18 ms. The prefetch helps
where a warp streams many tiles of keys that are not in L2: long contexts; at 32K the attention is a quarter of the step and the gain
within the noise.

### 78.3 One launch for a layer's q rope, k rope + cache write and v cache write

Qwen3 lowers each layer's q / k norm + rope as two `rope_row` launches (the k one storing into the cache) and the v rows as a
`cache_write`: 108 launches per step. `GroupLayerRopes` (fusion pass) merges, per cached attention, the query rope unit, the key cache
write (with its rope and norm) and the value cache write into one unit, and `LowerRopeQkv` emits it as one `rope_qkv` launch (rope.slang:
one 64-thread workgroup per token and query, key or value head, the same arithmetic as rope_row / rope / cache_write) wherever the
rows are [T, heads, D] with contiguous heads, both caches are f16 or f32 of one shape and the two ropes differ only in their heads;
else the three launches stay (`SHARPLIGHT_ROPE_QKV_DEBUG=1` names the layer and the reason). Models without q / k norms (gpt-oss,
Llama, Qwen2.5) take it too.

* Qwen3-8B-FP8, 64 sequences, profile (`profiles/qwen3_64_*`): the three launches took 0.54 ms per step, `rope_qkv` 0.25; dispatches
  per step 439 → 367; the step 15.51 → 15.46 ms in that hold and 15.61-15.63 → 15.61 in the final one: the three launches were already
  independent branches of the captured CUDA graph (§74), so their launch latencies overlapped.
* **On Vulkan** the fused kernel gave wrong values from the second row on for heads of 16-64 values in `FusionTests.NormRopeIntoCache`
  (|d| 2.6e-3 against a tolerance of 7.9e-4; heads of 128 and 256 passed, and an earlier form that selected between the query and key
  pointers inside the kernel failed at 128 too, `explore/vulkan_rope_qkv_failure.txt`); the cause is not found, so the fusion is limited
  to targets that compile CUDA C++ and Vulkan keeps the three launches (its greedy text and steps are unchanged, 78.5).

### 78.4 Int-dot q / k / v biases in the multi-output GEMM's store

Since §76 the biases of int-dot q / k / v projections (Qwen2.5 GGUF, gpt-oss GGUF) are a separate launch after the multi-output GEMM.
A member whose epilogue is a lone bias add now hands the bias to its multi-output part (`EmitMatMulLaunches`' `multiBias`), so the group's
`gemm_cm2` adds it in its store for the batches it serves (`MULTI_BIAS`, as for f16 weights), writing the biased rows directly;
`MultiGemmGroup.StoresBias` drops the launch after it for those batches. `SHARPLIGHT_NO_INT_DOT_MULTI_BIAS=1` restores the separate
launch. `MatMulEpilogueTests.ProjectionBiases*` (Q8_0 and Q4_K shapes, 1-300 rows, also with `SHARPLIGHT_SPLITK_EPILOGUE=0`) pass on both
providers. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M, BatchBench `--text`: 16 / 64 sequences 11.43 / 19.44-19.62 ms (`develop`) against 11.42-11.46 / 19.55-19.65 (two alternated pairs); the multi-output
GEMM adds the bias for the 28 layers' q / k pairs (`final/q25_multi_debug.txt`, `SHARPLIGHT_MULTI_DEBUG=1`: "bias True"): within the noise (one small launch per layer).
After merging perf/feed-r2 (§77: the hand-written K-quant decode GEMM `gemm_kq_native.cu` and its q / k / v multi-output form, which
the group's GEMM hands its 9-64-row batches to): the multi-output parts carry the bias to that form too (it adds each member's bias in
its store, as `gemm_cm2`'s `MULTI_BIAS` does), and `StoresBias` covers every batch the group serves. Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M, two alternated
pairs with and without `SHARPLIGHT_NO_INT_DOT_MULTI_BIAS=1`: 16 / 32 / 64 sequences 7.15-7.16 / 8.93-8.98 / 14.09-14.15 against
7.19-7.20 / 8.99-9.11 / 14.02-14.20 ms (`postmerge/q25_bias_switch.txt`): within the noise; ProjectionBiases passes on the merged build
on both providers.

### 78.7 Gap to vLLM and plan (state after this round)

| benchmark | CUDA / vLLM | where the time goes |
|---|---:|---|
| gpt-oss-20b decode at depth 130,048, 1 / 4 streams, fed back | 1.05 / 1.00-1.03 | 4 streams: attention 1.33 against 1.30 ms per layer, our small launches ~0.65 ms more per step; expert GEMMs at par |
| gpt-oss-20b decode at depth 32,768, 1 / 4 streams | 1.08 / 1.10 | |
| gpt-oss-20b decode step, 64 sequences (`--text` / `--feedback`) | 0.98 / 1.01 | expert GEMMs (~12.3 ms against Marlin's 11.5; per byte Marlin ~10 % ahead, not by its layout, §76.4) |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 decode step, 64 sequences | 1.00 | the o / down inputs' E4M3 rows (0.36 ms, own launches); norms |
| gpt-oss-20b / Qwen3-8B-FP8 serving 16 / 64 streams | §72: 0.95 / 0.92, 0.94 / 0.93 | prompt waves on full expert tiles, decode steps |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 long prefill 128K | 0.94 (§70) | attention at head size 128 |

Ranked levers:

1. **The expert GEMM's per-byte efficiency against Marlin** (gpt-oss at 64 sequences, the largest remaining decode gap, ~0.8 ms per
   step): Marlin's blocking (one pass over up to 64 rows of an expert, two launches by tile height, §75.3), judged by energy per token
   with the sampler (§73.2). Not started this round.
2. **Serving 16 / 64 streams** (0.92-0.95x, not re-measured since §72): the prompt waves' full 128-row expert tiles and the decode steps
   in between.
3. **Qwen3's o / down E4M3 rows written by their producers** (attention's direct store / combine and the gate / up GEMM's SiLU·mul
   epilogue, 0.36 ms per 64-sequence step; needs a per-128-column amax in the epilogue). Not started this round.
4. **Small launches of few-row decode steps** (gpt-oss 4 x 128K: ~1.0 ms per step of adds, gathers, norms, routing against vLLM's
   ~0.35): fold the residual adds and the MoE gather into their neighbours.
5. **`rope_qkv` on Vulkan**: find why its SPIR-V form is wrong for heads of 64 or fewer values (78.3), then enable it there (Vulkan
   has no graph branches to overlap the three launches).
6. **Head size 128 prefill attention** (Qwen3 128K 0.94x); **fused combine in `attn_decode_native.cu`** for narrow groups.

### 78.8 Reproduce

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<i>
# harness: develop's kernel without the prefetch (-DND_PF=0), paged in random order (-DPAGED=1), in order (-DPAGE_SEQ=1), Qwen3's shape
cd bench/s78_decode && nvcc -O3 -arch=sm_120 -std=c++17 -DPAGED=1 -DCHECK=1 \
  -DKFILE='"../../src/Sharplight.Shaders/Kernels/attn_decode_native.cu"' bench_decode.cu -o d && ./d
nvcc ... -DHQ=32 -DD=128 -DHPW=4 -DL_KEYS=32768 ...
# both engines at depth 130,048, 4 streams, fed back
BB=bench/BatchBench/bin/Release/net11.0/BatchBench
$BB ~/models/hf/gpt-oss-20b --provider cuda --slots 4 --ctx 130560 --depth 130048 --batch 2048 --sizes 1,4 --modes greedy --reps 5 --feedback
python bench/s54_vllm_decode_profile.py ~/models/hf/gpt-oss-20b --seqs 4 --depth 130048 --ctx 131072 --steps 64 --skip 5 --gpu-util 0.92
python bench/s58_long_vllm.py ~/models/hf/gpt-oss-20b gptoss --lens "" --depths 32768,130048 --streams 1,4 --max-len 130560
# the switches: SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_PF=0, SHARPLIGHT_NO_ROPE_QKV=1 (SHARPLIGHT_ROPE_QKV_DEBUG=1), SHARPLIGHT_NO_INT_DOT_MULTI_BIAS=1
```

### 79.2 48-row token tiles

The 64-row token tile of `gemm_kq_native.cu` served every batch of 33-64 rows, so a 40- or 48-row batch paid for 64 rows of tensor
work (Qwen3-8B: 32 sequences 10.9 ms, 40 and 48 sequences 15.8-16.1 ms). The kernel takes `KQ_BM = 48` (three 16-row fragments per
warp, 24 KiB of activations per stage) and the lowering picks it for 33-48 rows (`NativeKQuantTileRows`; `SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_KQ_BM`
forces a tile). Harness (`bench/s77_kq`, sustained µs over 16 weight copies, 48 rows):

| shape | 64-row tile (2 stages) | **48-row tile, 2 stages** | 48-row tile, 3 stages (99 KiB) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q4_K [4096 → 12288] | 86.7 | **63.6** | 63.8 |
| Q6_K [12288 → 4096] | 97.3 | **73.1** | |
| Q4_K [4096 → 4096] | 31.2 | **21.6** | 21.2 |

The same lever on Vulkan's (and CUDA's other formats') generated GEMM: gemm_cm2 had 32- and 64-token tiles; it now has a 48-token tile
(one row of four subgroups with three 16-row fragments each, `[1, 4, 3, 2]`; `[1, 2, 3, 4]` for 32-value K blocks) for 33-48 rows,
the split-K probes include 48 (`NextSplitProbe`), and `SHARPLIGHT_GEMM2_TILE48=0` keeps 64. The split-f16 form keeps its tiles.

Decode steps (GPU ms, BatchBench `--feedback` at depth 256, minimum of 20 steps; A/B in one hold, `steps_*.txt`):

| model, provider | sequences | 64-row tiles | **48-row tiles** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M, CUDA | 40 | 15.79 | **12.18** |
| | 48 | 16.12 | **13.02** |
| Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M, CUDA | 48 | 64.15 | **55.86** |
| Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M, Vulkan | 40 | 19.74 | **17.71** |
| | 48 | 20.72 | **18.77** |

Greedy text (`--chat --temp 0 -n 64`, a 40-44-token prompt whose prefill runs the 48-row tiles): Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4 31B identical
with the 64-row tiles and the separate gate / up launches, and identical to Vulkan; Qwen3.8 27B identical too (its chat prompt is 84
tokens, so it checks the rest of the branch only).

### 79.3 The dual gate / up form

`KQ_DUAL`: one launch for a gate / up pair of one K-quant format feeding one elementwise group (SwiGLU, GELU-tanh · up): a block's 64
weight rows interleave the two matrices (even rows the gate's row o0 + r / 2, odd rows the up's), so each thread's two accumulator
columns of an MMA tile are the gate and up products of one output, and the store applies the group (`DualEpilogueCudaSource`, the
same expression the elementwise launch runs) after undoing a row-ranged copy's row scales. K splits reduce both products before the
epilogue. Emitted by `LowerDualMatMul` for the rows past the fused matvec / skinny range up to 64 (`EmitNativeKQuantDualGemm`), so a
decode step of 9-64 sequences runs one launch per layer instead of three (Qwen3-8B: 492 → 420 launches per step).

In the harness the dual launch beats the two launches it replaces (Q4_K [4096 → 12288] at 32 rows 98.9 µs against 2 x 52.4;
Qwen3.8 27B's [5120 → 17408] at 32 / 48 rows 164.1 / 203.9 µs against 2 x 87.3 / 2 x 109.8), but in the decode step the separate
launches already overlap on CUDA's graph branches (§74), so the step gain is small: Qwen3-8B 0.3-1 % at 9-64 sequences (32: 10.95 →
10.88 ms, 64: 16.47 → 16.36), Qwen3.8 27B within noise with the branches (32: 40.89-41.08 → 40.88-40.91, 48: 56.07-56.21 →
55.75-55.92) and 2.8 % without them (`SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_CONCURRENT=0`, 32: 42.79 → 41.59), Gemma 4 31B within noise (16: 37.38 /
37.70, 32: 50.93 / 51.29 with / without the separate launches, one run each). Kept (one launch and one f32 round trip less per layer,
never slower beyond run-to-run noise); `SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_KQ_DUAL=0` switches it off.

Tests: `KQuantGatedProjectionMatchesTheCpu` now covers 9-64 rows, Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K, SiLU and GELU-tanh, and 1000 outputs (a
partial 32-output tile), against the CPU.

### 79.4 The 64-row tiles: tensor-issue bound, not copy bound

The brief's lever was a deeper copy ring for the 64-row tile (two stages fit). Measured on Q4_K [4096 → 12288] at 64 rows (sustained
µs; the "no ..." variants are harness-only builds of the same kernel that skip one part):

| variant | µs |
|---|---:|
| kernel | 82.0 |
| weight blocks in a ring of their own, 3 deep (`KQ_WST = 3`, 91 KiB) | 84.8 |
| L2 prefetch 2 / 3 / 4 superblocks ahead (`prefetch.global.L2`), bulk prefetch (`cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2`) | 85.4-95.8 |
| one stage, two blocks per SM (`KQ_STAGES = 1`) | 83.4 |
| 2 x 4 warps (half the token rows, 16 weight rows each: half the `ldmatrix` traffic, twice the dequantization, `KQ_WM = 2`) | 82.9 |
| **no copies** (the first stage reused) | **53.5** |
| no copies, no `ldmatrix` | 49.8 |
| no copies, no dequantization | 52.6 |
| no copies, no `ldmatrix`, no dequantization (MMAs only) | **46.0** |
| the same with f16 accumulation (`mma ... f16.f16.f16.f16`) | 45.9 |
| no copies, no MMAs | 51.2 |
| no copies, no `ldmatrix`, no MMAs (dequantization only) | 36.1 |

The 1.57 M `mma.sync.m16n8k16` of a 64-row product alone take 46 µs (about 140 TFLOPS on this card at 200 W, the same with f16
accumulators; int8 `m16n8k32` at half the instruction count took 26 µs, i.e. the same instruction rate), and the dequantization and
`ldmatrix` work overlaps with them only partly (53.5 µs with everything but the copies), while streaming the weights alone needs
~45 µs. Deeper rings, prefetches and two blocks per SM do not move it, so the 64-row tile is bound by the MMA issue rate plus its
companions, not by copy latency. A faster 64-row tile needs fewer MMA instructions per weight byte: int8 MMAs on q8_1 activations
(twice the products per instruction; llama.cpp's MMQ), whose per-sub-block scale epilogue costs ~20 ALU operations per MMA and would
need its own design (79.7).

The one-stage form (`KQ_STAGES = 1`, kept as an option) helped the large 16- and 32-row grids (Q4_K [4096 → 12288] 43.8 → 39.9 µs at
16 rows, 53.3 → 48.6 at 32) but lost on small grids and Q6_K ([4096 → 4096] 14.1 → 19.0, 17.8 → 23.0; Q6_K [12288 → 4096] 58.8 → 66.7,
60.4 → 77.8), so the stage choice is unchanged.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 128K | 838.8 tok/s (156.3 s) | | |
| decode after the 128K prompt | 19.97 tok/s best, 19.43 median (GPU 49.93 ms) | 25.0 (tg64 at d 128K) | **0.80** |

### 79.6 Measured and not kept

* Separate weight ring (`KQ_WST`), L2 prefetches, 2 x 4 warps (`KQ_WM = 2`) and the one-stage form for 64-row tiles: 79.4. The

* 48-row tiles with three stages (99 KiB, past the 96 KiB cap that leaves L1 room): no faster than two (63.8 against 63.6 µs).

### 79.7 Leads worth promoting and the next levers

Promotable (like for like, same hold, both engines interleaved):

* **Batched decode at 48 sequences against llama.cpp**: Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M 1.40x (CUDA, from 1.16x) and 1.81x (Vulkan, from 1.72x);
  Qwen3.8 27B 2.01x on CUDA (from 1.76x). The 16-64 sequence range on CUDA is now 1.37-1.43x (8B) and 1.70-2.05x (27B).

Not promotable: Gemma 4 31B at 128K (0.80x of llama.cpp's decode), Gemma's single stream (0.89 / 0.96x).

Next levers:

1. **64-row K-quant tiles with fewer MMA instructions**: int8 `m16n8k32` on q8_1 activations (the copy the int-dot matvec already
   makes) with a per-sub-block scale epilogue that stays under the MMA time; or a 64-output-per-warp layout (16 weight rows per
   warp) that halves the `ldmatrix` traffic, which needs the Q4_K header in registers to fit two stages in 99 KiB (79.4).
2. **Gemma 4 31B decode at depth** (0.80x at 128K, 0.91x at 32K): the decode attention of the head-size-512 global layers (§74
   levers 2-4), coordinated with the LLM round that owns `attn_decode_native.cu`.
3. **Vulkan 64-row batches** (23.4 ms at 64 sequences against 15.6 at 32 on Qwen3-8B): gemm_cm2's 64-token tile; a hand-written
   coopmat K-quant kernel like CUDA's (raw blocks decoded in registers) is the larger lever there.
4. **Gemma 4 31B prefill 512 on CUDA** (0.89x).

### 79.8 Reproduce

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<i> SHARPLIGHT_VK_DEVICES=<i> GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<i> LLAMA_ROOT=...
LENS="512" DEPTHS=" " SEQS="16 32 48 64" BCTX=512 bench/s74_feed.sh out qwen3-8b ~/models/gguf/Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf cuda
BB=bench/BatchBench/bin/Release/net11.0/BatchBench
$BB ~/models/gguf/Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf --provider cuda --slots 48 --ctx 384 --depth 256 --sizes 48 --modes greedy --reps 20 --feedback
# A/B switches: SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_KQ_BM=64, SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_KQ_DUAL=0, SHARPLIGHT_GEMM2_TILE48=0, SHARPLIGHT_CUDA_CONCURRENT=0
# 128K session path (three 128K prefills: the warm-up, the timed one, the one before the decode steps)
SHARPLIGHT_BENCH_PREFILL_REPEATS=0 sharplight ~/models/gguf/gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf --provider cuda --bench 131072 --ctx 131328
# kernel harness (KQ_BM 16 / 32 / 48 / 64, KQ_DUAL=1, KQ_STAGES=1, KQ_WST, KQ_WM, KQ_PF)
cd bench/s77_kq && nvcc -O3 -arch=sm_120 -std=c++17 -DK=4096 -DN=12288 -DKQ_FMT=4 -DKQ_BM=48 -DKQ_STAGES=2 -DKQ_SPLIT=1 \
  -DKFILE='"../../src/Sharplight.Shaders/Kernels/gemm_kq_native.cu"' bench_kq.cu -o b && ./b 48
```

### 80.1 Where serving loses against vLLM (gpt-oss-20b, 64 streams)

`bench/s16_serve.sh` (64 slots of 512 tokens, ~250-token random-word prompts, 128 output tokens, `ignore_eos`, closed loop, 192 requests per
round), both engines in one hold before any change of this round (`serve0/`): ours 2925-2930 tok/s, vLLM 3139-3153 (0.93x); at 16 streams
1395-1405 against 1390-1435 (0.99x, within vLLM's round-to-round spread). vLLM's API server runs `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 on this
32 GB card (its default below 70 GB), our step budget is 2048 rows too, so both engines prefill the waves of prompts in steps of the same size.

Our round (`SHARPLIGHT_STEP_PROFILE`, `bench/s60_steps.py`, `profiles/steps64.csv`; `SHARPLIGHT_SCHED_TRACE=1`, `profiles/sched_trace_64.txt`):

| steps of a 64-stream round | steps | GPU ms per step | host idle per step | share of the round |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| decode only, 64 rows | 358 | 13.68 | 0.15 | 52 % |
| decode only, fewer rows (wave tails) | 134 | ~8.0 | 0.5 | 12 % |
| mixed (prompt chunks + decode rows; ~1,580 prompt rows) | 31 | 108.6 | 3.2 (a new row count: recorded, not replayed) | 36 % |

The round is GPU-bound (GPU busy 97.7 %); the host's share between steps is 0.15 ms on replayed decode steps (1.1 %), so scheduling,
sampling, detokenization and streaming are not where the 7 % go. Like for like per step:

* **Prompt rows**: vLLM's 1,792-row prompt step (7 prompts of 256 random tokens, `s54_vllm_decode_profile.py --prefill 256 --seqs 8`,
  `profiles/vllm_prefill_8x256.txt`) takes 97.7 ms (54.5 µs per row); ours (BatchBench `--mixed 0+256x8`, 8 prompts of 256) 125.5 ms for
  2,048 rows (61.3 µs per row, 12 % more). The expert GEMMs are at par per row (Marlin 74.4 ms for the 1,792 rows, 41.5 µs per row; our
  `gemm_moe_native` 83.0 ms for 2,008 rows, 41.3 µs). The rest is 23.3 ms (13.0 µs per row) for vLLM against 41 ms (20.4 µs per row):
  per 2,008-row step (`profiles/mixed.txt`, ms) the dense f16 projections 22.2 (cutlass ~18.5 at our row count), the two expert gathers
  4.5 (Marlin reads the routed rows through its sorted ids), `rope_qkv` 3.9 (vLLM's rope + cache write ~0.9), the slot sum 2.7 (vLLM
  `moe_sum` ~1.2), the add + norm launches 3.7 (f32 residual rows; vLLM's bf16 triton norms ~1.5), prefill attention 2.5 (flashinfer 1.55).
* **Decode steps**: inter-token latency p50 13.9 ms against vLLM's 13.2-13.35 (the 64-row decode steps; ours 13.68 GPU + 0.15 host).

So ~0.38 s of the 0.58 s per round are the prompt rows and ~0.2 s the decode steps.

### 80.2 Prefill attention: the runs' query tiles enumerated in grid y

`attn_prefill_native.cu` ran a grid of (query heads, query tiles of all T rows, runs): with eight 250-token prompts in a 2,008-row step,
each run needs 2 of the 16 tile rows and the other 14 x 9 x 64 blocks returned at once, at three blocks per SM (32 KB of stages each)
about 30 waves of empty blocks. Grid y is now ceil(T / FN_BR) + runs, a bound on the tiles of all runs together; each block finds its
(run, tile) by a warp prefix sum over the runs' tile counts (runs below MIX_RUN rows count zero tiles), longest tiles of a run first as
before. Same blocks, same arithmetic: products unchanged. BatchBench `--mixed` (`explore/attn1*`): the launch 102.8 → 87.4 µs per layer,
8 + 8 x 250 rows 124.12 → 123.59 ms, 40 + 7 x 250 113.22 → 112.13 ms, 2,048 prompt rows 125.75 → 125.51 ms. The rest of the gap to
flashinfer (32 µs per layer for the same 1,792 rows) is the kernel's 128-row tiles at 250-token prompts.

### 80.3 rope_qkv: several rows per workgroup

`rope_qkv` (§78.3) ran one 64-thread workgroup per (token, head) row: 2,048 tokens x 80 heads of gpt-oss are 164K workgroups of 32 busy
threads (64 values, no q / k norm), bound by how fast workgroups start (161 µs, ~500 GB/s). Each workgroup now runs QKV_RPW rows one after
another (`rope_qkv_row`; the norm's shared-memory reduction ends with a barrier before the next row reuses it). µs per launch
(`explore/rope_rpw/`), 64 / 2,048 tokens: 1 row 8.1 / 161.0, 4 rows 4.7 / 77.4, 8 rows 6.0 / 71.5, 16 rows 8.1 / 71.7; the lowering takes 4
below 32,768 rows and 8 from there for rows without a q / k norm. Rows with a norm keep one row per workgroup: with four, Qwen3-8B-FP8's
1 / 16 / 64-sequence steps were 0.3-0.6 % slower (11.02-11.03 / 12.66-12.67 / 15.65-15.68 against 10.95 / 12.60-12.61 / 15.59-15.62 ms,
`final/steps*`), since the rows of a workgroup then wait on each other's barriers; with the rule both builds measure alike (`stepsC*`).
gpt-oss-20b 2,048-row prompt step 125.76 → 123.63 ms in the probe, 64-row decode unchanged (13.54 → 13.52 ms: the launch overlaps other
graph branches). Products unchanged (same values per row). (The branch withdrew this while fix/rope-qkv owned the kernel and took it back
after that branch merged; `deferred/` has the diff.)

### 80.4 Matmul epilogues in the skinny GEMM's store

The skinny GEMM (2-16 rows, `gemm_sk`) wrote its product and left the epilogue (a projection's bias, a residual add) to its own launch:
four `fused[Add]` launches per gpt-oss layer at 4 rows. `gemm_sk` now stores `MM_STORE` (mm_epi.slang, the generated epilogue gemm_cm2's
split-K reduction already uses) where the product is dense rows of N and the weights are not on the int-dot path; the separate epilogue
skips those row counts. Same f32 operations in the same order, so the values are identical; Vulkan runs the same Slang kernel.
`SHARPLIGHT_SKINNY_EPILOGUE=0` restores the separate launch. gpt-oss-20b `--text` (`explore/skepi/`): 4 rows 522 → 450 dispatches,
8.95 → 8.93 ms; 8 rows 11.09 → 11.05; 16 rows 546 → 522 dispatches, 12.94 → 12.87 ms (-0.5 %).

### 80.5 Measured and not kept

* **The expert slot sum read in place by the residual Add + RmsNorm** (`rejected/slot_sum_fold.diff`: the group loads the S slot rows of
  the [T, S, N] expert outputs and adds them in the narrow ReduceSum's order, the reduce launch dropped, the Reshape in between followed,
  batches of the int-dot slot-sum matvec lowered on the written sum). No gain where it matters: at 2,008 rows the folded norm took 158.5 µs
  against 107 (reduce) + 48 (norm), since it reads the four f32 slot rows either way; at 64 rows the reduce is 2.8 µs. Its first form
  also computed wrong values on gpt-oss-20b (`rejected/slot_sum_fold_wrong/`: the steps "sped up" to 8.75 ms because the routing collapsed),
  while the new `MoeTests.RoutedExpertSumIntoResidualNorm` (the same block shape, every product path) passed; not debugged further once
  the gain was known to be nil. The test stays as coverage of the unfused path.
* **The full step budget at any load** (`--min-step-tokens 0`; the prompt steps of waves 2 and 3 run 1,800-1,824 rows because 56-57 of 64
  slots are busy when the wave arrives, `explore/sched/`): 64 streams 2932-2947 → 2943-2957 tok/s (+0.4 %, within the rounds' spread),
  16 streams TTFT p50 108-110 → 162-202 ms. The default stays.
* **`rope_qkv` on Vulkan with its norm reduction in uniform control flow** (`rejected/rope_qkv_uniform_norm_reduction.diff`): still 4 of
  101 FusionTests fail on the Vulkan provider, now also NormRopeIntoCache cases without the norm (f16 / D 128, f32 / D 64 rot 32;
  `rejected/rope_qkv_vulkan_uniform_reduction_tests.txt`), so the SPIR-V bug is not the barriers; Vulkan keeps the three launches.


### 80.6 Serving after the round

At 64 streams gpt-oss-20b gains 1.4 % (0.93 → 0.95x), the prompt steps' share of the gap; the decode steps (inter-token p50 13.85-13.88
against vLLM's 13.26-13.37 ms) are unchanged. Qwen3-8B-FP8 gains 0.6 % (0.94x at 64 streams, 0.95x at 16): its 16-stream decode step

(p50 246-285 against 408-477 ms at 64 streams), since our wave of prompts takes the steps before the decode rows go on, vLLM's interleaves.

### 80.7 Correctness and tests

* Greedy text, 120 tokens, the ~40-word prompt and the ~1000-token prompt, `develop` (`7b7f6231`) against this round (`final/greedy/`):

  None of the changes alters arithmetic: the attention blocks compute the same tiles, `rope_qkv` the same rows, the skinny GEMM's
  store applies the epilogue's f32 operations in the order the separate launch did.
* New test `MoeTests.RoutedExpertSumIntoResidualNorm` (an expert sum through a Reshape into the residual Add and RmsNorm, MXFP4 / Q4_K /
  bf16, 1-300 rows): passes on both providers.
* Sharplight.Cuda.Tests: 61 / 0 failed / 1 skipped (cuBLASLt). Sharplight.Vulkan.Tests, one process per class, CUDA and Vulkan providers:

### 80.8 Gap to vLLM and plan (state after this round)

| benchmark | CUDA / vLLM | where the time goes |
|---|---:|---|
| gpt-oss-20b serving 16 / 64 streams | 1.00 / 0.95 | 64: prompt rows ~10 % dearer per row (60.2 against 54.5 µs), decode steps ~4 % (13.85 against 13.3 ms p50) |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 serving 16 / 64 streams | 0.95 / 0.94 | decode steps at 16 rows (13.0 against 12.4 ms p50), prompt rows |
| gpt-oss-20b decode, 64 sequences / 4 x 130K | 0.98-1.01 / 1.00-1.03 (§78) | expert GEMMs (Marlin ~10 % ahead per byte) |

Ranked levers:

1. **Prompt rows of gpt-oss (serving at 64 streams)**, per 2,008-row step: the two expert gathers (4.5 ms; Marlin reads routed rows
   through its sorted ids: let the gate / up GEMM store its output as the down GEMM's sorted f16 rows with a row-range flag and a fixup
   of flagged rows, ~2 ms, and read the gate / up input rows by token from an f16 copy, ~1 ms); the dense f16 projections at 2k rows
   (22 ms against cutlass ~18.5: deeper pipelining / wave quantization of the 128 x 256 tiles); prefill attention for short prompts
   (87 against 32 µs per layer: 64-row tiles or the 8 query heads of a KV head in one block); the f32 residual's add + norm launches.
2. **Decode steps at 16-64 rows**: the expert GEMM's per-byte efficiency against Marlin (§76.4; its 64-row blocking in two launches
   bounded at ~3 % of the expert GEMMs, §75.3); Qwen3's 16-row step (0.6 ms behind vLLM's inter-token p50).
3. **Host time between decode steps** (0.15 ms of 13.8 per replayed 64-row step, 1.1 %): scheduling step N + 1 while step N runs
   (vLLM's asynchronous scheduling; needs the sampled tokens fed back on the device).
4. **`rope_qkv` on Vulkan**: the SPIR-V form is wrong also without the norm (80.5); next suspects the pointer arguments of
   `qkv_rope_head` and the cache index of the multi-sequence form.
5. Small launches of few-row decode steps (§78.7 item 4): after 80.4 the 4-row gpt-oss step has 450 launches; the router chain
   (to_f16, split-K GEMM, reduce: ~10 µs per layer at 64 rows) is the next fold.
