### 81.2 Where the time went at depth

Profile of one Gemma 4 31B decode step after 32K keys (BatchBench `--profile 1`, `ab/g32k_*`): the attention launches took 7.8 ms of
33.3 on CUDA and 10.0 of 34.7 on Vulkan, almost all of it the ten global layers (head size 512, 4 KV heads with 8 query heads each,
268 MB of keys and values per layer at 32K: ~455 GB/s on CUDA). The window layers (head size 256, 16 KV heads, 1024 keys, L2
resident) were ~30 µs each, the split-K combine 0.35 ms per step. The global layers' rows ran the generic `decode` (the hand-written
`attn_decode_native.cu` covered head sizes 64 / 128 only): at head size 512 a lane group of 32 lanes holds 8 heads x 16 query values
and 8 x 16 accumulators (256 registers before the key rows) on CUDA, and on Vulkan's 48 KiB the block takes only 4 of the 8 heads, so
every key row is read twice. The paged ring path of the window layers and the combine were not the gap.

### 81.3 The wide form of the hand-written decode attention (CUDA)

`attn_decode_native.cu` now also serves head sizes 256 and 512 (`D` > 128 selects the wide form): a block of 4 warps shares each
tile instead of each warp streaming its own.

* A tile is 8192 / D keys (32 at 256, 16 at 512): 32 KiB of keys and values, copied with `cp.async` into a ring of three stages of
  dynamic shared memory (rows of 16-byte chunks, XOR swizzle inside each 128-byte group; rows past the range zero-filled; paged
  caches: one block-table read per lane, the row addresses passed by shuffle), so two tiles are in flight while the third is computed.
* S = Q · Kᵀ: warp w computes key fragment w mod NF over a slice of the dimensions (D = 256: each warp 8 keys over all 256; D = 512:
  pairs of warps split the 512 dimensions), query fragments in registers (the block's heads as the MMA rows), K by `ldmatrix`. The
  partial scores go to 1 KiB of shared memory; after a barrier every warp sums them in the same order, so all warps run the same
  online softmax (softcap, mask) and hold the same (m, l). O += P · V: warp w owns D / 4 output dimensions (V by `ldmatrix.trans`), so
  no merge of warp states is needed. Two barriers per tile; partials and the direct output (sinks) as before, same combine.
* 201 registers at 512, 157 at 256, no spills; one block per SM (99 KiB), so the split rule aims for 2 x SMs blocks
  (`NativeWideDecodeWaves`): 4 KV groups x 41 ranges at one row.
* Fallbacks: two stages where the device's shared memory does not take three, the generated `decode` where neither fits, for other
  head sizes, quantized caches and the forms the narrow kernel does not serve; `SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_DECODE_WIDE=0` switches it off.

Harness (`bench/s78_decode`, now also for D > 128; paged f16 cache, 20 launches, min; `harness/sweep1.txt`):

| shape | keys | grid | ms | GB/s | max error vs f32 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Gemma 4 global (32 / 4 heads, D 512), 1 row | 131,072 | 4 x 41 | 1.305 | 823 | 2.2e-6 |
| same, blocks in random order | 131,072 | 4 x 41 | 1.307 | 821 | |
| same, 64 ranges (`decode`'s split rule, 3.1 waves) | 131,072 | 4 x 64 | 1.338 | 803 | |
| same, 2 stages | 131,072 | 4 x 41 | 1.306 | 822 | |
| same | 32,768 | 4 x 41 | 0.334 | 804 | |
| Qwen3.8 27B (24 / 4 heads, D 256), 1 row | 131,072 | 4 x 41 | 0.654 | 821 | 1.3e-6 |
| same, 16 rows | 2,048 | 4 x 16 x 2 | 0.167 | 804 | 6.5e-6 |
| Gemma 4 window layer (32 / 16 heads, D 256) | 1,024 | 16 x 10 | 0.0106 | (L2) | 5.8e-6 |

In the engine the 27B's attention layer at 128K was 868.7 µs with `decode` on CUDA (618 GB/s, §74's profile); the harness gives 654.

### 81.4 The tensor-core decode form on other targets (`fa_mqa` with separate key and value tiles)

`fa_mqa` (attention.slang) is the cooperative-matrix split-K kernel of absorbed latent attention, whose keys and values are one row.
With `FM_SEPV` it takes separate f16 key and value caches of one head size: both tiles are fetched into registers during the previous
tile's products and staged side by side, `FM_BC` keys per tile (32 at 256, 16 at 512, so both fit 48 KiB), the group's heads (up to
16) as the matrix rows, so each key and value row is read once per KV head. Decode rows of head sizes 256 / 512 take it where the
CUDA kernel does not serve (Vulkan, and CUDA with the wide form off), split for 2 x compute units workgroups; rows of long runs in
mixed steps are left to the flash kernel (`MIX_RUN`, new in `fa_mqa`). `SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_TC=0` keeps `decode`,
`SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_TC_CFG=waves,minKeys,maxSplits,keys` sets the split rule and tile.

A/B (BatchBench, GPU ms per step, minimum of 20, same build, switches on / off, one hold each; `ab/`):

| step | CUDA off | **CUDA on** | Vulkan off | **Vulkan on** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Gemma 4 31B, 1 row after 32K keys | 33.29 | **29.74** | 34.68 | **29.31** |
| of which attention (profile, ms per step) | 7.84 | **4.64** | 10.02 | **4.65** |
| Qwen3.8 27B, 1 row after 32K keys | 25.53 | **24.49** | 26.07 | **24.43** |
| of which attention | 3.70 | **2.72** | 4.08 | **2.65** |

Vulkan tile and split variants (Gemma 4 31B at 32K, `ab/g_*.txt`; default 2 waves, 32-key tiles at 256): 1 wave 29.21 ms, 4 waves
29.72, 8 waves 30.22, 16-key tiles at 256 29.19 (Qwen3.8 27B 24.53 against 24.43 with 32), so the defaults stay.

### 81.5 The K split of GEMM grids of one to four waves

Gemma 4 31B's prefill at 512 tokens is 90 % K-quant GEMMs (gemm_cm2 on dequantized tiles, `pp/gemma_p512_cuda.txt`); gate / up ran
at 112 TFLOPS, the [21504 → 5376] down projections at 69-71 (1.72 / 1.66 ms): N = 5376 gives 42 x 4 = 168 tiles of 128 x 128 for 82
SMs, three waves with the third nearly empty. `ChooseSplit` split such grids only when two K halves filled the last wave 15 points
better (168 tiles: 68 → 82 %, so no). It now splits in two when the halves take under 90 % of the time in whole waves (each half wave
costs half a tile's K steps: 168 tiles 3 waves → 5 half waves), for grids of one to four waves; the earlier example (234 tiles of a
192-tile wave) splits under both rules, and grids of many waves are unchanged. `SHARPLIGHT_GEMM_SPLIT_FILL=1` restores the earlier
rule. Gemma 4 31B pp512 (`pp/gemma_pp512_split.txt`, best of 5, two runs of the new rule around the old one): CUDA 1532 → 1649 /
1643 tok/s, Vulkan 1484 → 1606 / 1604. Prefill at 2K+ rows (grids of more than four waves) and Qwen3-8B / Qwen3.8 27B at 512 (grids
of 128 / 160 tiles, two waves, which the rule leaves unsplit) are unchanged.

### 81.7 Measured and not kept

* 64 ranges for the wide CUDA form (`decode`'s split rule: 256 blocks, 3.1 waves of one block per SM): 1.338 against 1.305 ms at
  128K keys; 1 / 3 waves are as fast as 2 at one row (1.305-1.307).
* Two ring stages: as fast as three in the harness (1.306 ms); three stay where they fit.
* Vulkan: 16-key tiles at head size 256, 1 / 4 / 8 waves (81.4).

### 81.8 Leads worth promoting and the next levers

Promotable (like for like, same hold, both engines interleaved):

* **Long-context decode on Vulkan against llama.cpp's Vulkan backend**: Qwen3.8 27B at 128K 1.14x (from 0.96x), at 32K 1.12x;
  Gemma 4 31B at 32K 1.14x (from 0.92x); Gemma 4 31B at 128K 1.06x (CUDA 1.02x, from 0.80x).
* Gemma 4 31B on Vulkan: prefill 512 1.19x, batched decode at 16 sequences 2.06x.

Parity, not a lead: CUDA decode at depth (Qwen3.8 27B 1.04-1.05x, Gemma 4 31B 1.01x at 32K, 1.02x at 128K, from 0.80x), Gemma 4 31B prefill 512 and
single-stream decode on CUDA (0.99 / 1.01x).

Next levers:

1. **Vulkan K-quant decode GEMM at 49-64 rows** (§79.7 item 3; not started this round): a hand-written cooperative-matrix kernel that
   decodes the raw Q4_K / Q6_K blocks in registers, like CUDA's `gemm_kq_native.cu`.
2. **The decode attention at 820 GB/s** is at ~92 % of the card's bandwidth; past it, the f16 cache's bytes: a q8_0 cache on the wide
   forms (half the bytes; today quantized caches fall back to `decode` at head sizes 256 / 512).
3. **Batched decode at depth** with the wide forms: one block per (KV group, row) keeps the 16 rows of a step apart; grouping the rows
   of one sequence (speculative / multi-token steps) into the MMA rows would read each key once per step.
4. **Gemma 4 31B's 128K prefill on Vulkan**: 513 tok/s against 884 on CUDA (both the session path, one timed prefill); the
   head-size-512 global layers' prefill attention on `fe` with split head dimensions (§74), confined to head sizes 256 / 512.
5. Gemma 4 31B's ~180 RMS norms per decode step (2.7 µs each, ~0.5 ms of 25.6): the q / k / v norms beside the rope / cache writes.

### 82.2 What changed

§80.8 ranked the prompt rows of gpt-oss at 64 streams first: per 2,008-row step the two expert gathers (4.5 ms), the dense f16
projections, short-prompt attention. In order of the commits (gpt-oss-20b, BatchBench `--mixed`, GPU ms of the 2,048-row prompt step):

* **Prompt-sized q / k / v as one launch** (`gemm_f16_native.cu` `MULTI` on the 128-row tiles; from 256 rows, 1,024 with biases;
  `SHARPLIGHT_MULTI_GEMM_TALL=0`): q / k / v 378 + 2 x 51.4 → 406 µs per layer (k and v alone leave most SMs idle).
* **Narrow f16 products on gemm_cm2's K split** (`LibraryGemmMinColumns` 256): gpt-oss's router [2880 → 32] ran the hand-written
  GEMM's 128-row token tiles in one column tile, 16 blocks at 2,048 rows; on the K split 39.6 → 16.9 + 3.9 µs (with the reduction,
  which adds the bias). Same kernel as Vulkan's router (see 82.4 for what that does to long-prompt logits).
* **The gate / up GEMM stores the down projection's input** (`NM_Y16`, `SHARPLIGHT_MOE_SORTED_STORE=0` keeps the f32 store): the dual
  form writes the epilogue's values as f16 rows at their expert-sorted position (the layout of `moe_gather_x16`), so the down
  projection's gather launch and the f32 round trip (2,008 x 4 x 2,880 x 4 bytes written and read again) go. On row-ranged copies a
  value ≥ 2^15 is stored as an f16 infinity, its f32 value spilled to the f32 output, the row's scale word set to 1; `moe_range_fixup`
  stores flagged rows scaled (as the ranged gather would) and clears every other row's word. A/B in one hold, same build
  (`final2/store_ab/`): 2,048-row step 119.14 → 115.04 ms (-3.4 %), 64-row decode 16.89 / 16.89 → 16.71 / 16.74 ms (-1.0 %), 16 rows
  12.80 / 12.80 → 12.77 / 12.74 ms (-0.3 %); logits bit-identical to the gather path (963- and 2,889-token prompts).
* **Token-row reads** (`NM_X_TOKEN`, `SHARPLIGHT_MOE_TOKEN_ROWS=0`): the gate / up GEMM reads its items' rows from the router's f16
  copy of x (per token) under that copy's write condition instead of a gathered copy per (token, slot). Store and token rows together: 121.71 →
  117.68 ms in the probe.
* **Row-range unscale in the f16 GEMM's store** (`H_XRS` without a bias): no `f16_range_unscale` launch after the plain f16
  projections; 117.68 → 116.48 ms with the token-row condition fix.
* **Prefill attention head groups for multi-sequence runs** (`FN_HG`: the 8 query heads of a KV head in one block, each K / V tile
  feeding all of them; `SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_HG=1` / `=0` everywhere / nowhere; single-sequence prefill keeps one head per block): 8
  prompts of 256 rows 72.3 → 69.2 µs per layer, 8 + 8 x 250 rows 114.73 / 114.99 → 114.49 / 114.57 ms (`explore/attn_hg/`).

### 82.3 The fix-up anomaly (resolved: a timing artifact)

The 64-row decode profile of the round (`final/prof/steps_gptoss64_new.txt`) showed `moe_range_fixup` at 73.3 ms over 480 calls
(152 µs mean, 2.7 µs min), 19 % of the profiled GPU time, which would mean many flagged rows or a fix-up far costlier than intended.
Neither:

* **No row is ever flagged on gpt-oss.** `moe_range_fixup` instrumented with a printf of flagged rows and rows whose maximum is
  ≥ 2^15 per workgroup (not committed, `final2/fixup_probe/flag_counts.txt`): 6,576 calls on `--text` decode at 16 / 64 rows (and the
  256-row prompts of the depth), 14,592 on prompt steps (8 x 256, 8 + 8 x 250 rows): 0 flagged, 0 large. gpt-oss's clamped SwiGLU
  ((up + 1) · gate · σ(1.702 gate), gate ≤ 7, |up| ≤ 7) bounds the down projection's inputs at ~56, so for this model the flag path
  is never taken and bf16 or per-row scales would buy nothing.
* **The fix-up costs 2-4 µs.** The same profile re-run (`final2/fixup_probe/prof64_rerun.txt`): 1.97 ms over 480 calls (4.1 µs mean,
  2.3 µs min); total profiled GPU time 309.8 ms against 388.5 in the round's profile, 71 of the 79 ms difference the fix-up's. The
  profiler times each launch between its own pair of events on an idle stream, so a host-side stall between the start event and the
  launch counts as the launch's time; the round's profile most likely caught such stalls (or another context on the shared GPU) on
  this launch. Its min (2.7 µs) was the real cost all along.
* **A/B** (82.2): the store with its fix-up is faster than the gather at every size measured.

Coverage: `MoeTests.RoutedExpertBlockLargeActivations` (separate gate / up products) never reaches the hand-written grouped GEMM, so
it tested the ranged gather only. New `CudaCodeTests.NativeMoeSortedStoreScalesLargeRows`: two gpt-oss-style blocks (fused gate / up
halves, MXFP4) on one routing, every seventh token 300 times larger so the first block's products pass 2^15, the second block reading
its RmsNorm; 50 tokens (one fix-up workgroup) and 300 (five), both outputs against the CPU provider. It fails with a fix-up that keeps
the previous block's scale words (y2[0] -37.3 against -0.68) and passes with the real one.

| benchmark | CUDA / vLLM | where the time goes |
|---|---:|---|
| gpt-oss-20b serving 16 / 64 streams | 1.00 / 0.98 | 64: decode steps (inter-token p50 13.5-13.6 against 13.0-13.4 ms); prompt rows now 56.7 µs per row (116.1 ms per 2,048) against vLLM's 54.5 |

Ranked levers:

1. **Qwen3-8B-FP8 decode at 16 rows** (0.6 ms per step behind vLLM; untouched since §80) and its prompt rows (FP8 projections at
   2k rows).
2. **gpt-oss decode steps at 64 rows**: the expert GEMMs' per-byte efficiency against Marlin (§76.4); the router chain (to_f16,
   split-K GEMM, reduce) and the slot sum at decode sizes.
3. **gpt-oss prompt rows**: the dense f16 projections at 2k rows (cutlass ~18.5 ms against ~21.5 per step), the f32 residual's add +
   norm launches, the slot sum (2.7 against vLLM's 1.2 ms).
4. **Host time between decode steps** (§80.8 item 3): asynchronous scheduling.
5. The sorted store's flag path never runs on gpt-oss (clamped SwiGLU). A model on this GEMM whose expert activations often pass
   2^15 would pay for the fix-up's serial loop over flagged rows (one workgroup per 256 rows): measure its flag counts first.

### 83.2 A cooperative-matrix K-quant decode GEMM for Vulkan (`gemm_kq.slang`)

At 9-64 rows the K-quant projections ran gemm_cm2 on Vulkan (split-K, weights dequantized to f16 at fetch and staged as f16 tiles)
and the skinny GEMM up to 16 rows; CUDA has had the hand-written `gemm_kq_native.cu` since §77. Qwen3-8B on Vulkan, profile of one
step (BatchBench `--profile`, `base_prof*.txt`): at 64 sequences gate / up [4096 → 12288] Q4_K 108 µs per launch (two launches and the
SiLU product), Q6_K down [12288 → 4096] 134.5 µs, o [4096 → 4096] 36.2 µs, the vocabulary head 1315 µs; at 32 sequences 88.6 / 114.0 /
27.9 / 913 µs.

`gemm_kq.slang` is the counterpart of the CUDA kernel in Slang, for targets without CUDA C++ whose 16x16 f16 fragments have the MMA
element layout (`DeviceFeatures.MatrixMmaLayout`; the kernel verifies it once and stores NaN where it differs):

* A workgroup covers 16 / 32 / 48 / 64 token rows (by batch) and 64 weight rows with 8 subgroups: subgroup s owns the 16 weight rows
  of fragment s % 4 and K half s / 4 of every 256-value superblock, so each weight value is dequantized once and each staged activation
  is read by four subgroups; the halves' accumulators are summed through shared memory at the end.
* A K step is one superblock: its activation rows (16-byte chunks XOR-swizzled by row parity) and the raw Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K blocks of
  the 64 rows (each row's 16-byte-aligned window; Q6_K's 210-byte blocks start at any even byte and are read with a funnel shift) are
  staged from registers loaded during the previous step's products (no asynchronous copies on Vulkan), within the 48 KiB of a workgroup.
* Fragments are filled from registers: lane (g, c) takes the 8 values 8c .. 8c + 7 of each 32-value quarter of its K half, the same
  permutation for A and B (a dot product does not see the K order), so one 16-byte activation read per row and one 8-byte read of the
  codes (Q4_K / Q5_K: one nibble plane; Q6_K: 8 low-nibble and 8 high-bit bytes) serve two MMAs; each code becomes an exact f16
  integer (0x6400 bias) scaled with one f16 FMA by the sub-block scale and minimum, gemm_cm2's arithmetic.
* Single projections with a bias row and the row scales of a row-ranged f16 copy, the q / k / v multi-output form, and the dual gate /
  up form (even tile rows the gate's, odd the up's; the store applies the elementwise group as `epi2`) like the CUDA kernel; K splits
  reduce in the last workgroup of a tile in slice order (deterministic, counters self-resetting). Split rule: the CUDA one, counting two
  slots per compute unit for 16-row tiles (two workgroups fit an SM: 115 registers, 18 KiB) and one for the larger tiles.

The lowering uses it wherever the CUDA kernel serves on CUDA (`UsesNativeKQuantDecode`), so 9-16 row batches leave the skinny GEMM and
9-64 row batches gemm_cm2; `SHARPLIGHT_COOP_KQ=0` keeps them, and devices without the MMA layout (or with less shared memory than a
64-row tile's 47 KiB) keep them anyway.

Kernel times (Vulkan.Tests `BenchTests.MatMulPrefill` with `SHARPLIGHT_BENCH_COPIES=8`: eight weight copies per launch set so the
weights stream from memory, sum of the per-dispatch minimum times / 8, µs; gemm_cm2 from the step profiles above, CUDA's
`gemm_kq_native.cu` from §77 / §79; `kernel/`):

| shape | rows | **gemm_kq** | gemm_cm2 (Vulkan, before) | gemm_kq_native (CUDA) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Q4_K [4096 → 12288] gate / up pair (dual form) | 16 | **86** | (skinny GEMM, two launches) | |
| | 32 | **127-131** | 2 x 88.6 + SiLU · up | 98.9 |
| | 64 | **191** | 2 x 108.1 + SiLU · up | |
| Q4_K [4096 → 12288] | 16 / 32 / 64 | **49 / 75 / 112** | – / 88.6 / 108.1 | 43.8 / 52.4 / 82.1 |
| Q6_K [12288 → 4096] | 16 / 32 / 64 | **61 / 79 / 112** | – / 114.0 / 134.5 | 58.8 / 60.4 / 89.7 |
| Q4_K [12288 → 4096] | 16 / 32 / 64 | **49 / 75 / 110** | – / 79.1 / 111.9 | |
| Q4_K [4096 → 4096] | 16 / 32 / 64 | **20 / 28 / 39** | – / 27.9 / 36.2 | 14.1 / 17.8 / 27.3 |

1024): 9 sequences 11.51 → **8.83**, 16: 13.20 → **9.39**, 24: 15.09 → **13.09**, 32: 16.32 → **14.19**, 40: 18.59 → **16.77**, 48:

### 83.3 Where the 32- and 64-row tiles lose against CUDA

At 32 rows gemm_kq takes 75 µs on Q4_K [4096 → 12288] against 52.4 for CUDA's kernel, which copies with `cp.async` into a ring of
2-3 stages. Harness-only variants (`SHARPLIGHT_COOP_KQ_MACROS`, results wrong by construction; µs at 32 / 64 rows; `kernel/kexp*.txt`):

| variant | 32 rows | 64 rows |
|---|---:|---:|
| kernel | 75-77 | 112-114 |
| no copies after the first superblock (`KQ_X_NOCOPY`: no loads, no stores, no barriers) | 35 | 64 |
| barriers kept, no loads and no stores (`KQ_X_NOSTAGE`) | 36 | 65 |
| activations loaded once, weights each step (`KQ_X_NOXCOPY`) | 76 | 99 |
| weights loaded once, activations each step (`KQ_X_NOWCOPY`) | 63 | 98 |
| loads each step, no shared stores (their words XOR-ed into a register, `KQ_X_NOSTS`) | 69 | 102 |
| the same, loads two steps ahead (`KQ_PF=2`) | 63 | 92 |
| MMAs only (no copies, constant fragments) | 24 | 47 |
| loads two steps ahead (`KQ_PF=2`), loads before the second barrier (`KQ_X_EARLY`) | 77 / 77 | 114 / 112 |
| execution-only barriers (`KQ_X_BAR=1`), release / acquire around them (`KQ_X_BAR=2`) | 77 / 75 | 110 / 114 |
| 4 subgroups per workgroup, each over both K halves (`KQ_KH=1`) | 73 | 108 |
| 128 weight rows per workgroup, activations staged per half superblock (`KQ_NT=2`) | 78 | 112 |

The products and dequantization take about half the time (35 / 64 µs); barriers are cheap (36 / 65 with them), and the rest is the
register-staged loads, whose latency the deeper register prefetch and the earlier issue barely hide (one 64-row workgroup per SM at
205 registers, 146 at 32 rows: one workgroup of 8 warps per SM in both cases). Without an asynchronous copy to shared memory in Vulkan, the
lever is more independent workgroups per SM (16-row tiles: two, 115 registers) or fewer bytes per step (int8 activations).

### 83.4 Gemma 4 31B's long prefill on Vulkan: 64-query blocks for head size 512

On Vulkan the prefill attention of the ten global layers (head size 512, 32 query / 4 KV heads) is `fe` with the register softmax and
split head dimensions (`FE_DS` = 2, §74): 16-key K / V tiles (33 KiB with the padded rows) and, since the staged Q rows had to fit
the same 48 KiB, 32-query blocks of 4 subgroups. Each 16-key tile was therefore read from L2 for 32 queries only. Q is now staged in two
passes of 32 rows (`FE_QPASS`; each pass's subgroups load their fragments before the next pass overwrites the rows), so a block holds
64 queries in 8 subgroups and shares each tile between twice the queries; shared memory 33 KiB of K / V plus 8 KiB of score exchange.
Only head sizes above 256 change (`FeBlockRows`); `SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_FE_WIDE_ROWS=32` restores the old blocks.

Prefill of Gemma 4 31B Q4_K_M on Vulkan at 16K (CLI `--bench 16384`, two runs each, one hold, `ab/gemma_16k_fe_rows.txt`): 1288-1292 tok/s
with 32-query blocks, **1419-1435** with 64; at 128K 513 → **705** tok/s (83.1). Greedy text of the 5,200-token prompt is identical with
both block sizes (83.7).

### 83.5 q8_0 caches on the wide decode forms

The tensor-core decode forms of §81 took f16 caches only; q8_0 caches (`--kv-type q8_0`, half the bytes per key) fell back to the
generic `decode` at head sizes 256 / 512.

* CUDA (`attn_decode_native.cu`, `ND_KVQ8`): the ring holds the tiles' raw q8_0 rows (a row of D values is D / 32 blocks of 34 bytes,
  16-byte aligned at 256 / 512: 17 / 34 chunks), copied with `cp.async` like the f16 rows; after the barrier that makes tile i visible
  the block converts it into one f16 tile in the swizzled layout (d · q rounded to f16), behind a third barrier, and the products are
  those of the f16 form. Shared memory 3 x 17 KiB of raw stages + 32 KiB + the scores (85 KiB).
* Vulkan (`fa_mqa` with `FM_SEPV`): the quantized fetch of the latent-attention form (whole 34-byte blocks read as the words covering
  them) now also stages the value tile.

`SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_DECODE_Q8=0` keeps `decode` on CUDA; Vulkan's form follows `SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_DECODE_TC`.

Decode steps over q8_0 caches (GPU ms, wide form on / `decode`, same hold, `ab/q8_wide_decode_and_nt2.txt` and `final/`): Qwen3.8 27B at
32K CUDA 26.09 → **23.44**, Vulkan 25.90 → **23.65** (f16 caches: 24.49 / 24.43, §81); Gemma 4 31B at 8K CUDA 29.81 → **27.03**, Vulkan
27.96 → **26.34**. Tests: `StatefulTests.CachedAttentionWideDecode` has q8_0 cases at head sizes 256 and 512 (windows, soft caps, sinks,
rows of several ranges and batches), against the CPU, on both providers.

### 83.6 A row norm, an elementwise group and a row norm in one launch

Gemma 4's layers run their post-attention norm, the residual add and the pre-feed-forward norm (and the post-feed-forward norm, the
residual add with the layer scale and the next layer's input norm) as a standalone RmsNorm and a `fused[Add]+RmsNorm`: 180 standalone
norms per decode step at 2.8 µs. A norm whose output only feeds an elementwise group that already ends in a row norm is now folded
into it (`FoldNormHeads` takes groups with a tail norm; `RowNormKernelSource` reduces the head norm's input in a first pass, and both
later passes form its value `nrmh` before the group's statements), so the pair is one launch: 120 launches less per Gemma step.
`SHARPLIGHT_NORM_HEAD_TAIL=0` keeps the separate launch. Gemma 4 31B decode, GPU ms per step (`ab/gemma_norm_head_tail.txt`): 1
sequence CUDA 25.58 → **25.48**, Vulkan 25.26 → **25.00**; 16 sequences Vulkan 39.57 → **39.31**, CUDA 36.06 → 35.97. Test:
`FusionTests.NormThenResidualAddThenNorm` (rows in registers and reloaded rows, with and without a head weight) against the CPU.

### 83.7 Correctness

* Greedy text (`--chat --temp 0 -n 64`; the 40-44-token prompt of §81 for the three models, whose prefill pass runs gemm_kq at 40-44
  rows on Vulkan, and the 5,200-token prompt for Gemma 4 31B, whose global layers' prefill runs the 64-query `fe` on Vulkan): with
  and without this round's paths (`SHARPLIGHT_COOP_KQ=0 SHARPLIGHT_ATTN_FE_WIDE_ROWS=32 SHARPLIGHT_NATIVE_DECODE_Q8=0
  SHARPLIGHT_NORM_HEAD_TAIL=0`) byte-identical for Gemma 4 31B (both prompts) and Qwen3.8 27B on both providers and Qwen3-8B on CUDA, and
  identical between the providers. Qwen3-8B on Vulkan changes after 31 tokens ("I remember that sunlight ..." against "I remember
  that shorter ..."): a near tie, " sunlight" 34.288 against " shorter" 34.149 on Vulkan and 34.287 / 34.174 on CUDA (`--logits` on
  the prefix, either path, `text/qwen3_8b_near_tie_logits.txt`).
* Tests: new `KQuantDecodeGemmTests` (Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K at 9-64 rows, K = 1280 with Q6_K blocks at any even byte, partial weight
  tiles, bias rows, q / k / v, wide matrices with and without K splits, the dual form with SiLU and GELU-tanh against the CPU, and
  against gemm_cm2 within 1e-3 of the output scale), on Vulkan (the new kernel) and CUDA (the CUDA C++ one).
* Suites (final build, one process per class, `suites.txt`): Vulkan.Tests MatMul 164, SkinnyGemm 42, RowInvariance 77, Mmq 48,
  QuantFormat 197, DualGemm 13, MatMulEpilogue 16, FullAttention 30, PagedAttention 10, Stateful 78, CompressedKv 12,
  KQuantDecodeGemm 30, Fusion 105 on Vulkan and on CUDA, all passing; Sharplight.Cuda.Tests 63 (1 skipped, the cuBLASLt probe);
  Families `SessionWindowKvTests` 6 passing; FamilyGenerationTests `gemma-4` 12 (9 skipped) passing, `qwen3` 63 (30 skipped) with the
  three CPU cases of the Qwen3.5-122B truncated checkpoints failing with `InsufficientMemoryException` (host memory, as in §77 / §81).

### 83.8 Measured and not kept

* Register prefetch two superblocks ahead (`KQ_PF=2`), loads issued before the second barrier, execution-only or split
  release / acquire barriers, 4-subgroup workgroups (`KQ_KH=1`), 128-row weight tiles with half-superblock activation stages
  (`KQ_NT=2`): within ±4 % of the kernel (83.3); the options stay in the kernel for the harness, defaults off.
* 32-row token tiles for 48-64 rows (two tiles, each reading the weights): 125-149 against 94-114 µs; K splits in two of 32-64-row
  grids: 77-100 against 75-110 µs (only 16-row tiles, two per SM, gain: Q6_K [12288 → 4096] 71 → 61 µs, now the rule's choice).

### 83.9 Leads worth promoting and the next levers

Promotable (like for like, same hold, both engines interleaved):

* **Batched decode on Vulkan against llama.cpp's Vulkan backend**: Qwen3-8B 2.93 / 2.30 / 2.02 / 1.79x at 16 / 32 / 48 / 64 sequences
  (from 2.09 / 1.95 / 1.80 / 1.67x), Qwen3.8 27B 3.45 / 2.92 / 2.78 / 2.62x (from 2.49-2.59x). Gemma 4 31B at 16 sequences 2.65x (from 2.07x).
* **q8_0 KV caches at depth**: Qwen3.8 27B at 32K 1.39x of llama.cpp on CUDA, 1.15x on Vulkan; Gemma 4 31B at 8K 1.06 / 1.14x.

Not a lead: Gemma 4 31B's 128K prefill on Vulkan (705 tok/s, 0.80x of our CUDA path; llama.cpp's 128K prefill was not measured).

Next levers:

1. **gemm_kq at 32-64 rows** (75 / 112 µs against CUDA's 52 / 82): half its time is the register-staged copies (83.3). Int8 MMAs on
   q8_1 activations (`MatrixInt8`, half the activation bytes per step and twice the products per instruction) or a producer /
   consumer split of the subgroups.
2. **Gemma 4 31B's 128K prefill on Vulkan** (0.80x of CUDA): `fe` at head size 512 still uses 16-key tiles; the next step is fewer
   bytes per tile (f16 K / V shared with a narrower padding, or the K tile reused for the score exchange) to fit 32 keys.
3. **q8_0 prefill attention at head size 512** (the per-(head, query) kernel; Gemma's 32K q8_0 prompts take minutes): `fe` and the
   hand-written CUDA prefill kernel take f16 caches only.
4. Gemma's 60 remaining standalone norms per step (v norm): into the rope / cache-write launch.

## 84. LLM round 29: Qwen3-8B-FP8 decode at 16 rows (the dual gate / up pair on the FP8 GEMM's decode form, a register-streaming FP8 decode GEMM, weight copies before the dependency wait); vLLM's FP8 prompt GEMMs twice as fast per row (2026-11-22)

Branch `perf/llm-r29` (`develop` at `8246ce2e`, nothing newer to merge). GPU 0 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell 32 GB, 82 SMs,
200 W cap), shared with perf/feed-r5: every run held the verify lock; ours, `develop` and vLLM 0.33 (venv `vllm-r12`) ran in the same
hold. §83 is perf/feed-r5's. Every change is CUDA only (NVRTC kernels and their lowering); Vulkan's kernels and lowering are unchanged.
Raw output in [`bench/results/s84/`](../bench/results/s84) (`final/` the final hold, `explore/` the A/B holds, `harness/` the kernel
harness, `correct/` greedy text and logits, `tests.txt`).

### 84.1 Results (final hold)

Serving (`bench/s16_serve.sh`, 16 / 64 slots of 512 tokens, ~250-token random-word prompts, 128 output tokens, closed loop, two rounds
each, tok/s per round; ours `--provider cuda`, vLLM `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`), all in one hold (`final/serve/`):

| model, streams | `develop` 8246ce2e | **this round** | vLLM 0.33 | ours / vLLM before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B-FP8, 16 | 1049 / 1052 | **1090 / 1094** | 1121 / 1121 | 0.94 → **0.97-0.98** |
| the same: TTFT p50 / inter-token latency mean, p50 (ms) | 115-117 / 14.23, 13.04 | 114-116 / 13.65-13.68, 12.45 | 160-161 / 12.88, 12.37 | |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8, 64 | 2532 / 2533 | 2540 / 2536 | 2696 / 2691 | 0.94 → 0.94 |
| the same: TTFT p50 / ITL mean, p50 | 285-287 / 21.95, 16.33-16.37 | 283-286 / 21.91, 16.29-16.31 | 405 / 20.20, 15.99-16.02 | |
| gpt-oss-20b, 16 | 1405 / 1412 | 1404 / 1414 | 1413 / 1394 | 1.00 → 1.00 |
| gpt-oss-20b, 64 | 3042 / 3067 | 3042 / 3070 | 3130 / 3182 | 0.97 → 0.97 |

At 16 streams Qwen3-8B-FP8's inter-token p50 drops 13.04 → 12.45 ms (vLLM 12.37), +4 %. At 64 streams the decode steps are
unchanged (64 rows take none of the changed paths) and the prompt rows are the gap (84.4). gpt-oss-20b has no FP8 weights and is
unchanged (its 64-stream ratio, 0.97, is vLLM's faster round in this hold; §82 measured 0.98).

Steps (BatchBench `--slots 64 --ctx 640 --depth 256 --modes greedy --reps 10 --text`, GPU ms min, this round and `develop` alternated
twice, `final/steps1`, `steps2`):

| step | `develop` | **this round** | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 decode 1 / 16 / 64 rows | 10.94-10.96 / 12.59-12.61 / 15.46-15.53 | 10.94 / **12.18-12.20** / 15.52-15.56 | 0 / **-3.3 %** / 0 |
| gpt-oss-20b decode 1 / 16 / 64 rows | 5.19-5.20 / 12.17-12.20 / 16.98-17.06 | 5.19 / 12.10-12.16 / 16.86-17.07 | unchanged (no FP8 weights) |

Like for like against vLLM's decode profile (`s54_vllm_decode_profile.py --words --skip 5`, `final/vllm_qwen_decode*.txt`; its
`execute_context` excludes the LM head, 1.52-1.55 ms, and sampling, as in §76): 16 sequences 10.82 + ~1.6 = ~12.4 ms against our
12.18-12.20 ms; 64 sequences 14.21 + ~1.6 = ~15.8 against 15.52-15.56. So the GPU step is now at or below vLLM's at both sizes; the
serving gap at 64 streams is the prompt rows (84.4).

### 84.2 What changed

* **The dual gate / up pair from 9 rows on the FP8 GEMM's decode form** (`SkinnyMaxRowsFor`, `UsesNativeFp8Decode`): grouped E4M3
  weights left 9-16 rows to `gemm_fp8_native.cu`'s 32-row token tiles for single matmuls but kept the dual pair on the skinny GEMM
  (`gemm_sk`, 139 µs per layer at 16 rows). The skinny GEMM now stops at 8 rows for these weights, as it does for K-quants on their
  hand-written decode GEMM (§77): gate / up 139.1 → 131.1 µs per layer, the norm's separate E4M3 quantization launch gone; 16-sequence
  step 12.58 → 12.31 ms (`explore/h3`, `h5`). `SHARPLIGHT_SKINNY_MAX_ROWS=16` restores the old split.
* **`gemm_fp8_decode.cu`**, a register-streaming FP8 GEMM for 9-16 rows of single matmuls: no shared-memory stages and no block
  barrier in the main loop; every lane loads 16 bytes of weight rows g and g + 8 of each of its fragments and of token g straight into
  registers, with the same permutation of K inside each 64-value chunk for weights and activations, so the words fill m16n8k32 fragments
  with the weights as the A operand (16 rows) and the tokens as B (8 per fragment). The K range is split over 1-8 warps of a block
  (the fewest divisors of the K blocks giving ~512 warps) and added through shared memory in a fixed order. Harness (`harness/`, read
  flush, T = 16): down [12288 → 4096] 67.6 µs (768 GB/s), gate / up dual 133.1 µs (780 GB/s); a plain 16-byte read of 100 MB reaches
  813 GB/s on this card, 50 MB 806, 17 MB 725. In the model: down 69.8 → 67.4 µs, o 24.3 → 24.3 µs, 16-sequence step 12.31-12.32 →
  12.19 ms (`explore/h7`). The dual pair is slower on it (141.8 against 131.5 µs: 192 blocks of 4 warps, one row fragment of each matrix
  per warp) and stays on `gemm_fp8_native.cu`. `SHARPLIGHT_FP8_DECODE_KERNEL=0` / `=1`: off / dual pairs too.
* **Weight copies before `griddepcontrol.wait`.** A programmatic dependent (§58.3: one-wave kernels after one-wave kernels) waited
  at its entry before its first copy. The FP8 decode kernels now issue the first stages' weight copies (`gemm_fp8_native.cu`: the code
  copies of the first two stages, which join the first stage's commit group; `gemm_fp8_decode.cu`: the first K block's registers)
  before the wait, and only the activations and scales after it. The translator injects only `launch_dependents` into a kernel that
  issues the wait itself. Harness with a 5 µs predecessor (`harness/h4.log`): the dependent launch saves 2-4 µs per GEMM; in the
  model the step is unchanged within noise (12.31 against 12.32 ms with the skinny split restored, `explore/h5`), since most of the
  launches before the decode GEMMs are the norms and quantizations of a few µs.

### 84.3 Measured and not kept

* **L2 prefetch of the next K blocks before the wait** (`cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2`, `SHARPLIGHT_FP8_L2_PREFETCH=n`, kept as a switch,
  default off): 4 blocks 12.48, 16 blocks 12.82 against 12.32 ms at 16 rows; with the decode kernel 8 blocks 12.51 against 12.55.
  The prefetches compete with the stream itself.
* **The dual pair on `gemm_fp8_decode.cu`** (above): 12.55-12.58 against 12.30-12.33 ms.
* **Deeper register pipelines in `gemm_fp8_decode.cu`** (2-3 K blocks in flight): equal or slower in the harness (gate / up 135.2 /
  145.4 against 135.2 µs), more registers, fewer resident warps; one block in flight with ~12 warps per SM covers the latency.

### 84.4 Qwen3-8B-FP8 prompt rows against vLLM: its FP8 GEMMs run at twice our rate

vLLM's prefill of 7 prompts of 256 random tokens (`s54_vllm_decode_profile.py --prefill 256 --seqs 8`, `final/vllm_qwen_prefill_8x256.txt`)
takes 98.2 ms for 1,792 rows (54.8 µs per row, LM head apart); ours (BatchBench `--batch 2048 --mixed 0+256x8 --profile 0`,
`final/prefill/`) 138.4 ms for 2,048 rows (67.6 µs per row, 23 % more). Per layer (µs; vLLM scaled to 2,048 rows in brackets):

| launch | ours, 2,048 rows | vLLM, 1,792 rows [2,048] |
|---|---:|---:|
| gate / up (ours dual with SiLU · mul; vLLM GEMM, then a fused mul + quant) | 1,608.7 | 662.2 + 68.7 [833] |
| down | 823.0 | 353.4 [404] |
| q / k / v (ours q 261.4 + k, v 2 x 76.3; vLLM one GEMM) | 414.0 | 184.3 [211] |
| o | 261.4 | 113.3 [129] |
| norms + quantization | 2 x 98.9 + 130.2 + 23.0 | 26.8 + 14.4 + 10.8 [59] |
| rope + cache | 118.8 | 12.6 + 4.3 + 10.6 [31] |
| attention | 82.0 | 43.4 [50] |

DeepGEMM's sm120 kernels (`sm120_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d`, "DeepGEMM E8M0 enabled") run the gate / up product at 2 x 1,792 x 4,096 x 24,576 /
662 µs = 545 TFLOPS, above the 474 TFLOPS `mma.sync` E4M3 peak of this GPU (cuda.md): they use the block-scaled MMA (`kind::mxf8f6f4`
with UE8M0 scales applied in the tensor core), whose throughput the f32-accumulate `mma.sync` with per-block promotion in registers
cannot reach; ours runs 256 TFLOPS (`gemm_fp8_tma.cu`). The scales are then powers of two: vLLM rounds the checkpoint's f32 block
scales to E8M0 (a numerics change). The planned fusion of the down input's E4M3 quantization into the gate / up store (130 µs + the f32
round trip per layer, ~3 % of the step) is small next to this; not done this round.

### 84.5 Correctness and tests

* **Greedy text**, 120 tokens, the ~40-word prompt and the 963-token prompt, this round against `develop` (`correct/`): gpt-oss-20b and
  Qwen3-8B-FP8 byte-identical on CUDA and Vulkan, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M byte-identical on CUDA. Single-sequence decode runs 1 row
  and its prompts more than 64, so these runs take none of the changed row counts.
* **Logits** of the last token of a ~2,900-token prompt (`--logits`, CUDA): Qwen3-8B-FP8 and gpt-oss-20b bit-identical to `develop`.
* The changed paths (9-16 rows) sum their K blocks in another order than the skinny GEMM (dual pair) and the 32-row tiles (single
  matmuls); new `Fp8GemmTests.DecodeRowsGroupedWeights` (9-40 rows, N 256-1024, K 512-3072: the decode kernel's K splits 2-8, the
  32-row tiles) and `DualDecodeRowsGroupedWeights` (4-24 rows) check them against the CPU on both providers.
* **Suites** (`tests.txt`): Sharplight.Vulkan.Tests, one process per class, CUDA and Vulkan providers: Fp8Gemm 41, SkinnyGemm 42,
  DualGemm 13, MatMul 164, MatMulEpilogue 16, Moe 129, Fusion 101, NormHalfCopy 23, Norm 10, RowInvariance 77: **616 / 0 failed on each
  provider**; Sharplight.Cuda.Tests 63 / 0 failed / 1 skipped (cuBLASLt); Sharplight.Serving.Tests 396 / 0 failed / 13 skipped.

### 84.5a After merging `develop` (`bc59e105`, perf/feed-r5 with its norm + add + norm launch)

The final hold ran before perf/feed-r5 merged; the branch was then merged with `develop` and checked against a `develop` build in one
hold (`merged/`): Qwen3-8B-FP8 1 / 16 / 64 rows 10.94-10.95 / **12.20** / 15.50-15.53 against 10.94-10.95 / 12.58-12.59 / 15.45-15.46 ms,
gpt-oss-20b 5.20 / 12.12 / 16.85 against 5.18 / 12.11 / 16.87; greedy text of gpt-oss-20b and Qwen3-8B-FP8 (both prompts, CUDA and
Vulkan) byte-identical to `develop`'s; Fp8Gemm 41, DualGemm 13, SkinnyGemm 42, Fusion 105, NormHalfCopy 23, Norm 10, MatMul 164 pass on
both providers. The fused norms do not change which E4M3 rows the decode GEMMs read.

### 84.6 Gap to vLLM and next levers

| benchmark | CUDA / vLLM | where the time goes |
|---|---:|---|
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 serving 16 / 64 streams | 0.97-0.98 / 0.94 | 64: prompt rows (67.6 against 54.8 µs per row: the FP8 GEMMs at half deepGEMM's rate, 84.4); decode steps at par |
| gpt-oss-20b serving 16 / 64 streams | 1.00 / 0.97 | 64: decode steps (expert GEMMs against Marlin), prompt rows 56.7 against 54.5 µs per row (§82) |

Ranked levers:

1. **Block-scaled FP8 MMA for prompt rows** (`mma.sync ... kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale` with UE8M0 scale vectors, sm_120): ~2x on the
   FP8 GEMMs of Qwen3-8B-FP8's prompt steps (~112 of 138 ms per 2,048 rows), i.e. serving at 64 streams well past vLLM. Needs E8M0
   activation scales (free: quantize_fp8 chooses them) and weight scales rounded to powers of two at load, with the remainder folded
   into the codes where it fits (a numerics change to measure with logits, greedy and a perplexity check; vLLM does the same), behind
   a feature and a fallback to the current kernels.
2. **Qwen3 prompt-step small launches**: rope + cache 119 µs per layer against 27 (vLLM's), norms + quantization 351 against 52 (the
   norm writing E4M3 rows for both readers, the down input's quantization in the gate / up store with 128-output dual tiles).
3. **gpt-oss prompt rows** (§82.6 item 3, not reached this round): the slot sum (110 µs) and norms (72 + 51 µs) per layer, the
   post-attention norm writing the router / MoE f16 copy, the attention output in f16 for the o projection.
4. **Decode**: `gemm_fp8_decode.cu` for 17-32 rows (four token fragments) and as the multi-output q / k / v form; asynchronous scheduling
   for the 0.15 ms host gap per step.

## 85. MoE with CPU offload, round 6: routed experts on disk (models larger than RAM + VRAM), DeepSeek-V3.1 Q4_K_M (405 GB) on a 62 GB / 32 GB pod (2026-11-22)

Branch `perf/offload-r6` (`develop` at `8246ce2e`, §82; `bc59e105` (§83) and `e9c118ee` (§84) merged before the final runs). Same machine as §71: GPU 0 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell
32 GB), AMD EPYC 7443 with a ~10-CPU cgroup quota shared by every job on the pod (AVX2), a 62 GB memory cgroup for the whole pod,
llama.cpp b11177. Two other agents shared the GPU (runs held the verify lock) and the CPU. Model files on the pod's local disk (overlay on a
Samsung 9100 PRO 4 TB NVMe), never on `/workspace` (a FUSE network file system). Raw output and the disk probe in
[`bench/results/s85/`](../bench/results/s85).

### 85.1 What the disk does

A small probe (`uring_probe.c`, raw io_uring syscalls or pread threads, `O_DIRECT`, a 48 GB GGUF as the file) on `/`:

| mode | block | depth / threads | pattern | GB/s |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| io_uring | any | any | any | refused: `io_uring_setup` returns EPERM (the container's seccomp profile) |
| pread, O_DIRECT | 1 MiB | 1 | random | 4.02 |
| pread, O_DIRECT | 1 MiB | 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 | random | 7.36-7.41 |
| pread, O_DIRECT | 64 KiB | 16 | random | 6.82 |
| pread, O_DIRECT | 256 KiB, 4 MiB, 16 MiB | 16 | random | 7.31-7.40 |
| pread, O_DIRECT | 4 MiB, 16 MiB | 16, 8 | sequential | 7.38-7.40 |
| mmap page faults (MADV_RANDOM, pages dropped first) | 1 MiB of 4 KiB faults | 1 | random | 0.73 |
| mmap page faults | | 1 | sequential | 0.27 |
| `/workspace` (FUSE), pread | 4 MiB | 16 | random | 1.82 |

The device saturates at 7.4 GB/s from two reads in flight (the 9100 PRO is a PCIe 5.0 drive; 7.4 GB/s is the PCIe 4.0 x4 link it sits on
here), for any block from 256 KiB up. Page faults on the mapping, which llama.cpp's mmap paging relies on, get 0.3-0.7 GB/s with one
thread: 10-25x less. io_uring cannot be measured on this pod; the reader detects that at run time and uses its thread fallback (8 threads,
8 MiB pieces: 5.4-7 GB/s in the store's own probe).

### 85.2 Qwen3.5-122B-A10B UD-IQ2_XXS (36.6 GB): disk against resident, same placement

A functional test on a model that would fit: the GPU capped at 16 GiB (`--gpu-mem 16`) so that 32 layers' experts (20.7 GiB) go to the CPU,
and a 6 GiB cache (`--expert-cache 6G`) so that they do not fit it. "Resident" is the same placement with the experts read from the
memory-mapped file (page cache warm; `SHARPLIGHT_STREAM_EXPERTS_MIN_ROWS=0`: no streamed prefill or split decode; a disk placement has no
streamed prefill either, and on the final build CUDA splits its small passes, copying from the pinned cache slots), CUDA, `--bench 64` and
`-p "The capital of France is" -n 32` in one hold per build:

| run | decode best / median (tok/s) | prefill 64 tok (tok/s) | hit rate (decode) | read in 64 decode steps |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| resident, CPU experts (first build, before the split) | 29.2 / 24.3 | 60.8 | | |
| disk, 6 GiB cache, CPU experts only (first build) | 25.0 / 21.1 (0.86x) | 34.5 | 69.5 % (41507 hits, 6059 read ahead, 12116 misses) | 16.0 GB (250 MB per step) |
| resident, CPU experts (final build, `develop` merged) | 29.2 / 24.9 | 61.3 | | |
| disk, 6 GiB cache, CUDA split from the pinned slots (final build) | 25.5 / 18.2 | 34.5 | 69.5 % | 16.0 GB |
| text run (32 tokens), resident / disk, first build | 12.5 / 15.5 | | 75.2 % | 5.8 GB |
| text run (32 tokens), resident / disk (split), final build | 14.5 / 18.7 | | 75.2 % | 5.8 GB |

Greedy text identical in all four text runs (" Paris.\nThe capital of France is Paris. ..."), CPU-only and split. The text runs
are faster on disk than resident because the first steps of the resident run fault the mapped experts in (32 tokens; 0 evictions on disk).
The prefill (64 rows) selects nearly every expert of every layer and reads them all (26.8 GB for warm-up and two prefills), chunked behind
the compute: 34.5 against 61 tok/s. The store's load-time probe reports 0.7-0.8 GB/s here: 16 single reads of this model's small experts
(0.2-1 MB at IQ2_XXS) are latency-bound; the decode steps read at the speed they need.

### 85.3 DeepSeek-V3.1 Q4_K_M (405 GB) on 62 GB of host memory and a 32 GB GPU

unsloth/DeepSeek-V3.1-GGUF `Q4_K_M` (9 shards, 405.4 GB; `deepseek2`, 61 layers of which 58 MoE with 256 routed experts, 8 per token, plus
one shared expert). It is 4x the pod's memory and VRAM together. `--provider cuda --cpu-offload --experts-on-disk --expert-cache 28G
--ctx 4096 --batch 64`: the placement keeps the dense part (attention, shared experts, the 3 dense layers, embeddings and head) and two
layers' experts on the GPU (24.5 GiB), and leaves 56 layers' experts (353 GiB, 168 weights) on disk. The first load compiled 'decode' in 67 s (CUDA kernels not yet cached,
the 25 GB upload included).

| run | decode tok/s | hit rate | read | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| CUDA, `-p "The capital of France is" -n 24` | 1.03 (24 tokens) | 40.9 % (prefill included) | 193.9 GB | " Paris. The capital of Spain is Madrid. The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of Germany is Berlin. The" |
| CUDA, `--bench 8` (64 decode steps), first build | best 1.17, median 0.93, mean 0.91 | 37.6 % (decode) | 513.7 GB in the decode steps (7.3 GB per step) | prefill 8 tokens: 8.7 s (0.9 tok/s); GPU 18.6 ms per step |
| same, final build (`develop` merged), twice | best 1.15 / 1.20, median 0.80 / 0.92 | 37.6 % | 513.7 GB | the same counters every run (synthetic tokens, deterministic routing) |
| CUDA text run, final build | 0.97 (24 tokens) | 40.9 % | 193.9 GB | same text |
| `--bench 8`, CUDA split from the pinned cache slots (slots page-locked outside the mapped-file budget), `develop` at `bc59e105` / `e9c118ee` | best 1.11 / 1.12, median 0.87 / 0.87 | 37.6 / 36.6 % | 513.2 / 521.0 GB | the split changes nothing measurable: the step waits for the disk either way |
| CPU only (`--cpu --cpu-offload --gpu-mem 14 --expert-cache 16G`, dense part on the CPU too) | 0.62 (8 tokens) | | 121.8 GB | " Paris. The capital of Spain is Madrid" |

The decode steps read at 7.3 GB/s on average, the disk's limit: decode is bound by the reads of the experts the cache misses, as designed.
The store's own estimate at load (4.4 GB/s probe, 11.9 GB per step without hits: "about 0.37 tok/s from a cold cache") was
pessimistic; the cache's 38-41 % hits and the reads at the full 7.3 GB/s give 0.9-1.2 tok/s.

### 85.5 Changes

* **`ExpertStore`** (Core, `Sharplight.Runtime.Experts`), one per loaded model (`LlmModel.DiskExperts`, `TaskModel.DiskExperts`): the decision
  (CPU experts larger than the fallback's budget minus a 4 GiB reserve, or than the cache asked for), the weights left on disk
  (`IWeightSource.TryGetFileRange`: GGUF, `.slm`, safetensors), one slot pool per slot size (budget split by bytes, at least 32 small-pass
  experts per pool), segmented LRU (experts used twice protected up to 80 % of a pool; `SHARPLIGHT_EXPERT_CACHE=lru`), the pool memory
  committed at layout, statistics (hits, read ahead, misses, evictions, bytes, wait), a read-speed probe and the speed estimate in the load log.
* **`IExpertReader`**: batches of (file, offset, length, destination) reads, awaited per batch; `IoUringExpertReader` (raw syscalls,
  `IORING_OP_READ`, 32 in flight, a reaper thread, short reads resubmitted), `ThreadPoolExpertReader` (8 threads of `pread`), `O_DIRECT`
  files with a buffered fallback, 8 MiB pieces; destinations may name device buffers (DirectStorage / GPUDirect Storage later).
* **Placement**: `PlacementPlan.DiskExpertGroups`; a disk placement is placed again without the streaming memory (no streamed prefill),
  keeping the sparse banks only where the GPU copies from the cache (`IComputeDevice.CopiesFromExpertCache`: CUDA);
  `PlacementPlan.StreamsPrefill`.
* **CPU**: the expert products of disk weights hold the pass's experts in the cache (the layer's down product queued behind the gate / up
  reads), in chunks of a quarter pool for large passes with the next chunk read ahead; the int-dot units of a chunk keep the unchunked
  layout (the row pairing of the two-row dot depends on it), so the outputs are bit-identical; the weights count as no resident memory.
* **CUDA**: split decode passes take their experts from the page-locked cache slots (one asynchronous copy per expert, in the batched copy).
* **Options**: `TaskLoadOptions.ExpertsOnDisk` / `ExpertCacheBytes`; CLI `--experts-on-disk`, `--expert-cache`; hosting
  `HostedModelOptions.ExpertsOnDisk` / `ExpertCacheGiB`, `HostedModelDefaults.ExpertsOnDisk`; `FitQuery.ExpertsOnDisk` →
  `FitReport.ExpertsFromDisk` (`NeedsOffload` instead of `DoesNotFit`); Studio's load toggle and fit text.

### 85.4 Against llama.cpp under the same limits

The pod gives no way to cap one process's memory (the cgroup's controllers are not delegated to the container: a child cgroup gets no
`memory.max`, and there is no systemd), so the like-for-like limit is the pod itself: 62 GB of host memory for everything, 32 GB of VRAM,
for a 405 GB model. llama.cpp b11177 maps the file and pages the experts in on demand (`llama-completion -ngl 99 -ncmoe 59 -fa on -t 10
-c 4096 --temp 0 --no-warmup`: the last two expert layers on the GPU, as in our placement), same prompt, same hold:

| | llama.cpp (mmap paging) | Sharplight (experts on disk, 28 GiB cache) |
|---|---:|---:|
| decode (tok/s) | 0.62 (15 steps) | 0.97 (24-token text run), 0.80-0.93 median / 1.15-1.20 best (`--bench`, 64 steps) |
| prompt, 6 tokens | 16.4 s (0.37 tok/s) | 8.1 s (0.74 tok/s) |
| load | 2 min 54 s (mapping and uploading the dense part) | 67 s to compile 'decode' on the first load (uploads and kernel compilation) |
| page cache used | grew from 25.7 to 57.3 GB of the pod's file cache (evicting other users' cached models) | none for the experts (`O_DIRECT`) |

That is 1.6x llama.cpp's decode by the text runs (1.3-1.9x by median and best step) and 2.0x its prompt speed. llama.cpp pages better
than the single-thread fault probe of §85.1 suggests (10 threads fault in parallel and the kernel reads ahead), but it reads whole
readahead windows through the page cache and competes with every other process for it. Greedy text: both give " Paris. The capital of"
and then differ ("France is Paris." against "Spain is Madrid."); our disk path equals our resident path (§85.2 and the tests), and this
model's real-size output has no reference beyond llama.cpp on this pod (DeepSeek-V2-Lite and GLM-4.7-Flash are the verified `deepseek2`
models), so the divergence at the fourth token is not resolved here.

### 85.7 Not done, next

* io_uring is implemented (raw syscalls) but could not run on this pod; its test skips here. Registered (fixed) buffers were not added.
* Vulkan and Metal: disk layers run on the CPU alone (no imports of the slots yet). No prefill on the GPU from the cache (the CPU prefills
  disk layers: 34 against 61 tok/s on the 122B, 0.9 tok/s for 8 DeepSeek tokens). CPU-only machines work through `--cpu --cpu-offload
  --gpu-mem N` (the cap on the CPU's own share), which is a workaround, not an option of its own.
* Overlapping the reads with the GPU part of a step needs the next layer's experts before its router runs (prediction from the current
  hidden state); spare VRAM as a second cache tier; DirectStorage / GPUDirect Storage readers.
* The DeepSeek-V3.1 greedy text diverges from llama.cpp's at the fourth token; not investigated.

### 85.8 Reproduce

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<i> SHARPLIGHT_VK_DEVICES=<i>
CLI=samples/Sharplight.Cli/bin/Release/net11.0/sharplight
DS=~/models/DeepSeek-V3.1-Q4_K_M/DeepSeek-V3.1-Q4_K_M-00001-of-00009.gguf
$CLI $DS --provider cuda --cpu-offload --experts-on-disk --expert-cache 28G --ctx 4096 --batch 64 -p "The capital of France is" -n 24
SHARPLIGHT_BENCH_PREFILL_REPEATS=1 $CLI $DS --provider cuda --cpu-offload --experts-on-disk --expert-cache 28G --ctx 4096 --batch 64 --bench 8
$LLAMA_ROOT/runtime.llama-b11177-cuda13/llama-completion -m $DS -ngl 99 -ncmoe 59 -fa on -t 10 -c 4096 --temp 0 --no-warmup -no-cnv -p "The capital of France is" -n 16
M=~/models/gguf/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-UD-IQ2_XXS.gguf
SHARPLIGHT_STREAM_EXPERTS_MIN_ROWS=0 $CLI $M --provider cuda --cpu-offload --gpu-mem 16 --bench 64          # resident, CPU experts
$CLI $M --provider cuda --cpu-offload --gpu-mem 16 --experts-on-disk --expert-cache 6G --bench 64            # disk
gcc -O2 -o uring_probe uring_probe.c -lpthread && ./uring_probe <file> pread 1024 8 8192 1                  # disk probe (pread | uring | mmap)
```

## 86. LLM round 30: the block-scaled FP8 MMA measured (same issue rate as plain E4M3 on this GPU), an opt-in block-scaled FP8 mode with power-of-two scales and its numerics, vLLM's prompt-row GEMMs re-measured (§84.4 overstated them) (2026-11-22)

Branch `perf/llm-r30` (`develop` at `e9c118ee`; `10b5ac10` (§85, perf/offload-r6) and `6be4b7d8` (studio/sizing-r2) merged before the
final holds). GPU 0 of the RunPod machine (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell 32 GB, 82 SMs, 200 W cap), shared with other agents: every run held
the verify lock; `develop` (`6be4b7d8`), this branch and vLLM 0.33 (venv `vllm-r12`) ran in the same holds. §85 and §87 are other
rounds'. Every change is CUDA only (one NVRTC kernel and its lowering, a weight repack, a macro of `e4m3.slang` set only in the new
mode); Vulkan's kernels and lowering are unchanged. Raw output in [`bench/results/s86/`](../bench/results/s86).

### 86.1 The premise: block-scaled MMA does not issue faster here, and vLLM's FP8 GEMMs are 1.2x, not 2x, ours

§84.4 put vLLM's DeepGEMM gate / up product at 545 TFLOPS, above the 474 TFLOPS `mma.sync` E4M3 peak, and concluded that it used a
faster block-scaled MMA. Both halves were wrong:

* **MMA rates** (`bench/s86_bs/mma_rate.cu`, 8 independent accumulators per warp, 32 warps per SM, registers only, `sm_120a`):
  `mma.sync.m16n8k32.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` 473.2 TFLOPS, `kind::f8f6f4` 471.6, `kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale.scale_vec::1X ... ue8m0`
  470.3. The block-scaled form issues at the plain rate; it only removes the promotion's instructions (a fresh accumulator and a
  multiply-add per MMA in `gemm_fp8_tma.cu`) and their energy, which matters because prompt-sized GEMMs run at the 200 W cap.
* **vLLM's GEMM times.** The 662 µs of §84.4 was the average of vLLM's own per-kernel table over 72 calls: the scheduler split the 8
  prompts into a step of 7 (1,792 rows) and a step of 1 (256 rows), and the table mixed both. `bench/s54_vllm_decode_profile.py` now
  reports every prefill range on its own (it raised a division by zero on such a split before). Per call (µs):

| GEMM (per layer) | vLLM 8 x 256: the 1,792-row step | vLLM one 2,048-token prompt | ours, 2,048 rows (`develop`) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gate / up (vLLM: GEMM, then mul + quant 125 / 155 µs) | 1,157.4 | 1,383.4 | 1,612 (dual, SiLU · mul in the store) |
| down | 599.9 | 720.6 | 824 |
| q / k / v (vLLM one GEMM) | 305.0 | 346.1 | 263 + 2 x 76 |
| o | 196.6 | 230.8 | 263 |

  At 2,048 rows DeepGEMM runs gate / up at 298 TFLOPS against our 256 (1.17x), not 545. Standalone (`bench/s86_bs/vllm_dg_gemm.py`,
  random bf16 data quantized per vLLM, sustained 1.5 s): DeepGEMM gate / up 1.581 ms (261 TFLOPS), CUTLASS's blockwise sm120 kernel
  (f32 scales) 1.459 ms (283 TFLOPS), ours 1.701 ms (242 TFLOPS, `bench/s86_bs/bench_fp8.cu`); the model's real activations draw less
  power than random codes, so all three run faster in the model.

### 86.2 The block-scaled FP8 mode (opt-in)

`gemm_fp8_tma.cu` with `F8N_BLOCK_SCALED` (`block_scaled_fp8`, compute capability 12.x with a CUDA 12.9+ driver; NVRTC compiles it for
`compute_120f`, selected by the `SL_FAMILY_ARCH` macro): the consumer warps pass the exponent fields of the stage's f32 scales as UE8M0
scale vectors (`scale_vec::1X`: per 16-row fragment of A, lanes 4g / 4g + 2 give row g and 4g + 1 / 4g + 3 row g + 8; every lane of
quad g gives column g of B) and accumulate all of K in one accumulator per output. It needs power-of-two scales everywhere, so the mode
(`SHARPLIGHT_FP8_BLOCK_SCALED=1`, default off) also

* requantizes grouped E4M3 weights at load (`WeightRepack.Fp8B128GroupedUe8m0`, `Fp8PowerOfTwoScales`): each row's 128-value block
  gets d' = 2^ceil(log2(amax / 448)) and its codes become E4M3(e4m3(c) · d / d'), rounded to nearest even. vLLM does the same per
  128 x 128 block; per row the rows that do not reach the block's maximum keep more precision. Every kernel reading the weights (decode
  too) sees the requantized values, so decode and prompt steps agree;
* gives every E4M3 activation row power-of-two scales (`E4M3_UE8M0` in `e4m3_group_scale`, set on all kernels of the compilation:
  `quantize_fp8` and the norms that write E4M3 rows);
* stores the down projection's E4M3 rows from the dual gate / up GEMM from 256 rows (`QOUT`, `SHARPLIGHT_FP8_QSTORE_MIN_ROWS`): a
  128-value scale group spans two 64-output tiles, so a block walks the two tiles of a group back to back, keeps the first tile's
  outputs in registers, combines each row's maximum in shared memory (two barriers of the computing warps per pair; the mbarrier ring
  guarantees no warp reaches the next pair's maxima before all have read them, since K has at least 4 blocks and the ring 3 stages)
  and writes the codes and scales `quantize_fp8` would write, bit for bit (`Fp8BlockScaledTests.E4m3StoreMatchesSeparateQuantization`).

Kernel harness (sustained, power-of-two scales, gate / up 2,048 x 4,096 → 2 x 12,288): promoting form 1.701 ms 242 TFLOPS 0.82
pJ/flop, block-scaled 1.580 ms 261 TFLOPS 0.75 pJ/flop, block-scaled with the E4M3 store 1.643-1.667 ms (it saves the 129 µs
quantization launch and three quarters of the f32 traffic in the model); down [12,288 → 4,096] 0.883 → 0.806 ms.

### 86.3 Numerics of the block-scaled mode (and the default decision)

Perplexity on a fixed text: the first 12,288 tokens of the wikitext-2-raw-v1 test split (`Salesforce/wikitext`, the concatenated
`text` column of `test-00000-of-00001.parquet`), cut into 4 sequences of 3,072 tokens, each a fresh context, every token after the
first scored. Ours: `bench/PplBench` (new: prompt steps of 1,024 rows with logits for every row, `SequenceInput.LogitsRows`, so every
row runs through the prompt-sized GEMMs); vLLM: `bench/s86_bs/vllm_ppl.py` (`prompt_logprobs` on the same token ids). KL and top-1
over all 3,072 positions of the first sequence (f16 logits dumps, `PplBench --compare`), the block-scaled mode against ours with f32
scales:

| model | ours, f32 scales | ours, block-scaled | change | KL mean (max) | top-1 agreement | vLLM CUTLASS (f32 scales) | vLLM DeepGEMM (E8M0, its default) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 | 8.6693 | 8.7358 | **+0.77 %** | 0.0154 (20.4) | 96.0 % | 8.6863 | 8.7686 (+0.95 % over its CUTLASS) |
| Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 | 5.6904 | 5.7052 | +0.26 % | 0.0068 (0.89) | 96.2 % | | |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8, weights requantized only (`SHARPLIGHT_FP8_UE8M0_WEIGHTS=1`, diagnostic) | | 8.7183 | +0.56 % | | | | |

The weights' second rounding is most of the change (+0.56 of +0.77 %); the activations' power-of-two scales add the rest. Greedy text
(120 tokens, the ~40-word and the 963-token prompt, CUDA) is byte-identical to the f32-scale path; the last-token logits of a ~2,900-token
prompt differ by KL 3.4e-4 (max |Δ| 2.15, same top-1).

**Decision: off by default.** The rule was ±0.3 % perplexity and comparable to vLLM's: Qwen3-8B-FP8 changes by +0.77 % (vLLM's own E8M0
path +0.95 %, so comparable, but outside ±0.3 %); Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 +0.26 %. `SHARPLIGHT_FP8_BLOCK_SCALED=1` turns it on; the owner can
decide per model class. The default path is bit-identical to `develop` (greedy text of gpt-oss-20b, Qwen3-8B-FP8 on CUDA and Vulkan and
Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M on CUDA byte-identical; last-token logits of Qwen3-8B-FP8 and gpt-oss-20b bit-identical; `PplBench` argmax hash and
perplexity identical).

### 86.4 Steps (final hold)

BatchBench (`--slots 64 --ctx 640 --depth 256`, GPU ms min; `develop` `6be4b7d8`, this branch, this branch with
`SHARPLIGHT_FP8_BLOCK_SCALED=1`, alternated twice in one hold, `steps/`):

| step | `develop` | this branch (default) | block-scaled mode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 prompt, 2,048 rows (8 x 256) | 136.25 / 139.14 | 138.55 / 138.60 | **125.84 / 125.61** (-9 %) |
| the same: gate / up, down, q and o, k and v per layer (µs) | 1,611 / 823 / 262 / 79 (branch, default) | | 1,513 (E4M3 store, no quantization launch) / 771 / 242 / 72 |
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 decode 1 / 16 / 64 rows | 10.96, 10.95 / 12.20, 12.19 / 15.53, 15.59 | 10.94, 10.94 / 12.19, 12.19 / 15.61, 15.59 | 10.95 / 12.17, 12.18 / 15.51, 15.50 |
| gpt-oss-20b prompt, 2,048 rows | 115.46 / 115.77 | 115.65 / 115.86 | 115.62 / 115.25 (no FP8 weights) |
| gpt-oss-20b decode 1 / 16 / 64 rows | 5.19 / 12.16 / 16.91, 17.03 | 5.18 / 12.17, 12.18 / 17.20, 17.18 | 5.19, 5.18 / 12.17, 12.20 / 17.18, 16.90 |

The default path is unchanged (its kernels compile to the same SASS as `develop`'s; the spread between holds of the same build was
128-139 ms for the Qwen3 prompt step on this shared GPU, which is why only same-hold rows are compared). The block-scaled mode does not
touch decode (decode rows run the skinny / decode GEMMs, which read the requantized weights at the same cost). At 2,048 prompt rows the
block-scaled step is 61.4 µs per row against vLLM's 54.8 (1,792-row step) to 62.2 (one 2,048-token prompt, longer attention).
